Theorem 29.1.4, page 1025 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\) and let \(g\) be a measurable function on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_0^1|g(x)|x^{-1}dx+\int_1^\infty|g(x)|e^{-x}dx<\infty\). If \(\int_0^\infty g(x)\operatorname{sech}(nx)\,dx=0\) for all \(n\in\mathbb N\), then \(g=0\) almost everywhere. The same holds with \(\mathbb N\) replaced by a set \(\Lambda\subset(0,\infty)\) containing an interval, provided the integrals \(\int g\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\,dx\), \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), converge absolutely and vanish. The proof uses \(e^{-kx}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nkx)\) for \(k\in\mathbb N\), with \(\mu\) the M"obius function and \(\chi_4\) the nonprincipal character modulo \(4\), together with Lerch’s theorem that \(\int_0^\infty e^{-kx}h(x)\,dx=0\) for all \(k\in\mathbb N\) forces \(h=0\) when \(\int|h|e^{-x}<\infty\).
Source: ch/lv1.tex, label lv:thm:L1.




Theorem 29.2.2, page 1027 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\), let \(\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots\) be the Dirichlet beta function, with \(\chi_4\) the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo \(4\), let \(\mu\) be the M"obius function, \(M_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\) and \(S_N(x)=\frac12\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)\). For \(c\ge1\), \(S_N\to e^{-x}\) in \(\mathcal W_c\), that is \(\|S_N-e^{-x}\|_c\to0\). For \(c>1\) this follows from \(|\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)n^{-s}|\le\zeta(c)\) and dominated convergence in the Mellin Plancherel formula; for \(c=1\) it follows from the prime number theorem \(M_\chi(x)\ll x\exp(-a\sqrt{\log x})\) for some \(a>0\) and partial summation.

Theorem 29.3.2, page 1028 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\). Let \(c>0\) and let \(\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)\) satisfy \(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty\). Then \(\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) is complete in \(\mathcal W_c\), that is, a function of \(\mathcal W_c\) orthogonal to every \(\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\) is zero. In particular the integer dilates \(\operatorname{sech}(nx)\) and the prime dilates \(\operatorname{sech}(px)\), \(p\) prime, are complete in every \(\mathcal W_c\), including \(c=\frac12\). The proof writes the Mellin transform of the orthogonal function against \(\Gamma(c+it)\beta(c+it)\) and applies Carleman’s formula to an analytic function on the right half plane that vanishes on \(\Lambda\).

Theorem 29.5.2, page 1030 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\), let \(\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots\) be the Dirichlet beta function, with \(\chi_4\) the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo \(4\), and let \(\mu\) be the M"obius function, \(M_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\) and \(S_N(x)=\frac12\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)\). For \(\frac12\le\theta<1\) the following are equivalent: (i) \(L(s,\chi_4)\ne0\) for \(\Re s>\theta\); (ii) \(\{\operatorname{sech}(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}\) is complete in \(\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b\) (normed by \(\|f\|_a+\|f\|_b\)) for all \(\theta<a<b<1\); (iii) \(S_N\to e^{-x}\) in \(\mathcal W_c\) for every \(c\in(\theta,1)\). Theorem 29.6.1, page 1031 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\), let \(\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x\) (so \(\varphi\in\mathcal W_c\) exactly for \(0<c<1\) and \(\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}\varphi(x)\,dx=\Gamma(s)\zeta(s)\) for \(0<\Re s<1\)), let \(\mu\) be the M"obius function, \(M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\) and \(T_N(x)=\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\varphi(nx)\). (1) For every \(c\in(0,1)\) the dilates \(\{\varphi(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}\) are complete in \(\mathcal W_c\), unconditionally. (2) Let \(\frac12\le\theta<1\) and suppose \(M(x)=O_\varepsilon(x^{\theta+\varepsilon})\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). Then \(T_N\to e^{-x}\) in \(\mathcal W_c\) with \(\|T_N-e^{-x}\|_c=O_\varepsilon(N^{\theta-c+\varepsilon})\) for \(\theta<c<1\) and \(0<\varepsilon<c-\theta\). (3) For \(\frac12\le\theta<1\), completeness of \(\{\varphi(nx)\}\) in \(\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b\) for all \(\theta<a<b<1\) is equivalent to \(\zeta(s)\ne0\) for \(\Re s>\theta\) (the pole at \(1\) being allowed); with \(\theta=\frac12\) it is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis.

Theorem 29.10.2, page 1035 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\) and let \(\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots\) be the Dirichlet beta function, with \(\chi_4\) the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo \(4\). Let \(c>0\) and assume \((\mathrm N_c)\): \(1/\beta(c+it)\ll(1+|t|)^{A}\) for some \(A\ge0\) and all real \(t\). If \(\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)\) and \(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda<\infty\), then \(\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) is not complete in \(\mathcal W_c\). So under \((\mathrm N_c)\) the dilates are complete in \(\mathcal W_c\) if and only if \(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty\). The hypothesis \((\mathrm N_c)\) holds unconditionally for \(c\ge1\) and fails at \(c=\frac12\), where \(\beta\) has zeros on the line.

Corollary 29.10.3, page 1036 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.

Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\) and let \(\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots\) be the Dirichlet beta function, with \(\chi_4\) the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo \(4\). For \(\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)\), \(\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) is complete in \(\mathcal W_c\) if and only if \(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty\), in each of these cases: for \(c\ge1\) (unconditionally); for \(c>\frac78\) given that \(L(s,\chi_4)\ne0\) for \(\Re s>\frac78\); and for every \(c>0\) with \(c\ne\frac12\) under the generalised Riemann hypothesis for \(\beta\).

Theorem 29.11.1, page 1037 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\sigma>0\), let \(k\) be \(1/(e^x+1)\) or \(\operatorname{sech}x\), and let \(\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)\) satisfy \(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty\). Then \(\{x^{\sigma-1}k(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) is complete in \(L^1(0,\infty)\) if and only if the Mellin transform of \(k\) has no zero on the line \(\Re s=\sigma\). In particular, for \(\frac12<\sigma<1\) the integer dilates of the Fermi kernel \(1/(e^x+1)\) are complete in \(L^1\) if and only if the Riemann zeta function has no zero on \(\Re s=\sigma\), and the integer dilates of \(\operatorname{sech}\) if and only if the Dirichlet beta function \(\beta=L(\cdot,\chi_4)\) has none.

Proposition 29.12.1, page 1040 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\), let \(\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots\) be the Dirichlet beta function, with \(\chi_4\) the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo \(4\), \(c>0\), \(T\ge1\) and \(a_n\) arbitrary complex coefficients, with \(D_N(s)=\sum_{n\le N}a_nn^{-s}\), \(\|a\|_{N,c}=\sum_{n\le N}|a_n|n^{-c}\) and \(K_c(t)=\Gamma(c+it)\beta(c+it)\). Then \(\|e^{-x}-\sum_{n\le N}a_n\operatorname{sech}(nx)\|_c^2=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta(c+it)D_N(c+it)|^2dt\), and this is at most \(\frac1{2\pi}\int_{|t|\le T}|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta D_N|^2dt+C_ce^{-\pi T}T^{2c}(1+\|a\|_{N,c})^2\) for a constant \(C_c\) depending only on \(c\). Where \(\beta\ne0\) the integrand of the first term is \(|K_c(t)|^2|2D_N-1/\beta|^2\). The Mellin transform of \(\operatorname{sech}(nx)\) carries the factor \(2\), which is why \(2D_N-1/\beta\) appears and not \(D_N-1/\beta\).

Theorem 29.13.1, page 1041 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(t>0\) let \(f_t(x)=|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2\), \(x>0\). For \(0<\Re s<1\), \(M_t(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}f_t(x)\,dx=2^s\pi\,\Gamma(t)Z_t(1-s)/\sin(\pi s/2)\), where \(Z_t\) is the entire function \(Z_t(w)=\Gamma(w)^{-1}\int_0^\infty u^{w-1}(2\cosh(u/2))^{-t}\,du=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^k\binom{t+k-1}{k}(k+\frac t2)^{-w}\) for \(\Re w>t-1\). With \(\beta\) the Dirichlet beta function, \(\eta(w)=(1-2^{1-w})\zeta(w)\) the Dirichlet eta function and \(\zeta\) the Riemann zeta function, \(Z_1(w)=2^w\beta(w)\), \(Z_2(w)=\eta(w-1)=(1-2^{2-w})\zeta(w-1)\) and \(Z_3(w)=2^{w-3}(\beta(w)-\beta(w-2))\). For integer \(t\), \(Z_t\) is a linear combination of \(\eta(w-j)\), \(j\) odd, when \(t\) is even, and of \(2^{w-2i}\beta(w-2i)\) when \(t\) is odd.

Corollary 29.13.2, page 1042 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\) and \(f_t(x)=|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2\) for \(t>0\). For every \(t>0\) and every \(c>0\), \(\{f_t(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) with \(\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)\) is complete in \(\mathcal W_c\) whenever \(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty\); in particular the integer dilates are complete. The proof checks that \(f_t\in\mathcal W_c\) and that its Mellin transform on \(\Re s=c\) is nonzero almost everywhere with the bound \(C(1+|\tau|)^Ae^{-\pi|\tau|/2}\), the only properties used in the proof of single weight completeness.

Theorem 29.13.3, page 1043 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(c>0\) let \(\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)\) and \(\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh\) and let \(\mu\) be the M"obius function, \(c_n=\mu(n)\) for odd \(n\) and \(c_n=0\) for even \(n\), and \(\operatorname{csch}=1/\sinh\). Then for every \(x>0\), with absolute convergence, \(e^{-x}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}c_n\operatorname{csch}(nx)\) and \(xe^{-x}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}(c_n/n)(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)\), and \(\sum_n(c_n/n)n^{-s}=1/((1-2^{-s-1})\zeta(s+1))\) converges absolutely for \(\Re s>0\). Consequently the series for \(xe^{-x}\) converges absolutely in every \(\mathcal W_c\), \(c>0\), and \(\{(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}\) is complete in every \(\mathcal W_c\) and in every \(\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b\), \(0<a<b\), unconditionally.

Theorem 29.14.2, page 1045 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Xi\) be either the Riemann function \(\xi\) or \(\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)\) with \(\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)\); both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy \(\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)\) and have the Hadamard product \(\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)\) over the nontrivial zeros \(\rho\), paired with \(\bar\rho\). For \(\theta\ge\frac12\) let \(F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)\) for \(s\) in the plane cut along \((-\infty,0]\), with the principal square root. A probability law on \([0,\infty)\) is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is \(\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))\) with \(a\ge0\) and a locally finite positive Thorin measure \(U\) on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty\) and \(\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty\). For \(a\ge0\) and \(\gamma>0\) let \(Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}\) and, for \(a>0\), \(Q_{a,\gamma}\) be the probability measure on \((0,\infty)\) that is the image under \(v\mapsto v^2\) of the law of \(|\gamma+aC|\) with \(C\) standard Cauchy, with density \(\frac1{2\pi\sqrt u}[\frac a{a^2+(\sqrt u-\gamma)^2}+\frac a{a^2+(\sqrt u+\gamma)^2}]\). Let \(\theta\ge\frac12\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(\Xi\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>\theta\); (ii) \(F_\theta\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC; (iii) \(F_\theta\) is analytic in the cut plane. When they hold, the Thorin measure of \(F_\theta\) is \(U_\theta=\sum_{\rho,\ \Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\ \Im\rho}\) over the distinct zeros \(\rho\) in the upper half plane with multiplicity \(m_\rho\), and \(F_\theta(s)=\exp(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U_\theta(du))\) with no linear term. For \(\Xi=\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)\), (i) is equivalent to two weight completeness of the secant dilates on \((\theta,1)\) (for \(\theta<1\), the two weight criterion for \(\beta\)); for \(\Xi=\xi\), to two weight completeness of the dilates of \(\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x\) (the zeta version of the two weight criterion).
Source: ch/lv2.tex, label lv:thm:thorin.




Corollary 29.14.3, page 1045 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on The zero free half plane \(\Re s>\frac78\) for the Riemann zeta function and, for the statement about \(\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)\), for \(L(s,\chi_4)\), from the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, unrefereed, announced for Dirichlet \(L\) functions; that the theorem covers the character modulo \(4\) has not been checked); the part for \(\theta\ge1\) is unconditional.
Statement. Let \(\Xi\) be either the Riemann function \(\xi\) or \(\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)\) with \(\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)\); both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy \(\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)\) and have the Hadamard product \(\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)\) over the nontrivial zeros \(\rho\), paired with \(\bar\rho\). For \(\theta\ge\frac12\) let \(F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)\) for \(s\) in the plane cut along \((-\infty,0]\), with the principal square root. A probability law on \([0,\infty)\) is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is \(\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))\) with \(a\ge0\) and a locally finite positive Thorin measure \(U\) on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty\) and \(\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty\). Let \(U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}\), over the distinct zeros \(\rho\) with \(\Im\rho>0\) and with \(m_\rho\) the multiplicity of \(\rho\), be the Thorin measure of \(F_\theta\) when \(\Xi\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>\theta\), where for \(a\ge0\) and \(\gamma>0\), \(Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}\) and, for \(a>0\), \(Q_{a,\gamma}\) is the image under \(v\mapsto v^2\) of the law of \(|\gamma+aC|\) with \(C\) standard Cauchy. For every \(\theta\ge1\), \(F_\theta\) for \(\xi\) and for \(\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC with the absolutely continuous Thorin measure \(U_\theta\), since the zeros have \(\Re\rho<1\). Conditionally on the zero free half plane \(\Re s>\frac78\) the GGC representation holds for every \(\theta\ge\frac78\), and the Thorin measure is absolutely continuous for \(\theta>\frac78\), and at \(\theta=\frac78\) if no zero lies on \(\Re s=\frac78\); a zero \(\rho\) on that line contributes an atom \(m_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho^2}\), \(\gamma_\rho=\Im\rho\). For \(\theta=\frac12\) the statement for \(\xi\) is the Riemann Hypothesis and the Thorin measure is then \(\sum_{\gamma>0}m_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}\), over the ordinates \(\gamma>0\) of the zeros \(\frac12+i\gamma\) of \(\xi\) with multiplicity \(m_\gamma\).

Theorem 29.14.4, page 1046 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Xi\) be either the Riemann function \(\xi\) or \(\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)\) with \(\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)\); both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy \(\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)\) and have the Hadamard product \(\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)\) over the nontrivial zeros \(\rho\), paired with \(\bar\rho\). For \(\theta\ge\frac12\) let \(F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)\) for \(s\) in the plane cut along \((-\infty,0]\), with the principal square root. A probability law on \([0,\infty)\) is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is \(\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))\) with \(a\ge0\) and a locally finite positive Thorin measure \(U\) on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty\) and \(\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty\). Let \(\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,a)\) be the Cauchy law of centre \(\gamma\) and scale \(a>0\) and \(\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma\), and let \(U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}\), over the distinct zeros \(\rho\) with \(\Im\rho>0\) and with \(m_\rho\) the multiplicity of \(\rho\), be the Thorin measure of \(F_\theta\) when \(\Xi\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>\theta\), where for \(a\ge0\) and \(\gamma>0\), \(Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}\) and, for \(a>0\), \(Q_{a,\gamma}\) is the image under \(v\mapsto v^2\) of the law of \(|\gamma+aC|\) with \(C\) standard Cauchy. Suppose \(\Xi\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>\theta_0\). For \(\theta\ge\theta_0\) let \(\widetilde U_\theta=\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\,\mathrm{Cauchy}(\Im\rho,\theta-\Re\rho)\) be the symmetric measure on \(\mathbb R\) in the variable \(v\), summed over the distinct zeros \(\rho\) of both half planes with multiplicity \(m_\rho\) (the factor \(\frac12\) is needed: without it the image is \(2U_\theta\)). Then \(U_\theta\) is the image of \(\widetilde U_\theta\) under \(v\mapsto v^2\), and for \(\theta_0\le\theta<\theta'\), \(\widetilde U_{\theta'}=\widetilde U_\theta*\mathrm{Cauchy}(0,\theta'-\theta)\). In particular, if all zeros lie on \(\Re s=\theta_0\) (which for the completed functions forces \(\theta_0=\frac12\)), then \(\widetilde U_\theta\) is the Poisson smoothing at width \(\theta-\theta_0\) of \(\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\delta_{\Im\rho}\) and converges vaguely to it as \(\theta\downarrow\theta_0\). For \(\xi\) this is the Cauchy flow of the book’s Poisson structure result, credited to Nicholas Polson (Chapter 8 of his monograph On Hilbert’s 8th Problem, 2026).

Theorem 30.1.1, page 1051 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), let \(\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho\) run over its zeros with multiplicity, \(\Lambda\) the von Mangoldt function, and for \(\theta>\sigma_\rho\) for every \(\rho\) (in particular for every \(\theta>1\), and also for \(\theta=1\) because \(\zeta(1+it)\ne0\)) let \(\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)\) be the positive measure on \(\mathbb{R}\) with \(\int\mathfrak U_\theta(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty\), where \(\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,c)\) has density \((c/\pi)/(c^2+(v-\gamma)^2)\). Then \(\mathfrak U_\theta\) is absolutely continuous with real analytic density \(u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)=\frac1\pi\partial_\sigma\log|\xi(\sigma+iv)|\) at \(\sigma=\theta\), and \(\mathfrak U_\theta((0,V])=\frac1\pi\arg\xi(\theta+iV)\) for the branch with \(\arg\xi(\theta)=0\). At \(\theta=1\), for every real \(v\), \(u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac1{1+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{1+iv}2)-\lim_{X\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{n\le X}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n\cos(v\log n)-\frac{\sin(v\log X)}{v}\bigr)\bigr]\), where \(\sin(v\log X)/v\) means \(\log X\) at \(v=0\); the limit exists locally uniformly, equals \(\operatorname{Re}C(1+iv)\) with \(C(s)=-\zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)-1/(s-1)\), and \(u_1(0)=(2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi)/(2\pi)\) with \(\gamma_E\) Euler’s constant, while the cosine series itself has no limit. For \(\theta>1\), \(u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac\theta{\theta^2+v^2}+\frac{\theta-1}{(\theta-1)^2+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{\theta+iv}2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-\theta}\cos(v\log n)\bigr]\) with the prime sum absolutely convergent.
Source: ch/lo1.tex, label lo:thm:density.




Proposition 30.2.1, page 1053 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. With \(\mathfrak U_1=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,1-\sigma_\rho)\) the level one Thorin measure of \(\xi\) (zeros \(\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho\)), \(\Lambda\) the von Mangoldt function, \(P_c(v)=(c/\pi)/(c^2+v^2)\), \(\widehat f(\omega)=\int e^{-i\omega v}f(v)\,dv\), and for \(\theta\ge1\) \(g_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi[\theta/(\theta^2+v^2)-\frac12\log\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(\frac{\theta+iv}2)]\): as tempered distributions \(\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)=\widehat{g_1}(\omega)+1-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n(\delta_{\log n}+\delta_{-\log n})(\omega)\), the constant \(1\) being the transform of the atom at \(0\) that the pole of \(\zeta\) contributes in the limit \(\theta\downarrow1\), and on the zero side \(\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)=\sum_\rho e^{-(1-\sigma_\rho)|\omega|}e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}\) as the limit of the sums over \(|\gamma_\rho|<T\). Equivalently, for every Schwartz function \(\varphi\), \(\sum_\rho(P_{1-\sigma_\rho}*\varphi)(\gamma_\rho)=\int g_1\varphi\,dv+\varphi(0)-\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n(\widehat\varphi(\log n)+\widehat\varphi(-\log n))\). For \(\theta\ge1\), \(\mathfrak U_\theta=P_{\theta-1}*\mathfrak U_1\) and \(\widehat{\mathfrak U_\theta}(\omega)=e^{-(\theta-1)|\omega|}\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)\), which replaces \(\Lambda(n)/n\) by \(\Lambda(n)n^{-\theta}\) on the prime side.
Source: ch/lo1.tex, label lo:prop:spectrum.




Theorem 30.3.1, page 1056 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\frac12\le\theta'<1\), \(a=1-\theta'\), \(\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)\) the Thorin measure at level \(\theta\) of \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), over its zeros \(\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho\) with multiplicity (\(\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,c)\) the Cauchy law of centre \(\gamma\) and width \(c\), \(\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma\)), \(\Phi_\Omega(v)=(1-\cos\Omega v)/(\pi\Omega v^2)\) the Fejér kernel, and \(K_{\theta',\Omega}\) the inverse Fourier transform of \((1-|\omega|/\Omega)_+e^{a|\omega|}\). The band limited backward flow is \(B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_1*K_{\theta',\Omega}\). (i) If \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'\), then \(B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_{\theta'}*\Phi_\Omega\), which converges vaguely to \(\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\) as \(\Omega\to\infty\), with \(\int B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)\,dv/(v^2+s)\to\int\mathfrak U_{\theta'}(dv)/(v^2+s)\) for every \(s>0\); if moreover \(\theta'>\sigma_\rho\) for every zero the convergence is locally uniform as densities. (ii) If \(\zeta\) has a zero \(\rho\) with \(\sigma_\rho>\theta'\), there is no signed measure \(\mu\) with \(\int|\mu|(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty\) such that \(\int B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)\,dv/(v^2+s)\to\int\mu(dv)/(v^2+s)\) as \(\Omega\to\infty\) for all large \(s\). Hence the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to convergence of the flow at every \(\theta'>\frac12\).
Source: ch/lo1.tex, label lo:thm:dichotomy.




Result 30.3.1, page 1057 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: computed.
Statement. The computation samples the level one Thorin density \(u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)\), \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), on \([0,400]\) at spacing \(0.05\) from \(\zeta\) and \(\zeta'\) on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=1\) only (the Arb library (python flint) balls at \(128\) bits, with the analytic value of \(u_1(0)\)), applies a Hann window and the backward multiplier \(e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}\) with a cutoff at \(\Omega\), and inverts. Theorem 31.2.1, page 1076 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(A\) be a matrix with positive entries, \(y\) a vector of nonnegative data, and \(\ell(x)=\sum_i\bigl(y_i\log(Ax)_i-(Ax)_i\bigr)\) the Poisson log likelihood on the open orthant \(x>0\). Then \(\ell\) is concave. With independent gamma priors \(x_j\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha_j,\beta_j)\), \(\alpha_j\ge1\), the posterior density \(\pi(x)\propto e^{\ell(x)}\prod_jx_j^{\alpha_j-1}e^{-\beta_jx_j}\) is log concave on the orthant. In the discretised deconvolution of the book, \(A_{ij}=hP_{1-\theta'}(v_i-w_j)\) with \(P_a\) the Cauchy density of scale \(a\). The sampling clause of the chapter (sampling to total variation accuracy \(\varepsilon\) in polynomial time for a log concave density, by a theorem of Applegate, Kannan and Polson) is cited and needs a bound on a ratio of radii that is not proved.

Proposition 31.2.2, page 1077 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Omega\) be the largest frequency to be resolved. Then for the linear inverse the level one data must be supplied to absolute precision \(e^{-(1-\theta')\Omega}\) on the scale of \(u_1\), that is, to \((1-\theta')\Omega/\log 2\) binary digits, and this is sharp: an error of size \(\delta\) at frequency \(\omega\) in the Fourier transform of \(u_1\) produces an error of size \(\delta e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}\) in the inverted measure.

Proposition 31.3.4, page 1080 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\frac12\le\theta'<1\), \(a=1-\theta'\), \(\xi\) the Riemann xi function and \(u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)\). For a grid of spacing \(h\) with data points \(v_i=ih\), \(|i|\le M\), in the window \([-V,V]\) and unknown points \(w_j=jh\), \(|j|\le N\), in the window \([-W,W]\), \(W>V\), let \(A_{ij}=hP_a(v_i-w_j)\) with \(P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)\), \(y_i=u_1(v_i)\), \(R_h(x)=h\sum_{|i|\le M}\bigl(y_i\log\frac{y_i}{(Ax)_i}-y_i+(Ax)_i\bigr)\), \(R_h^*=\min_{x\ge0}R_h(x)\), let \(x_h\) be any minimiser (for instance the limit of EM from a positive start) and \(\mu_h=\sum_jx_{h,j}h\,\delta_{w_j}\). Consider grids with \(h\to0\) and \(V\to\infty\). (a) If \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'\) and \((\log W)^2/(W-V)\to0\), \((W-V)^2\log V/V^2\to0\) and \(h^2V\log^2V\to0\), then \(R_h^*\to0\) and \(\mu_h\) converges vaguely to the Thorin measure \(\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\), whose density is \(\sum_\rho P_{\theta'-\operatorname{Re}\rho}(v-\operatorname{Im}\rho)\) over the zeros \(\rho\) of \(\xi\) with multiplicity, with \(P_0\) read as the unit point mass. (b) If \(\zeta\) has a zero of real part greater than \(\theta'\), then \(\liminf R_h^*>0\), whatever the choice of \(W>V\).

Proposition 31.5.1, page 1087 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\theta'\in[\frac12,1)\), let \(A\) be the square section of order \(2N+1\) of the Toeplitz matrix \(A_{ij}=hP_{1-\theta'}((i-j)h)\) with \(P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)\), and let \(t=h/(\pi(1-\theta'))\). Let \(t_0=0.52219\ldots\) be the root in \((0,1)\) of \(\coth(1/t)=2t\). If \(t<t_0\), in particular if \(h<\pi(1-\theta')/2\), the bi infinite operator \(|I-A|\) has spectral radius \(1-2t+\coth(1/t)>1\), and so do its sections for all \(N\ge N_0(h,\theta')\). For such a section consider the von Neumann and Ulam estimator of \(\sum_{k\ge0}(I-A)^ky\): at state \(j\) it stops with probability \(q_j\in(0,1)\) and otherwise moves to \(k\) with probability \((1-q_j)p_{jk}\), \(p_{jk}>0\) wherever \((I-A)_{jk}\ne0\), and it returns the product of the weights \((I-A)_{jk}/((1-q_j)p_{jk})\) along the path times \(y_j/q_j\) at the stopping state \(j\). Its second moment is infinite from every starting state. If \(t_0<t\le1\) the spectral radius of \(|I-A|\) is below one for the bi infinite operator and all its sections, and the conclusion fails for the choice \(q_j=1-r_j\), \(p_{jk}=|(I-A)_{jk}|/r_j\) with \(r_j\) the row sums of \(|I-A|\).
Source: ch/cx1.tex, label cx:prop:vnvar.




Proposition 31.6.1, page 1089 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(T_a\) be the first passage time to level \(a>0\) of a Brownian motion, with density \(\ell_a(t)=a(2\pi)^{-1/2}t^{-3/2}e^{-a^2/(2t)}\). Then \(\frac{a/\pi}{a^2+(v-\gamma)^2}=\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-(v-\gamma)^2/(2t)}}{\sqrt{2\pi t}}\ell_a(t)\,dt\), so \(\gamma+B(T_a)\) has the Cauchy law of centre \(\gamma\) and scale \(a\) for an independent Brownian motion \(B\), and \(e^{-a|\omega|}=\int_0^\infty e^{-t\omega^2/2}\ell_a(t)\,dt\). Consequently, if \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0\) and \(\theta>\theta_0\), the Thorin measure \(\mathfrak U_\theta\), with density \(\sum_\rho P_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(v-\gamma_\rho)\) over the nontrivial zeros \(\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho\) of \(\zeta\) with multiplicity and \(P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)\), equals \(\sum_\rho\int_0^\infty(e^{t\Delta/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho})\,\ell_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(t)\,dt\), the sum over the nontrivial zeros of the heat flow of \(\delta_{\gamma_\rho}\) run to the random time \(T_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}\). Under the Riemann hypothesis it is the heat flow of \(\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}\) to the single random time \(T_{\theta-1/2}\).
Source: ch/cx1.tex, label cx:prop:subord.




Theorem 31.9.1, page 1094 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the Riemann xi function and, for \(\frac12\le\theta<1\), \(F_\theta(s)=\xi(\theta)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s)\) on the plane cut along \((-\infty,0]\) with the principal square root. A generalised gamma convolution (GGC) has Laplace transform \(\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))\) with \(a\ge0\) and a positive Thorin measure \(U\). For \(\frac12\le\theta<1\) the following are equivalent: (i) \(F_\theta\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC, that is, the measure \(U_\theta\) of the zeros is a positive Thorin measure; (ii) \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\); (iii) \(\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(s)>0\) for \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\), that is, \(u_\sigma(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iv)>0\) for every \(\sigma>\theta\) and every real \(v\). For \(\theta=\frac12\) the equivalence of (ii) and (iii) is the theorem of Lagarias.
Source: ch/cx2.tex, label cx:thm:positivity.




Proposition 31.9.2, page 1095 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the Riemann xi function, \(u_\sigma(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iv)\) and \(M_\sigma(T)=\int_0^Tu_\sigma(v)\,dv\). Let \(\frac12<\theta<1\) and \(T>0\), and suppose no zero of \(\xi\) lies on the segment \(\operatorname{Re}s=\theta\), \(0\le\operatorname{Im}s\le T\), nor on the segment \(\operatorname{Im}s=T\), \(\theta\le\operatorname{Re}s\le1\). Let \(N(\theta,T)\) be the number of zeros with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta\) and \(0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T\). Then \(2N(\theta,T)=M_1(T)-M_\theta(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)\), where \(\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)=-\int_\theta^1\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iT)\,d\sigma\) is the change of \(\arg\xi\) along the top side.
Source: ch/cx2.tex, label cx:prop:deficit.




Corollary 31.9.3, page 1096 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. With \(\xi\), \(u_\sigma\), \(M_\sigma(T)=\int_0^Tu_\sigma(v)\,dv\), \(N(\theta,T)\) and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)=-\int_\theta^1\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iT)\,d\sigma\) as in the mass deficit identity, let \(T>0\) not be the ordinate of a zero. For \(\theta\in(\frac12,1]\) not the real part of a zero below height \(T\), \(M_\theta(T)=M_1(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)-2N(\theta,T)\). The first two terms form a real analytic function of \(\theta\) with derivative \(\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iT)\), and \(2N(\theta,T)\) is a step function that drops by \(2m\) as \(\theta\) decreases through \(\operatorname{Re}\rho\), for each zero \(\rho\) of multiplicity \(m\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho>\frac12\) and \(0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T\). Hence \(\theta\mapsto M_\theta(T)\) extends continuously to \((\frac12,1]\) if and only if every zero below height \(T\) lies on the critical line, and its jumps occur exactly at the real parts of the off line zeros, of size twice the total multiplicity of the zeros with that real part and ordinate below \(T\).

Theorem 31.9.6, page 1102 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: computed.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the Riemann xi function, \(u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)\), \(\Xi(v)=\xi(\frac12+iv)\), \(T^*=1419.9\), \(N(T)\) the number of zeros \(\rho\) of \(\zeta\) with \(0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T\) and \(N(\theta,T)\) the number of those with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta\). Theorem 31.10.2, page 1105 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.

Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the Riemann xi function and \(u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)\). If \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78\), then, as measures, \(\mathfrak U_{7/8}\ge u_{7/8}(0)\,dv\), where \(\mathfrak U_{7/8}\) is the Thorin measure with density \(u_{7/8}\) (with atoms at the ordinates of zeros on \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78\) if there are any) and \(u_{7/8}(0)=\pi^{-1}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac78)=0.0055146635278\ldots\), and \(u_{7/8}(v)>u_{7/8}(0)\) wherever \(v\ne0\) is not the ordinate of a zero on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78\). Theorem 31.11.1, page 1110 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on The zero free half plane \(\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78\) for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book. The monotonicity of \(\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)\) is unconditional.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the Riemann xi function, \(u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)\) and \(\mathfrak U_\theta\) the Thorin measure at level \(\theta\), with density \(u_\theta\) for \(\theta>\frac78\). Suppose \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78\). Then for every \(\theta\in[\frac78,1]\) and every real \(v\ne0\) that is not the height of a zero on \(\operatorname{Re}s=\theta\), \(u_\theta(v)>u_\theta(0)=\pi^{-1}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta)\), and the singular part of \(\mathfrak U_\theta\) consists of positive atoms, which occur only if \(\theta=\frac78\) and a zero lies on \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78\); so \(\mathfrak U_\theta-u_\theta(0)\,dv\) is a positive measure. Unconditionally, \(\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)\) is increasing on \([\frac12,\infty)\). The values of \(u_\theta(0)\) run from \(0.0055147\) at \(\theta=\frac78\) to \(0.0073516\) at \(\theta=1\).

Theorem 31.11.3, page 1112 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: computed.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the Riemann xi function, \(u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)\) and \(\frac12<\theta\le1\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\); (ii) for every \(\theta'\in[\theta,1]\), \(u_{\theta'}(v)\ge u_{\theta'}(0)\) for all real \(v\) that are not heights of zeros on \(\operatorname{Re}s=\theta'\). Proposition 31.11.4, page 1114 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis, for the clause on the limiting bracket \(X\) (its minimiser and value in the first gap). The lower bounds for \(\inf B_c\) are a computation in ball arithmetic that needs only the hypothesis stated, no zeros of \(\zeta\) in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\), which holds for \(\theta=1\).
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the Riemann xi function, \(\theta\in(\frac12,1]\) be such that \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\), \(\theta'\in[\theta,1]\), \(c=2\theta'-1\), \(\gamma\) run over the ordinates of the zeros with multiplicity (both signs), \(V_c(v)=\sum_{|\gamma|<1419.9}\bigl(\frac{c^2}4+(v-\gamma)^2\bigr)^{-1}\) and \(B_c(v)=V_c(v)-V_c(0)-2\sum_{|\gamma|\ge1419.9}\gamma^{-2}\), the lower bound for \(\frac{2\pi}c(u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0))\) in which the zeros below height \(1419.9\) are on the critical line by the certified computation of the book. A computation shows \(\inf_{13.5\le|v|\le1418.9}B_c(v)\ge0.17575\) for \(c=1\), \(0.17838\) for \(c=\frac12\), \(0.17904\) for \(c=\frac14\) and \(0.17927\) as \(c\downarrow0\), each infimum approached at \(v=17.49\) to \(17.50\), between the first two zeros. Under the Riemann hypothesis the limiting bracket \(X(v)=\lim_{c\downarrow0}\frac{2\pi}c(u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0))=\sum_\rho\bigl(\frac1{(v-\gamma_\rho)^2}-\frac1{\gamma_\rho^2}\bigr)\) has in the first gap between the zeros \(14.1347\) and \(21.0220\) a unique minimiser \(v^*\in[17.4978,17.4980]\), and \(0.1838985448\le X(v^*)\le0.1838987563\). The statement that \(17.4979\) minimises \(X\) over all of \(13.5\le|v|\le1418.9\) is the author’s computation, not rerun, and is not claimed here.

Proposition 31.11.5, page 1116 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\theta'\in[\frac12,1)\), \(a=1-\theta'\), \(P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)\), and suppose \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'\), so that the Thorin measure \(\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\) exists and \(P_a*\mathfrak U_{\theta'}=u_1\,dv\) with \(u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)\). Let \(\mu\) be a finite positive measure and \(r=P_a*\mu-u_1\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). For a test function \(\varphi\) with \(\int e^{a|\omega|}|\widehat\varphi(\omega)|\,d\omega<\infty\) put \(\psi=\mathcal F^{-1}[e^{a|\omega|}\widehat\varphi]\), and assume that \(\psi\cdot(P_a*\mu+u_1)\) is integrable. Then \(\bigl|\int\varphi\,d\mu-\int\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\bigr|\le\int_{\mathbb{R}}|r(v)||\psi(v)|\,dv\).

Corollary 31.11.9, page 1122 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis, so that \(\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}\).
Statement. Assume the Riemann hypothesis, so that the Thorin measure at level \(\frac12\) is \(\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}\) over the ordinates with multiplicity. Let \(\varphi(v)=e^{-(v-c)^2/(2\sigma^2)}\), let \(\int\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{1/2}\in[\widehat M-B_0,\widehat M+B_0]\) with \(\widehat M>B_0\) and \(\int(v-c)\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{1/2}\in[\widehat m-B_1,\widehat m+B_1]\) be given bounds, let \(\gamma_*\) be an ordinate with \(|\gamma_*-c|\le R\), and let \(\Theta\ge\sum_{\gamma\ne\gamma_*}(|\gamma-c|+R)\varphi(\gamma)\), the sum over the other ordinates with multiplicity. Theorem 31.11.10, page 1124 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(v\ge2\), \(X\ge2\), \(s=1+iv\), \(L=\zeta'/\zeta\), \(\Lambda\) the von Mangoldt function and \(u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)\), and let \(u_1^X(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac1{1+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac{1+iv}2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n e^{-n/X}\cos(v\log n)\bigr]\) with \(\psi\) the digamma function. Then \(\pi(u_1(v)-u_1^X(v))=-\operatorname{Re}\sum_\rho\Gamma(\rho-s)X^{\rho-s}+\operatorname{Re}\Gamma(1-s)X^{1-s}+\operatorname{Re}[X^{-1}L(s-1)]+\operatorname{Re}R_X(s)\), with \(R_X(s)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{\operatorname{Re}w=-3/2}(-L(s+w))\Gamma(w)X^w\,dw\) and \(|R_X(s)|\le2.5X^{-3/2}\log(v+2)\). If every zero with \(|\gamma-v|\le Y\), \(Y\ge1\), lies on the critical line, then \(|u_1(v)-u_1^X(v)|\le\frac1\pi\bigl[c_\Gamma n(v)X^{-1/2}+2.6c_\Gamma'n(v+Y+1)e^{-\pi Y/2}+\sqrt{\pi/(v\sinh\pi v)}+\frac{27\log v}X+\frac{2.5\log(v+2)}{X^{3/2}}\bigr]\), where \(n(t)=0.39\log t+7\) bounds the number of ordinates in any interval of length one below height \(t\), \(c_\Gamma\le8.34\) and \(c_\Gamma'\le2.51\) are the explicit gamma function constants of the chapter.

Problem 31.1, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For EM applied to the continuous Cauchy deconvolution \(P_a*\mu=u_1\) at an atomic target, with \(R_k\) the residual after \(k\) steps and \(R^*\) its limit, prove the two phase picture of the chapter: a sublinear phase with \(k(R_k-R^*)\) near a constant of order \(50\) (observed \(54.7\), \(51.9\), \(49.5\), \(48.1\) at \(k=500\), \(1000\), \(2000\), \(3000\)), lasting of the order of \(10^4\) steps on the data of the chapter, followed by faster convergence on the support of the atoms with a grid independent rate, and compute that rate from the curvature of the divergence at the atoms. For the accelerated scheme with restart, explain the observed three point exponents, which oscillate between \(0.6\) and \(2.8\) with a running value near \(1.3\). The problem is open, and the numbers are observations.

Problem 31.2, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.

Problem 31.3, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)\). The smoothed prime sum evaluates \(u_1(v)\) to accuracy \(\varepsilon\) in time polynomial in \(\log v\) and in \(1/\varepsilon\). Is there an algorithm polynomial in \(\log v\) and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\)? Problem 31.4, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.

For a single atom at \(\gamma\) blurred by the Cauchy density \(P_a\) and observed exactly on a grid of spacing \(h\), with \(r_i\) the residuals at the grid points \(v_i\) and \(\psi_\gamma\) the weight of the a posteriori window bound for a window centred at \(\gamma\), what is the best achievable value of \(h\sum_i|\psi_\gamma(v_i)||r_i|\) after \(k\) steps of any first order method on the cone of nonnegative measures, as a function of \(k\), \(h\) and \(a\)?
