Theorem 11.4.6, page 476 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be Riemann’s xi function, let \(\rho=\beta+i\gamma\) run over its zeros (the nontrivial zeros of \(\zeta\)), counted with multiplicity, let \(P_w(x)=w/(\pi(w^2+x^2))\) be the Cauchy kernel of width \(w>0\), with \(P_0\) the unit point mass at \(0\), and for \(\alpha>\frac{1}{2}\) let \(v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)=v_\alpha^+(\theta)-v_\alpha^-(\theta)\) with \(v_\alpha^+(\theta)/\pi=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha,\,\gamma>0}[P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\alpha-\beta}(\theta+\gamma)]\) and \(v_\alpha^-(\theta)/\pi=\sum_{\beta>\alpha,\,\gamma>0}[P_{\beta-\alpha}(\theta-\gamma)+P_{\beta-\alpha}(\theta+\gamma)]\). The shifted clock \(T_\alpha\) has Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})=\varphi_\alpha^+(u)D_\alpha(u)\), where \(\varphi_\alpha^+(u)=\exp\{-\int_0^\infty\log(1+u/\theta^2)\,v_\alpha^+(\theta)\,\pi^{-1}d\theta\}\) is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with Thorin density \(v_\alpha^+/\pi\) and \(D_\alpha(u)=\prod_{\beta>\alpha,\,\gamma>0}\frac{(\beta-\alpha)^2+\gamma^2}{(\sqrt{u}-\beta+\alpha)^2+\gamma^2}\) is the defect. Let \(T_0=3\times10^{12}\), below which all zeros lie on the critical line (the verification of Platt and Trudgian), and let \(\Sigma_0=\sum_{\gamma>T_0}\gamma^{-2}\), the sum over all zeros above \(T_0\) counted with multiplicity. By the Riemann von Mangoldt formula with the explicit error term of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, \(\Sigma_0\) differs from \(\frac{\log(T_0/2\pi)+1}{2\pi T_0}=1.4797\times10^{-12}\) by less than \(2\times10^{-24}\), so \(\Sigma_0<1.48\times10^{-12}\). Then for every \(\alpha>\frac{1}{2}\) and every \(u\ge0\): (1) \(|\log D_\alpha(u)|\le(u+\sqrt{u})\,\Sigma_0\), so that \(e^{-1.5\times10^{-12}(u+\sqrt{u})}\varphi_\alpha^+(u)\le\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}\le e^{1.5\times10^{-12}(u+\sqrt{u})}\varphi_\alpha^+(u)\); (2) the negative part of the density satisfies \(v_\alpha^-(\theta)/\pi\le2\Sigma_0/\pi<9.43\times10^{-13}\) for \(0\le\theta\le T_0/2\); (3) consequently \(v_\alpha(\theta)>0\) for all \(0\le\theta\le T_0/2\) whenever \(\alpha-\frac{1}{2}>6\times10^{-10}\). Part of the proof is certified in ball arithmetic.

Corollary 11.4.7, page 477 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be Riemann’s xi function, let \(v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)\) for \(\alpha>\frac{1}{2}\) (the function whose quotient by \(\pi\) is the Thorin density of the shifted clock \(T_\alpha\), the positive random variable with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_\alpha}=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})\), in the chart \(\theta=\sqrt{z}\), when every zero lies to the left of the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha\)), let \(T_0=3\times10^{12}\) (every zero off the critical line has \(|\gamma|>T_0\), by the verification of Platt and Trudgian) and let \(V_\xi=(\log\xi)''(\frac{1}{2})=0.04620998623\). (1) For every \(\alpha>\frac{1}{2}\), \(v_\alpha(\theta)>0\) for \(|\theta|\le T_0-\frac{1}{2}\). (2) For every \(\alpha\in(\frac{1}{2},7.35]\), \(v_\alpha(\theta)>v_\alpha(0)\) for \(0<|\theta|\le T_0-\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}\), and \(0<v_\alpha(0)\le(\alpha-\frac{1}{2})V_\xi\).

Proposition 11.5.1, page 489 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)\), an entire function of \(u\) whose zeros are the numbers \(-a_k\), \(a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2\), one for each pair \(\{\rho,1-\rho\}\) of zeros of \(\xi\) counted with multiplicity (so \(a_k=\gamma_k^2>0\) for a zero \(\rho_k=\tfrac12+i\gamma_k\) on the critical line). With no hypothesis \(1/G\) is the Laplace transform of a probability law on \([0,\infty)\), the law of the clock \(T\), so that \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)\) for \(u\ge0\). Let \(W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}\), \(t>0\), be the heat trace, let \(m_0=\mathbb{E}T=\sum_ka_k^{-1}=0.0231049931\ldots\), and let \(\widehat T\) be the size biased clock, the variable with law \(t\,\mathbb{P}(T\in dt)/m_0\). With no hypothesis, \(\widehat T\overset{d}{=}T+A\), where \(A\) is independent of \(T\) and has density \(W(t)/m_0\) on \((0,\infty)\). The Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if \(A\) is a mixture of exponential laws, that is, \(A\overset{d}{=}E/V\) with \(E\) a standard exponential variable independent of a variable \(V>0\); and then \(V\) has the law \(m_0^{-1}\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2}\delta_{\gamma^2}\), the ordinates \(\gamma\) of the zeros \(\tfrac12+i\gamma\) counted with multiplicity.
Source: ch/pakes.tex, label pk:prop:sizebias.




Theorem 11.5.8, page 496 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)\), an entire function of \(u\) whose zeros are the numbers \(-a_k\), \(a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2\), one for each pair \(\{\rho,1-\rho\}\) of zeros of \(\xi\) counted with multiplicity. With no hypothesis \(1/G\) is the Laplace transform of a probability law on \([0,\infty)\), the law of the clock \(T\) (the centre clock), and \(W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}\), \(t>0\), is the heat trace. The ladder functions are \(W^{[0]}=W\) and \(W^{[j+1]}(t)=-t\,\frac{d}{dt}W^{[j]}(t)\). With no hypothesis the clock is self decomposable: \(T\overset{d}{=}\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\,dZ_t\) for a subordinator \(Z=Z^{[1]}\), its driving process, with Laplace exponent \(u(\log G)'(u)\) and Lévy density \(-W'(x)\); and \(Z^{[j+1]}\) denotes the driving process of the law of \(Z^{[j]}_1\) whenever that law is self decomposable. A law \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) is self decomposable if for every \(c\in(0,1)\) there is a law \(\mu_c\) with \(\widehat\mu(z)=\widehat\mu(cz)\widehat{\mu_c}(z)\) for the characteristic functions; Urbanik’s class \(L_0\) consists of the self decomposable laws and, for \(n\ge1\), \(L_n\) consists of the laws in \(L_{n-1}\) all of whose components \(\mu_c\) lie in \(L_{n-1}\). Unconditionally, that is, using only the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis below height \(2197.3\) (Platt and Trudgian): \(W^{[3]}(t)>0\) for every \(t>0\), and \(W^{[4]}(e^{-4.15})<0\) (in ball arithmetic \(W^{[4]}(e^{-4.15})=-0.11089729616255\pm10^{-23}\)). Consequently \(W\), \(W^{[1]}\) and \(W^{[2]}\) are positive on \((0,\infty)\); the centre clock lies in \(L_2\) and not in \(L_3\); its driving process \(Z=Z^{[1]}\) and the driving process \(Z^{[2]}\) of \(Z\) are self decomposable at every time (the laws of \(Z_s\) and of \(Z^{[2]}_s\) are self decomposable for every \(s>0\)); and the driving process \(Z^{[3]}\) of \(Z^{[2]}\) is self decomposable at no time.
Source: ch/pakes2.tex, label pk:thm:ladder.




Corollary 11.5.9, page 498 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)\), and \(T\) the clock, the random variable with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)\) for \(u\ge0\) (it exists with no hypothesis). With no hypothesis \(T\) is self decomposable: \(T\overset{d}{=}\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\,dZ_t\) for a subordinator \(Z\), its driving process, with Laplace exponent \(u(\log G)'(u)\); and \(Z^{[2]}\) denotes the driving process of the self decomposable law of \(Z_1\). A law \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) is self decomposable if for every \(c\in(0,1)\) there is a law \(\mu_c\) with \(\widehat\mu(z)=\widehat\mu(cz)\widehat{\mu_c}(z)\) for the characteristic functions; Urbanik’s class \(L_1\) consists of the self decomposable laws all of whose components \(\mu_c\) are self decomposable. With no hypothesis, for every \(s>0\) the laws of \(Z_s\) and of \(Z^{[2]}_s\) are self decomposable, hence unimodal, and the law of \(Z_s\) lies in \(L_1\).
Source: ch/pakes2.tex, label pk:cor:unimodal.




Theorem 11.5.11, page 502 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)\), and \(T\) the clock, \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)\) for \(u\ge0\). With no hypothesis \(T\overset{d}{=}\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\,dZ_t\) for a subordinator \(Z\) (its driving process) with Laplace exponent \(\Psi_Z(u)=u(\log G)'(u)\). Let \(H\) be the inverse function of \(\log G\) near \(0\) and \(g=\Psi_Z\circ H=H/H'=\sum_{k\ge1}g_kw^k\), so that \(g_1=1\). A supercritical continuous state branching process with finite Malthusian parameter is obtained, by Lamperti’s time change, from a spectrally positive Lévy process \(Y\) with Laplace exponent \(\Psi_Y(u)=-\log\mathbb{E}e^{-uY_1}\) and \(\Psi_Y'(0)\in(0,\infty)\); started at \(z>0\) it is a process \((\mathsf{B}_t)_{t\ge0}\) with \(\mathbb{E}\mathsf{B}_t=ze^{\Psi_Y'(0)t}\), and the nonnegative martingale \(e^{-\Psi_Y'(0)t}\mathsf{B}_t\) converges almost surely to a limit \(\mathsf{M}\). With no hypothesis, \((-1)^{15}g_{16}<0\): in ball arithmetic \(g_{16}=1.49524474945112\times10^{-15}\pm2\times10^{-30}\). Consequently, for no \(\lambda>0\), no such \(Y\) and no initial state \(z>0\) does \(\lambda T\) have the law of \(\mathsf{M}\): no positive multiple of the centre clock is the martingale limit of a supercritical continuous state branching process with finite Malthusian parameter, from any initial state.
Source: ch/pakes2.tex, label pk:thm:nobranch.




Proposition 11.5.12, page 504 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(\Phi(v)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5v/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})\) the Pólya kernel, an even positive function with \(\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv\); for \(t\le0\) put \(\Phi_t(v)=e^{tv^2/4}\Phi(v)\). For an even positive integrable function \(g\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) put \(\widehat g(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv\) and \(R_g(s)=\widehat g(0)/\widehat g(i\sqrt s)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(v)\,dv\big/\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(v)\cosh(\sqrt s\,v)\,dv\) for the \(s\ge0\) at which the last integral converges; for \(g=\Phi\) this is \(R_\Phi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\), the Laplace transform of the clock. A GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) is a random variable \(H\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\) for \(u>0\), where the drift \(d\ge0\) and the Thorin measure \(U\), a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\), satisfy \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log z|\,U(dz)+\int_{(1,\infty)}z^{-1}U(dz)<\infty\). Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be a property of even positive integrable functions on \(\mathbb{R}\) that \(\Phi_t\) has for some \(t<0\). Then \(\mathcal{P}\) implies neither that \(\widehat g\) has only real zeros nor that \(R_g\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC, for the functions \(g\) with \(\mathcal{P}\): the function \(g=\Phi_t\) has \(\mathcal{P}\), while \(\widehat g\) has nonreal zeros and \(R_g\) is not the Laplace transform of a GGC. At every \(t\le0\) the kernel \(\Phi_t\) (i) is positive and even, and strictly decreasing on \((0,\infty)\); (ii) is log concave; (iii) satisfies \(\log\Phi_t(v)=-\pi e^{2|v|}+O(v^2)\) as \(|v|\to\infty\); (iv) extends analytically to the strip \(|\operatorname{Im}v|<\pi/4\). So no combination of (i) to (iv) implies that \(\widehat g\) has only real zeros, or that \(R_g\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC. The proof uses the theorem of Rodgers and Tao that the de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative, which gives a nonreal zero of \(\widehat{\Phi_t}\) for every \(t<0\).
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prop:filter.




Proposition 11.5.13, page 505 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(\Phi(v)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5v/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})\) the Pólya kernel, an even positive function with \(\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)\). For \(t\le0\) let \(\Phi_t(v)=e^{tv^2/4}\Phi(v)\), let \(p_t=\Phi_t/\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_t\) be the corresponding probability density, which is even and decreasing on \((0,\infty)\), and let \(X_t\) be a variable with density \(p_t\) (so \(X_0\) is the Pólya variable). For every \(t\le0\) the function \(h_t(\rho)=-2\rho\int_\rho^\infty p_t'(r)\,dr/\sqrt{r^2-\rho^2}\), \(\rho>0\), is a positive probability density, and \(p_t(v)=\frac1\pi\int_{|v|}^\infty h_t(\rho)\,d\rho/\sqrt{\rho^2-v^2}\) for \(v\ne0\). Equivalently, \(X_t\overset{d}{=}\varrho_t\cos\Theta\) with \(\Theta\) uniform on \([0,2\pi)\) and \(\varrho_t\) of density \(h_t\) independent of \(\Theta\): \(X_t\) is a mixture of arcsine laws, the first coordinate of the rotation invariant vector \(\varrho_t(\cos\Theta,\sin\Theta)\) in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) and also of a rotation invariant vector in \(\mathbb{R}^3\).
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prop:arcsine.




Proposition 11.5.15, page 508 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(f(b)=\sum_{m\ge1}(4\pi^2m^4b-6\pi m^2)e^{-\pi m^2b}\), \(b>0\), the density of the variable \(\mathcal{B}\) of Biane, Pitman and Yor, with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda\mathcal{B}}=(\sqrt{\pi\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{\pi\lambda})^2\) and \(\mathbb{E}\mathcal{B}^{s/2}=2\xi(s)\); \(\mathcal{B}\) is a GGC with Thorin measure \(2\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_{\pi m^2}\). For real \(t\) let \(\mathcal{B}_t\) be the variable with density proportional to \(e^{t(\log b)^2/16}f(b)\) on \((0,\infty)\), so that \(\mathcal{B}_0=\mathcal{B}\). A GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) is a random variable \(H\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\) for \(u>0\), with drift \(d\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(U\), a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log z|\,U(dz)+\int_{(1,\infty)}z^{-1}U(dz)<\infty\). (i) \(\mathcal{B}_t\) is not a GGC for \(t=-20\), \(-5\), \(-1\), \(-\tfrac12\), \(-\tfrac1{10}\), \(-\tfrac1{100}\), \(\tfrac1{100}\), \(\tfrac15\), \(1\) and \(5\). (ii) There is \(t_0>0\) such that \(\mathcal{B}_t\) is not a GGC for \(0<|t|<t_0\).
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prop:bpytilt.




Proposition 11.5.18, page 511 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: counterexample, proved.
Statement. Let \(\chi_{-8}\) be the real primitive Dirichlet character modulo \(8\) with \(\chi_{-8}(-1)=-1\) (so \(\chi_{-8}(n)=1\) for \(n\equiv1,3\), \(\chi_{-8}(n)=-1\) for \(n\equiv5,7 \pmod{8}\), and \(\chi_{-8}(n)=0\) for even \(n\)), let \(\vartheta(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}n\chi_{-8}(n)e^{-\pi n^2x/8}\) for \(x>0\), a positive function with \(\vartheta(1/x)=x^{3/2}\vartheta(x)\), and \(\xi(s,\chi_{-8})=\int_0^\infty\vartheta(x)x^{(s+1)/2}\,dx/x=(8/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\tfrac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_{-8})\). Let \(\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-8}}\) be the variable with density \(b^{-1/2}\vartheta(b)/\xi(0,\chi_{-8})\) on \((0,\infty)\), so that \(\mathbb{E}\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-8}}^{s/2}=\xi(s,\chi_{-8})/\xi(0,\chi_{-8})\); its reciprocal \(1/\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-8}}\) has density \(\vartheta(x)/\xi(0,\chi_{-8})\). A GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) is a random variable \(H\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\) for \(u>0\), with drift \(d\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(U\), a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log z|\,U(dz)+\int_{(1,\infty)}z^{-1}U(dz)<\infty\). Neither \(\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-8}}\) nor \(1/\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-8}}\) is a GGC. (The proof is a certificate in ball arithmetic: the cumulants \(\kappa_2,\kappa_3,\kappa_4\) of a GGC with a finite fourth moment satisfy \(2\kappa_2\kappa_4\ge3\kappa_3^2\), and \(3\kappa_3^2-2\kappa_2\kappa_4\) equals \(7.55465911093\pm4\times10^{-12}\) for \(\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-8}}\) and \(78.8854168657\pm2\times10^{-11}\) for \(1/\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-8}}\), both positive.)
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prop:chi8.




Proposition 11.5.19, page 512 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(q\ge3\) and let \(a=(a_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a real sequence of period \(q\) with \(a_1=1\) and \(a_{q - n}=-a_n\), whose theta series \(\vartheta_a(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}na_ne^{-\pi n^2x/q}\), \(x>0\), satisfies \(\vartheta_a(1/x)=x^{3/2}\vartheta_a(x)\) and is positive. Put \(\xi(s,a)=\int_0^\infty\vartheta_a(x)x^{(s+1)/2}\,dx/x\), let \(\mathcal{B}_a\) be the variable with density \(b^{-1/2}\vartheta_a(b)/\xi(0,a)\) on \((0,\infty)\), so that \(1/\mathcal{B}_a\) has density \(\vartheta_a(x)/\xi(0,a)\), and for \(\lambda>0\) put \(w=\sqrt{\pi q\lambda}\) and \(\Sigma_a(w)=\sum_{1\le n<q/2}a_n\sinh\frac{(q - 2n)w}{q}\). A GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) is a random variable \(H\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\) for \(u>0\), with drift \(d\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(U\) (a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log z|\,U(dz)+\int_{(1,\infty)}z^{-1}U(dz)<\infty\)); the Laplace transform of a GGC extends holomorphically and without zeros to \(\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]\) and cannot vanish on \((-\infty,0)\) where it extends meromorphically. Then \(\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda x}\vartheta_a(x)\,dx=\sqrt q\,\Sigma_a(w)/\sinh w\) and \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda/\mathcal{B}_a}=\sqrt q\,\Sigma_a(w)/(\xi(0,a)\sinh w)\), and \(\xi(0,a)=q^{-1/2}\sum_{1\le n<q/2}(q - 2n)a_n\); the first formula is formula (96) of Biane, Pitman and Yor in this normalisation. In particular: (i) for the character of discriminant \(-4\) (\(q=4\), \(a=(1,0,-1,0)\)), \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda/\mathcal{B}_a}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\pi\lambda}\), and \(1/\mathcal{B}_a\), which is \(\tfrac\pi2\) times the exit time of Brownian motion from \((-1,1)\), is a GGC; (ii) for the character of discriminant \(-3\) (\(q=3\), \(a=(1,-1,0)\)), \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda/\mathcal{B}_a}=3\sinh(w/3)/\sinh w=\prod_{3\nmid m}(1+3\lambda/(\pi m^2))^{-1}\), so that \(1/\mathcal{B}_a\) is a GGC with Thorin measure \(\sum_{3\nmid m}\delta_{\pi m^2/3}\), and it is \(\tfrac{3\pi}2\) times the hitting time of \(1\) by a three dimensional Bessel process started at \(\tfrac13\); (iii) for the character of discriminant \(-8\) (\(q=8\), \(a=(1,0,1,0,-1,0,-1,0)\)), \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda/\mathcal{B}_a}=\cosh(w/4)/\cosh(w/2)=\prod_{k\ge1}(1+\lambda/(4\alpha_k))/(1+\lambda/\alpha_k)\) with \(\alpha_k=\tfrac\pi8(2k-1)^2\), so that \(1/\mathcal{B}_a\) is infinitely divisible with Lévy density \(\sum_k(e^{-\alpha_kx}-e^{-4\alpha_kx})/x>0\), and it is \(\pi\) times the hitting time of \(1\) by a reflected Brownian motion started at \(\tfrac12\) (the identifications of (ii) and (iii) with hitting times are those of Biane, Pitman and Yor); it is not a GGC, because its Laplace transform, continued meromorphically, vanishes at \(\lambda=-\pi/2\); (iv) if \(a=\chi_d\) for a real primitive character of fundamental discriminant \(d<0\) with \(\chi_d(2)=1\), that is \(d\equiv1 \pmod{8}\), and \(q=|d|\), the Laplace transform of \(1/\mathcal{B}_a\), continued meromorphically by the closed form, vanishes at a point of \((-4\pi/q,-\pi/q)\), so \(1/\mathcal{B}_a\) is not a GGC; for \(\chi_{-7}\) the point is \(\lambda=-1.033610573\). The same holds for the function of Davenport and Heilbronn, with \(q=5\), \(a=(1,\varkappa,-\varkappa,-1,0)\) and \(\varkappa=(\sqrt{10-2\sqrt5}-2)/(\sqrt5-1)\), at \(\lambda=-2.046575671\).
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prop:reflected.




Problem 11.1, page 514 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(q\ge3\), \(p\in\{0,1\}\) and let \(a=(a_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a real sequence of period \(q\) with \(a_1=1\) and \(a_{q - n}=(-1)^pa_n\), whose theta series \(\vartheta_a(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^pa_ne^{-\pi n^2x/q}\), \(x>0\), satisfies \(\vartheta_a(1/x)=x^{p+1/2}\vartheta_a(x)\); put \(\xi(s,a)=\int_0^\infty\vartheta_a(x)x^{(s+p)/2}\,dx/x=(q/\pi)^{(s+p)/2}\Gamma(\tfrac{s+p}2)\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}\), an entire function with \(\xi(s,a)=\xi(1-s,a)\). When \(\vartheta_a>0\) (a positive kernel) let \(\mathcal{B}_a\) be the variable with density \(b^{p/2-1}\vartheta_a(b)/\xi(0,a)\) on \((0,\infty)\), so that \(\mathbb{E}\mathcal{B}_a^{s/2}=\xi(s,a)/\xi(0,a)\). For the completed Riemann zeta function \(\xi\) the corresponding variable is \(\mathcal{B}\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda\mathcal{B}}=(\sqrt{\pi\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{\pi\lambda})^2\) and \(\mathbb{E}\mathcal{B}^{s/2}=2\xi(s)\), which is a GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution: a variable \(H\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\), \(u>0\), for a drift \(d\ge0\) and a positive measure \(U\) on \((0,\infty)\), the Thorin measure). The test by Hankel matrices of cumulants: for a positive variable \(\mathcal{V}\) with \(\ell(\lambda)=\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda\mathcal{V}}\) put \(\kappa_k(\lambda)=(-1)^k\frac{d^k}{d\lambda^k}\log\ell(\lambda)\) and \(c_k(\lambda)=\kappa_{k+1}(\lambda)/k!\); if \(\mathcal{V}\) is a GGC, the Hankel matrices \(\mathcal{K}_n(\lambda)=[c_{i+j}(\lambda)]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) and \(\mathcal{K}'_n(\lambda)=[c_{i+j+1}(\lambda)]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) are positive semidefinite for all \(n\) and \(\lambda\ge0\), so a variable for which one of them has a negative eigenvalue is not a GGC, and is said to fail the test (applied numerically for \(n\le12\) at \(\lambda=0\), \(\tfrac12\), \(2\), \(10\), \(20\), \(50\) and \(200\)). Question. Find a natural class of functions \(\xi(s,a)\) with positive kernels, containing \(\xi\), in which the GGC property of \(\mathcal{B}_a\) implies that every zero of \(\xi(s,a)\) lies on the critical line \(\operatorname{Re}s=\tfrac12\), or find a function in such a class whose variable \(\mathcal{B}_a\) is a GGC and which has a zero off the line. Since \(\mathcal{B}\) is a GGC, the first answer for a class containing \(\xi\) proves the Riemann Hypothesis. No candidate for the second is known: the function of Davenport and Heilbronn (coefficients of period \(5\), \((1,\varkappa,-\varkappa,-1,0)\) with \(\varkappa=(\sqrt{10-2\sqrt5}-2)/(\sqrt5-1)\)), the members with a positive kernel, among the \(17\) tested, of the real one parameter family \(f_r\) of combinations of \(L(s,\chi_{-7})\), \(L(s,\chi)\) and \(L(s,\bar\chi)\), with \(\chi\) and \(\bar\chi\) the complex odd characters modulo \(7\), that have real coefficients, \(a_1=1\) and the functional equation of the class, and the tilts \(\mathcal{B}_t\) of \(\mathcal{B}\) with density proportional to \(e^{t(\log b)^2/16}f(b)\) at the eleven values of \(t<0\) tested (\(f\) the density of \(\mathcal{B}\)) all fail the test by Hankel matrices of cumulants.
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prob:ggc.




Problem 11.2, page 515 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{B}\) be the variable of Biane, Pitman and Yor, a GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) with density \(f(b)=\sum_{m\ge1}(4\pi^2m^4b-6\pi m^2)e^{-\pi m^2b}\), \(b>0\), \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda\mathcal{B}}=(\sqrt{\pi\lambda}/\sinh\sqrt{\pi\lambda})^2\) and \(\mathbb{E}\mathcal{B}^{s/2}=2\xi(s)\) for the completed Riemann zeta function \(\xi\), and for real \(t\) let \(\mathcal{B}_t\) be the variable with density proportional to \(e^{t(\log b)^2/16}f(b)\) on \((0,\infty)\), so that \(\mathcal{B}_0=\mathcal{B}\). Let \(\Phi(v)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5v/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})\) be the Pólya kernel, an even positive function with \(\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv\), so that \(f(b)=b^{-5/4}\Phi(\tfrac12\log b)\), and for real \(t\) let \(\Phi_t(v)=e^{tv^2/4}\Phi(v)\) be the damped kernel; then \(\mathcal{B}_t\) has density proportional to \(b^{-5/4}\Phi_t(\tfrac12\log b)\). Question. Is \(\mathcal{B}_t\) a GGC for no \(t\ne0\)? For \(t<0\) a positive answer would mean that the GGC property of the variable \(\mathcal{B}_t\) built from the damped Pólya kernel \(\Phi_t(v)=e^{tv^2/4}\Phi(v)\) is lost at every \(t<0\), although the Pólya kernel \(\Phi\) itself has it (\(\mathcal{B}_0=\mathcal{B}\) is a GGC). Known: \(\mathcal{B}_t\) is not a GGC for \(0<|t|<t_0\) for some \(t_0>0\), and for \(t=-20\), \(-5\), \(-1\), \(-\tfrac12\), \(-\tfrac1{10}\), \(-\tfrac1{100}\), \(\tfrac1{100}\), \(\tfrac15\), \(1\) and \(5\).
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prob:tilt.




Problem 11.3, page 515 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For a real primitive Dirichlet character \(\chi_d\) of fundamental discriminant \(d\) (\(p=1\) for \(d<0\), \(p=0\) for \(d>0\)) with positive theta series \(\vartheta_{\chi_d}(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^p\chi_d(n)e^{-\pi n^2x/|d|}\), let \(\mathcal{B}_{\chi_d}\) be the variable with density proportional to \(b^{p/2-1}\vartheta_{\chi_d}(b)\) on \((0,\infty)\). A GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) is a random variable \(H\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\) for \(u>0\), with drift \(d\ge0\) and a positive Thorin measure \(U\) on \((0,\infty)\). For a positive variable \(\mathcal{V}\) with \(\ell(\lambda)=\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda\mathcal{V}}\) put \(\kappa_k(\lambda)=(-1)^k\frac{d^k}{d\lambda^k}\log\ell(\lambda)\) and \(c_k(\lambda)=\kappa_{k+1}(\lambda)/k!\); if \(\mathcal{V}\) is a GGC, the Hankel matrices \(\mathcal{K}_n(\lambda)=[c_{i+j}(\lambda)]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) and \(\mathcal{K}'_n(\lambda)=[c_{i+j+1}(\lambda)]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) are positive semidefinite for all \(n\) and \(\lambda\ge0\), so a negative eigenvalue shows that \(\mathcal{V}\) is not a GGC. A variable passes the test to order \(12\) if no \(\mathcal{K}_n(\lambda)\) or \(\mathcal{K}'_n(\lambda)\) with \(n\le12\) has a negative eigenvalue at \(\lambda=0\), \(\tfrac12\), \(2\), \(10\), \(20\), \(50\) and \(200\) (a numerical test). Question. Which of the variables \(\mathcal{B}_{\chi_d}\) for \(d=-4\), \(-3\), \(5\), \(8\) and \(12\), which pass the test to order \(12\), are GGCs? (For \(d=24\) the test fails at order \(11\).) On the reciprocal side, \(1/\mathcal{B}_{\chi_d}\) is a GGC for \(d=-3\) and \(d=-4\); for \(d=-4\) it is \(\tfrac\pi2\) times the exit time of Brownian motion from \((-1,1)\), whose density is not hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM), so the question for \(\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{-4}}\) cannot be settled through HCM. For even characters the Laplace transform of the reciprocal variable is the series \(\frac2{\xi(0,a)}\sum_na_nK_0\big(2n\sqrt{\pi\lambda/q}\big)\) of Bessel functions \(K_0\) (with \(q=|d|\), \(a_n=\chi_d(n)\) and \(\xi(0,a)\) the normalising constant of the density of \(\mathcal{B}_{\chi_d}\)), and no product formula for it is known to the authors.
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prob:side.




Problem 11.4, page 515 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)\), with zeros \(-a_k\), \(a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2\), one for each pair \(\{\rho,1-\rho\}\) of zeros of \(\xi\) counted with multiplicity. Let \(W(t)=\sum_ke^{-a_kt}\) be the heat trace, \(m_0=\sum_ka_k^{-1}\), and \(A\) a variable with density \(W(t)/m_0\) on \((0,\infty)\) (the size biased clock is the clock plus an independent copy of \(A\)). The Li coefficients are \(\lambda_n=\sum_\rho\big(1-(1-1/\rho)^n\big)\), \(n\ge1\), the sum over the zeros \(\rho\) of \(\xi\) grouped in pairs \(\{\rho,1-\rho\}\); they satisfy \(\lambda_n=\sum_k\varphi_n(a_k)\) with \(\varphi_n(z)=2-\big(\frac{2\sqrt z+i}{2\sqrt z-i}\big)^n-\big(\frac{2\sqrt z-i}{2\sqrt z+i}\big)^n\), a rational function of \(z\) with a pole of order \(n\) at \(z=-\tfrac14\) and no constant term in \((z+\tfrac14)^{-1}\) (for example \(\varphi_1(z)=(z+\tfrac14)^{-1}\) and \(\varphi_2(z)=4z(z+\tfrac14)^{-2}\)). Let \(k_n\) be the function with \(\int_0^\infty e^{-zt}k_n(t)\,dt=\varphi_n(z)\); it has the form \(k_n(t)=e^{-t/4}p_n(t)\) with \(p_n\) a polynomial of degree \(n-1\) (for example \(k_1(t)=e^{-t/4}\) and \(k_2(t)=(4-t)e^{-t/4}\)). With no hypothesis, \(\lambda_n=\int_0^\infty k_n(t)W(t)\,dt=m_0\,\mathbb{E}k_n(A)\). Question. Which unconditional properties of \(W\), or of \(A\), force \(\mathbb{E}k_n(A)\ge0\) for every \(n\), which is the Riemann Hypothesis by Li’s criterion? Positivity of \(W\) gives \(n=1\); complete monotonicity of \(W\), which is equivalent to RH, gives every \(n\), since \(\varphi_n\ge0\) on \((0,\infty)\).
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prob:li.




Problem 11.5, page 515 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\Phi\) be the Pólya kernel, with \(\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv\) for the completed Riemann zeta function \(\xi\), let \(\Phi_t(v)=e^{tv^2/4}\Phi(v)\), \(\Xi_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi_t(v)\cos(\theta v)\,dv\) and \(R_t(s)=\Xi_t(0)/\Xi_t(i\sqrt s)\), so that \(R_0(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\) is the Laplace transform of the clock. The zeros of \(\Xi_t\) are all real exactly when \(t\ge\Lambda\), where \(\Lambda\) is the de Bruijn Newman constant, \(0\le\Lambda\le0.2\) (Rodgers and Tao; Platt and Trudgian). For \(t\ge\Lambda\), in particular unconditionally for every \(t\ge0.2\), let \(\pm\theta_k(t)\), \(0<\theta_1(t)<\theta_2(t)<\cdots\), be the zeros of \(\Xi_t\) and \(a_k(t)=\theta_k(t)^2\); then \(R_t(s)=\prod_k(1+s/a_k(t))^{-1}\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC (generalised, or generalized, gamma convolution) with Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{a_k(t)}\). At \(t=0\) put \(a_k(0)=a_k=-(\rho_k-\tfrac12)^2\), one for each pair \(\{\rho,1-\rho\}\) of zeros of \(\xi\) (real when RH holds), the numbers of the clock. Put \(W(x;t)=\sum_ke^{-a_k(t)x}\) and \(W^{[j]}(x;t)=(-x\,\partial_x)^jW(x;t)\). A law with this Laplace transform lies in Urbanik’s class \(L_n\) exactly when \(W^{[n+1]}(\cdot\,;t)\ge0\) on \((0,\infty)\) (the classes \(L_n\): \(L_0\) is the class of self decomposable laws and \(L_n\) the class of laws in \(L_{n-1}\) all of whose components lie in \(L_{n-1}\)); the index on the window \(0\le-\log x\le8\) is the largest \(n\) with \(W^{[1]},\dots,W^{[n+1]}\ge0\) there. Question. Describe the ladder index of \(R_t\) along the de Bruijn Newman flow. A numerical computation (not certified for \(t>0\)) finds on the window the index two of the clock at the tested values of \(t\) up to \(27.8\) and the index one at the tested values \(t=27.9\), \(30\), \(40\) and \(50\). Is the index nonincreasing in \(t\), and is it one for all large \(t\)?
Source: ch/pakes3.tex, label pk:prob:ladder.

title: Results by chapter Computing the Riemann Hypothesis
text:
Problem 12.1, page 524 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(X\) be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\); its moment generating function is \(\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)\). Put \(b_j=\mathbb{E}X^{2j}/(2j)!\), so that \(\Xi(t)/\Xi(0)=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^jb_jt^{2j}\) with \(\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)\), and for \(d,n\ge0\) let \(J_{d,n}(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d\binom di(n+i)!\,b_{n+i}x^i\) be the Jensen polynomial of degree \(d\) and shift \(n\) of the sequence \(j!\,b_j\). Pólya proved that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if every \(J_{d,n}\) has only real zeros. The finite free multiplicative convolution \(\boxtimes_d\) of polynomials of degree \(d\) multiplies their normalised coefficients (the coefficient of \(x^{d - i}\) divided by \(\binom di\), up to the sign \((-1)^i\)) and keeps roots real and of one sign when both factors have real roots of one sign. The normalised coefficients of the reversed Jensen polynomial \(x^dJ_{d,n}(1/x)\) are, up to the signs \((-1)^i\), the numbers \((n+i)!\,b_{n+i}\) for \(0\le i\le d\). A factorisation \((n+i)!\,b_{n+i}=\alpha_i\beta_i\) into the normalised coefficients of two polynomials with only real roots of one sign would therefore give real zeros of \(J_{d,n}\). Open problem: find such factorisations for every shift \(n\) at a fixed degree \(d\), or show that none exists with factors of a given kind. The obvious split, a Gaussian multiplier sequence \(q^{i^2}\) with \(0<q\le1\) times a residual close to the coefficients of \((1+x)^d\), fails, because a root of multiplicity \(d\) splits into nonreal roots under a generic perturbation. Dividing the normalised coefficients of a polynomial with real roots of one sign by \((a)_i=a(a+1)\cdots(a+i-1)\) keeps its roots real, but multiplying them by \((a)_i\) does not (it turns \((1+x)^2\) into \(1+2ax+a(a+1)x^2\), whose discriminant is \(-4a<0\)). A factorisation has to put real structure into both factors.
Source: ch/ch22.tex, label prob:wigfree:jensen.




Problem 12.2, page 524 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(X\) be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\), and let \(\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)\). The book proves that for no \(a>0\) is \(|X|\) or \(X^2\) a scale mixture of Gamma\((a)\) laws, and that, under the Riemann Hypothesis, removing a gamma layer keeps zeros real while adding one does not: the function \(G_a(u)=\sum_kb_ku^k/(a)_k\), with \(b_k=\mathbb{E}X^{2k}/(2k)!\) and \((a)_k=a(a+1)\cdots(a+k-1)\), lies in the Laguerre Pólya class (the entire functions that are locally uniform limits of real rooted polynomials) for every \(a>0\), whereas multiplying the coefficients by \((a)_k\) instead does not preserve real zeros. Open problem: find a variable in which the Pólya density, or \(\Xi\) itself, has an expansion in Laguerre or Meixner Pollaczek polynomials with positive coefficients and truncations with only real zeros. The symmetric Meixner Pollaczek expansions treated in the book converge slowly, and a real rooted construction from their coefficients is a separate open problem of the chapter on the reciprocal zeta function.
Source: ch/ch22.tex, label prob:wigfree:laguerre.




Problem 12.3, page 525 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots\) be the positive ordinates of the zeros \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_j\) of \(\zeta\), put \(a_j=\gamma_j^2\) and let \(\nu=\sum_ja_j^{-1}\delta_{1/a_j}\), a measure whose moments are computed from the Taylor coefficients at the centre of the Xi function \(\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) is Riemann’s xi function. Under the Riemann Hypothesis \(\nu\) is a positive measure and all its Jacobi parameters exist: write \(\alpha_n\) for the diagonal entries and \(\beta_n>0\) for the off diagonal entries of its Jacobi matrix, the recurrence coefficients of its orthogonal polynomials. A semicircle law is a local model for them: constant parameters \(\alpha_n=\alpha\), \(\beta_n=\beta\) give the semicircle law on \([\alpha-2\beta,\alpha+2\beta]\), and a local model with right end \(L_n\) of the interval for row \(n\) has \(\alpha_n=\frac12L_n\) and \(\beta_n=\frac14L_n\). Let \(N\) be the smooth Riemann von Mangoldt count of the ordinates, \(n(L)=\int_{(0,L^{-1/2})}dN(T)/\sqrt{1-LT^2}\), and define \(L_n\) by \(n(L_n)=n\). Open problem: under the Riemann Hypothesis, prove that \(\alpha_n\sim2\beta_n\sim\frac12L_n\) as \(n\to\infty\), a spectral form of the Riemann von Mangoldt formula. A table in the book supports it to a few per cent for \(n\le49\), but the local model is a heuristic, outside the scaling of Kuijlaars and Van Assche (1999). Also decide between the rules \(n(L_n)=n\) and \(n(L_n')=n-\frac12\), which the data do not separate, and explain the scatter of the ratios, about six per cent, through the individual gaps between the zeros.
Source: ch/ch22.tex, label prob:wigfree:jacobi.




Problem 12.4, page 525 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be Riemann’s xi function, \(\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)\) the Xi function, and \(H_t\) the de Bruijn Newman heat flow in the normalisation of Rodgers and Tao, which the book uses: \(8H_t(2\theta)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(v)e^{tv^2/4}\cos(\theta v)\,dv\), where \(\Phi(v)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5v/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})\), so that \(8H_0(2\theta)=\Xi(\theta)\). Write \(\pm\theta_j(t)\) for the zeros of \(\theta\mapsto H_t(2\theta)\), so that \(\theta_j(0)=\gamma_j\), where \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_j\) are the nontrivial zeros of \(\zeta\), numbered by height. For every \(t<0\) the function \(H_t\) has nonreal zeros, by the theorem of Rodgers and Tao, and as \(t\) decreases from \(0\) pairs of consecutive real zeros \(\theta_k(t),\theta_{k+1}(t)\), which start at \((\gamma_k,\gamma_{k+1})\), collide and leave the real axis. Let \(\mathcal H_N(t)=[m_{i+j}(t)]_{i,j<N}\) be the Hankel matrix of order \(N\) of the moments \(m_n(t)=\sum_j\theta_j(t)^{-2n-2}\) (at \(t=0\) these are \(m_n(0)=\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2n-2}\)). Under the Riemann Hypothesis \(\mathcal H_N(0)\) is positive definite. Let \(n_{\rm fail}(t)\) be the least \(N\) for which \(\mathcal H_N(t)\) is not positive definite and \(t^*_N=\sup\{t<0:n_{\rm fail}(t)\le N\}\), the time, going back from \(t=0\), at which the Hankel test of order \(N\) first fails. Under the Riemann Hypothesis every \(t^*_N\) is negative, \(t^*_N\le t^*_{N+1}\) and \(t^*_N\to0\). The book computes \(t^*_N\) for \(N\le50\) and explains the steps of the staircase by collisions. The rule suggested in an unpublished note of N. G. Polson, that the collision of \((\gamma_k,\gamma_{k+1})\) is registered from order about \(2k+2\) on, holds for \(N=30\) and \(40\) and fails at \(N=50\): it gives the collision of \((\gamma_{24},\gamma_{25})\) at \(t=-1.144\), while the matrix of order \(50\) registers \((\gamma_{27},\gamma_{28})\), for which \(2k+2=56\), at \(t=-1.0325\), before \((\gamma_{24},\gamma_{25})\) has collided. Open problem: find the rule that gives the order at which a pair is registered, as a function of the index \(k\) of the pair and of its distance from the axis, and follow the staircase of \(t^*_N\) to orders of a few hundred, towards the limit \(0\) that it has under the Riemann Hypothesis.
Source: ch/ch22.tex, label prob:wigfree:window.




Problem 12.5, page 525 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be Riemann’s xi function, \(\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)\) the Xi function, and \(H_t\) the de Bruijn Newman heat flow in the normalisation of Rodgers and Tao, which the book uses: \(8H_t(2\theta)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(v)e^{tv^2/4}\cos(\theta v)\,dv\), where \(\Phi(v)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9v/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5v/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2v})\), so that \(8H_0(2\theta)=\Xi(\theta)\); as \(t\) decreases below \(0\), pairs of adjacent real zeros of \(H_t\) collide and leave the real axis, and \(H_t\) has nonreal zeros for every \(t<0\) by the theorem of Rodgers and Tao. The book brackets the collision times of such pairs by quantities computed along the flow and through the nonreal zeros of \(H_t\), and checks the hypotheses of the brackets on a grid of times for the \(58\) collisions of a census computed in the book. Open problem: find a priori control of the nonreal zeros of \(H_t\) for \(t<0\), of how far they travel and how close to a gap between real zeros they come, which would make the brackets statements about \(H_t\) computed from \(H_0\) alone.
Source: ch/ch22.tex, label prob:wigfree:collide.




Problem 12.6, page 525 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be Riemann’s xi function, \(\gamma_k\) the ordinates of its zeros \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_k\) in the upper half plane, \(a_k=\gamma_k^2\) and \(W(t)=\sum_ke^{-ta_k}\) the heat trace of the zeros. Let \(T\) be the clock, the positive random variable with Laplace transform \(1/G(u)\), \(G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac12)\), which has Lévy measure \(W(x)\,dx/x\). The Upsilon transform sends an infinitely divisible law \(\mu\) with Lévy process \((X_t)\), \(X_1\sim\mu\), to the law of \(\int_0^1\log(1/t)\,dX_t\), and the class BO is the class of infinitely divisible laws on \([0,\infty)\) whose Lévy measure has a completely monotone density. The book proves the derivative signs \((-1)^kW^{(k)}>0\) on ranges that grow with the height to which the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is verified, and complete monotonicity of \(W\) on \((0,\infty)\) is RH. Open problem: find a mechanism that extends these ranges with no new information on the zeros, for instance a functional equation for the law of \(T\) under the Upsilon transform, as suggested in an unpublished note of N. G. Polson. The book restricts the form such an equation can take: with no hypothesis \(T\) is not the Upsilon image of a law in BO, and under RH \(T\) is the Upsilon image of the law \(\mu_0\), the self decomposable law with no drift and Lévy measure \(N(x^{-1/2})\,dx/x\), where \(N(T)\) is the number of ordinates \(\gamma_k\le T\), which is neither a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) nor in BO.
Source: ch/ch22.tex, label prob:wigfree:ladder.

title: Results by chapter Computing the Riemann Hypothesis
text:
Theorem 13.1.4, page 531 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A real random variable \(X\) is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function \(L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}\), which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; equivalently every zero of the characteristic function \(\varphi_X(\theta)=L_X(i\theta)\) is real. By Newman’s theorem such an \(X\) has the Hadamard form \(L_X(s)=e^{bs^2}\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)\) with \(b\ge0\), \(c_k>0\) and \(\sum_kc_k^{-2}<\infty\), each \(c_k\) repeated according to the multiplicity of the zero \(ic_k\). Let \(X\) be ferromagnetic with this form, let \(e_k\) be independent standard exponential variables and \(Z\) a standard normal variable independent of them, and put \(T_X=b+\sum_ke_k/c_k^2\) and \(Y_X=Z\sqrt{2T_X}\); the series converges almost surely and in mean. Then (i) \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_X}=1/L_X(\sqrt{u})\) for \(u\ge0\), and \(T_X\) is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC, a law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(\exp\{-b\lambda-\int\log(1+\lambda/t)\,\mu(dt)\}\) for a drift \(b\ge0\) and a positive Thorin measure \(\mu\)) with drift \(b\) and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{c_k^2}\), one unit atom for each pair of zeros \(\pm ic_k\). (ii) \(\mathbb{E}e^{i\theta Y_X}=1/L_X(\theta)\) for real \(\theta\), so that \(\varphi_{Y_X}(\theta)\,\varphi_X(i\theta)=1\) and \((\varphi_X,\varphi_{Y_X})\) is a van Dantzig pair, and \(Y_X\overset{d}{=}\sqrt{2b}\,Z+\sum_kL_k/c_k\) with independent standard Laplace variables \(L_k\), whose characteristic function is \(1/(1+\theta^2)\). (iii) The moment generating function of \(Y_X\) is \(1/\varphi_X(t)\) for \(|t|<c_1=\min_kc_k\) and infinite for \(|t|\ge c_1\), unless \(X\) is Gaussian. (iv) Unless \(X\) is degenerate, \(Y_X\) has a Pólya frequency density of infinite order. (v) \(\kappa_m(T_X)=(-1)^{m+1}m!\,\kappa_{2m}(X)/(2m)!\) for \(m\ge1\), where \(\kappa_j\) denotes the \(j\)th cumulant; in particular \(\mathbb{E}T_X=\frac12\operatorname{Var}X\) and \(\operatorname{Var}T_X=-\kappa_4(X)/12\).
Source: ch/fm1.tex, label fm:thm:dual.




Theorem 13.1.5, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A real random variable \(X\) is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function \(L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}\), which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; Gaussian laws are allowed. Let \(X_n\) be ferromagnetic and suppose that \(X_n\to X\) in law. Then \(X\) is ferromagnetic, \(\operatorname{Var}X_n\to\operatorname{Var}X\), and \(L_{X_n}\to L_X\) locally uniformly on \(\mathbb{C}\).
Source: ch/fm1.tex, label fm:thm:closed.




Corollary 13.1.8, page 534 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A real random variable \(X\) is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function \(\mathbb{E}e^{zX}\), which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. The Pólya law is the law of the symmetric random variable \(X\) with density \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\); its moment generating function is \(\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)\). The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Pólya law is a limit in law of ferromagnetic laws.
Source: ch/fm1.tex, label fm:cor:limit.




Theorem 13.2.1, page 535 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: counterexample, proved.
Statement. A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let \(U\) be uniform on \([-1,1]\), so that \(\mathbb{E}e^{sU}=\sinh s/s\). For every \(0<q<1\) the mixture \((1-q)\,\mathrm{Unif}[-1,1]+q\,\delta_0\) of the uniform law on \([-1,1]\) with weight \(1-q\) and the point mass at \(0\) with weight \(q\) is symmetric and unimodal but not ferromagnetic: its moment generating function \((1-q)\sinh s/s+q\) has no real zero, only finitely many zeros on the imaginary axis, and infinitely many zeros in all, so that all but finitely many of its zeros are off the imaginary axis. Consequently, for every \(0<q<1\) and every small enough \(a>0\), the mixture of the uniform laws on \([-1,1]\) and on \([-a,a]\) with weights \(1-q\) and \(q\) is not ferromagnetic. Both components of these mixtures are ferromagnetic, so the class of ferromagnetic laws is not closed under mixtures.
Source: ch/fm2.tex, label fm:thm:atom.




Proposition 13.2.3, page 536 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f_2(x)=(1-|x|)_+\) be the triangular density on \([-1,1]\), so that its characteristic function is \(4\sin^2(\theta/2)/\theta^2\), and call \(X\) a scale mixture of \(f_2\) for a probability law \(\nu\) on \((0,\infty)\) if \(X=rY\) with \(r\sim\nu\) independent of \(Y\sim f_2\). Let \(\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})\) be the Pólya kernel, so that \(\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du\) for Riemann’s completed zeta function \(\xi\). (i) If \(X\) is a scale mixture of \(f_2\) for \(\nu\), then \(\mathbb{E}e^{i\theta X}\ge0\) for real \(\theta\), and for \(\theta\ne0\) it vanishes exactly when \(\nu\) is carried by \(\{2\pi j/|\theta|:j\ge1\}\); in particular if \(\nu\) has a nonzero absolutely continuous part, \(\mathbb{E}e^{i\theta X}\) has no real zeros. (ii) The Pólya law, with density proportional to \(\Phi\), is not a scale mixture of \(f_2\) for any probability law: with \(y_n=\pi n^2e^{2u}\) and \(R(y)=32y^4-224y^3+330y^2-75y\), \(\Phi''(u)=\frac12e^{u/2}\sum_{n\ge1}R(y_n)e^{-y_n}\), \(\Phi''(0)<0\), and \(\Phi''(u)>0\) for \(u\ge\frac12\log(7/\pi)\), whereas a mixture of the convex functions \((1-x/r)_+\) is convex on \((0,\infty)\). (iii) \(\Phi\) has exactly one positive inflection point \(u^*\), with \(\Phi''<0\) on \([0,u^*)\), \(\Phi''>0\) on \((u^*,\infty)\) and \(\Phi'''(u^*)>0\); certified in ball arithmetic, \(u^*=0.23726528718742524911\). The proof of (ii) and (iii) uses three inequalities certified in ball arithmetic.
Source: ch/fm2.tex, label fm:prop:triangle.




Theorem 13.2.4, page 537 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; equivalently every zero of its characteristic function \(\varphi_X\) is real. Let \(p\) be a symmetric probability density on \([-1,1]\) that is absolutely continuous and nonincreasing on \([0,1]\), with \(p(1)=0\), let \([-c,c]\) with \(0<c\le1\) be its support, and let \(X\) have density \(p\). (i) If \(p\) is concave on \([0,1]\), then \(X\) is ferromagnetic. (ii) If \(p\) is convex on \([0,1]\) and not linear on \([0,c]\), then \(X\) is not ferromagnetic; moreover \(\varphi_X\ge0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), and its real zeros, if any, are double and lie in a lattice \((2\pi/s_0)\mathbb{Z}\) with \(0<s_0<c\).
Source: ch/fm2.tex, label fm:thm:shoulder.




Corollary 13.2.5, page 538 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. (i) The law with density proportional to \(1-|x|^b\) on \([-1,1]\), \(b>0\), is ferromagnetic if and only if \(b\ge1\). In Khinchine’s form, \(UR\) with \(U\) uniform on \([-1,1]\) and \(R\) independent with the Beta\((a,1)\) law (density \(ar^{a-1}\) on \([0,1]\)) is ferromagnetic if and only if \(a\ge2\). (ii) For an integer \(k\ge1\) the symmetric \(k\) monotone kernel \(f_k(x)=\frac k2(1-|x|)_+^{k-1}\) (the uniform density for \(k=1\) and the triangle density for \(k=2\)) is ferromagnetic if and only if \(k\le2\). (iii) The laws with density proportional to \((1-x^2)^m\) on \([-1,1]\) with \(0<m\le1\), which include the semicircle law, are ferromagnetic. (iv) The product \(U_1U_2\) of two independent uniform variables on \([-1,1]\), with density \(\frac12\log(1/|x|)\) on \([-1,1]\), is not ferromagnetic.
Source: ch/fm2.tex, label fm:cor:shoulder.




Theorem 13.2.6, page 539 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A real random variable is called ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function, which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Every symmetric probability density on \([-1,1]\) that is nondecreasing in \(|x|\) is ferromagnetic. Equivalently, every mixture of the uniform laws on the shells \(\{a\le|x|\le1\}\), \(0\le a<1\), is ferromagnetic.
Source: ch/fm2.tex, label fm:thm:ushaped.




Proposition 13.3.1, page 541 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(X\) be a ferromagnetic random variable (a characteristic function \(\varphi_X\) with only real zeros) with \(b=0\) in its Hadamard product and infinitely many simple zeros \(\pm ic_k\), \(0<c_1<c_2<\cdots\), so that \(L_X(s)=\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)\), and let \(T_X=\sum_ke_k/c_k^2\) be its clock, with \(e_k\) independent standard exponential variables. Put \(\mathcal D_X(w)=\Gamma(w)\mathbb{E}T_X^{-w}=\int_0^\infty u^{w-1}(1/L_X(\sqrt u)-1)\,du\) for \(-1<\operatorname{Re}w<0\), and \(A_k=-2/(c_k\varphi_X'(c_k))\), \(B_k=2(c_k\varphi_X''(c_k)-\varphi_X'(c_k))/(c_k^2\varphi_X'(c_k)^3)\). (i) Near \(u=-c_k^2\), \(1/L_X(\sqrt u)=A_k(1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}+O(1)\) and \(1/L_X(\sqrt u)^2=A_k^2(1+u/c_k^2)^{-2}+B_k(1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}+O(1)\). (ii) If \(1/L_X(\sqrt u)=1+\sum_kA_k((1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}-1)\) for \(u\ge0\) and \(\sum_k|A_k|c_k^{2\sigma}<\infty\) for some \(\sigma\in(-1,0)\), then \(\mathcal D_X(w)=\frac{\pi}{\sin\pi w}\sum_kA_kc_k^{2w}\) for \(-1<\operatorname{Re}w\le\sigma\). (iii) If \(1/L_X(\sqrt u)^2=1+\sum_k[A_k^2((1+u/c_k^2)^{-2}-1)+B_k((1+u/c_k^2)^{-1}-1)]\) for \(u\ge0\) and \(\sum_k(A_k^2+|B_k|)c_k^{2\sigma}<\infty\) for some \(\sigma\in(-1,0)\), then for an independent copy \(X'\) of \(X\), \(\mathcal D_{X+X'}(w)=\frac{\pi}{\sin\pi w}\sum_k[(1-w)A_k^2+B_k]c_k^{2w}\) for \(-1<\operatorname{Re}w\le\sigma\). The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.
Source: ch/fm2m.tex, label fm:prop:residue.




Proposition 13.3.2, page 542 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(U_1,\dots,U_k\) be independent random variables uniform on \([-1,1]\), \(X_k=\pi(U_1+\dots+U_k)\), and \(\mathcal D_{X_k}(w)=\Gamma(w)\mathbb{E}T^{-w}\) the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock \(T\) of \(X_k\) (the sum of \(e_j/c_j^2\) over the zeros \(\pm c_j\) of the characteristic function, \(e_j\) independent standard exponential variables). For \(\operatorname{Re}w>0\), \(\mathcal D_{X_k}(w)=2(2\pi)^{-2w}\Gamma(2w+k)\sum_{m\ge0}\binom{m+k-1}{k-1}(m+\frac k2)^{-2w-k}\). For \(k=2r\) the series is \(\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}a_{r,i}\zeta(2w+1+2i)\), where \(a_{r,i}\) is the coefficient of \(j^{2r-1-2i}\) in \(j\prod_{l=1}^{r-1}(j^2-l^2)/(2r-1)!\), and for \(k=2r+1\) it is \(\sum_{i=0}^rb_{r,i}(2^{2w+1+2i}-1)\zeta(2w+1+2i)\), where \(b_{r,i}\) is the coefficient of \(h^{2r-2i}\) in \(\prod_{l=1}^r(h^2-(l-\frac12)^2)/(2r)!\). The first and the last of these coefficients are not \(0\), so for \(k\ge3\) the series has at least two terms. In particular \(\mathcal D_{X_1}(w)=4\pi^{-2w}(1-2^{-2w-1})\Gamma(2w+1)\zeta(2w+1)\), \(\mathcal D_{X_4}(w)=\frac13(2\pi)^{-2w}\Gamma(2w+4)[\zeta(2w+1)-\zeta(2w+3)]\) and \(\mathcal D_{X_6}(w)=\frac1{60}(2\pi)^{-2w}\Gamma(2w+6)[\zeta(2w+1)-5\zeta(2w+3)+4\zeta(2w+5)]\). The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Statement. Let \(X\) have the density \((1+\cos t)/2\pi\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), which is \(C^1\) and not \(C^2\) at \(\pm\pi\), let \(X'\) be an independent copy, and let \(\mathcal D_Y(w)\) be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock of \(Y\) (the clock being the sum of \(e_k/c_k^2\) over the zeros \(\pm c_k\) of the characteristic function of \(Y\), \(e_k\) independent standard exponential variables), \(U,U'\) independent uniform on \([-1,1]\). Result 13.3, page 544 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: computed.
Statement. For \(\varepsilon\ge0\) let \(X_\varepsilon\) have the density \((1+\varepsilon t^2)/(2\pi+\frac23\pi^3\varepsilon)\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), which is nondecreasing in \(|t|\), so that \(X_\varepsilon\) and the sum \(X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'\) with an independent copy are ferromagnetic, and let \(\mathcal D_{X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'}\) be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock of the pair. At \(\varepsilon=0\) the zeros \(w_k(0)=\frac{\rho_k-1}2\) of \(\mathcal D_{\pi U+\pi U'}\) (\(U,U'\) independent uniform on \([-1,1]\), \(\rho_k\) the zeros of \(\zeta\) on the critical line) move, where \(\rho_k\) is simple, with \(\frac{dw_k}{d\varepsilon}(0)=-\dot{\mathcal D}(w_k(0))/\mathcal D'_{\pi U+\pi U'}(w_k(0))\) by the implicit function theorem, \(\dot{\mathcal D}\) being the derivative of \(\mathcal D_{X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'}\) in \(\varepsilon\) at \(\varepsilon=0\). The computed values are \(\frac{dw_1}{d\varepsilon}(0)=5.89145-13.09321i\) and \(\frac{dw_2}{d\varepsilon}(0)=1.56442-16.25014i\), with real parts different from \(0\) and from each other (computed by quadrature with three rules that agree). So for small \(\varepsilon>0\) the first two zeros leave the line \(\operatorname{Re}w=-\frac14\) at different rates, and the nonreal zeros of \(\mathcal D_{X_\varepsilon+X_\varepsilon'}\) do not lie on one vertical line although every \(X_\varepsilon\) is ferromagnetic. By this computation no theorem whose hypotheses hold for all symmetric densities on an interval that are nondecreasing in \(|t|\) can put the zeros of the Mellin transform of the pair on one line.

Theorem 13.4.1, page 547 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(X\) be a symmetric random variable with \(\mathbb{E}e^{sX}<\infty\) for every real \(s\) and \(\log\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=o(s^2)\) as \(s\to\infty\), and suppose that \(X\overset{d}{=}D+R\) with \(D\) and \(R\) independent. Then \(\log\mathbb{E}e^{sD}=o(s^2)\) as \(|s|\to\infty\). In particular, if \(D\) is ferromagnetic (symmetric, with \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0D^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\) and a moment generating function vanishing only on the imaginary axis) and not \(0\), then in its Hadamard form \(\mathbb{E}e^{sD}=e^{bs^2}\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)\) the Gaussian factor has \(b=0\), and the characteristic function of \(D\) has infinitely many zeros. The Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density \(\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\) and moment generating function \(\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\), satisfies the hypothesis with no assumption on the zeros of \(\zeta\). So it has no Gaussian component (it is not the sum of an independent normal variable of positive variance and another variable), and it is not a finite or convergent infinite sum of independent ferromagnetic variables of which one is not \(0\) and has a characteristic function with finitely many zeros.
Source: ch/fm3.tex, label fm:thm:nosqrt.




Proposition 13.5.2, page 549 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on The Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than 7/8 (announced by OpenAI in October 2026, not refereed, and not proved in the book).
Statement. Let \(X\) be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\). For \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N>0\) and \(\mu\ge0\) put \(m(t)=e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)\) and \(c(m)=2\mu+\sum_{k\le N}\lambda_k^2\), so that \(m(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{tY}\) for \(Y=\sqrt{2\mu}\,Z+\sum_k\lambda_k\varepsilon_k\) with \(Z\) standard normal and \(\varepsilon_k\) independent fair random signs, and \(c(m)=\operatorname{Var}Y\); the same applies with \(N=\infty\) when \(\sum_k\lambda_k^2<\infty\). A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Assume that \(\zeta\) has no zero with real part greater than \(\frac78\). Then the zeros of \(z\mapsto\int\Phi(t)m(t)e^{izt}\,dt\) lie in the strip \(|\operatorname{Im}z|\le(\max(\frac9{64}-c(m),0))^{1/2}\). In particular the law with density proportional to \(m\,p\) is ferromagnetic whenever \(\operatorname{Var}Y\ge\frac9{64}\); for example \(\cosh(at)\,p(t)\) is ferromagnetic for \(a\ge\frac38\) and \(\frac{\sinh(ct)}{ct}\,p(t)\) for \(c\ge\frac{3\sqrt3}8\). With no hypothesis on the zeros the same statements hold with \(\frac14\) in place of \(\frac9{64}\), by theorems of de Bruijn (1950), so that \(\cosh(at)\,p(t)\) is ferromagnetic for \(a\ge\frac12\).

Theorem 13.5.4, page 551 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A symmetric real random variable \(X\) is called ferromagnetic if \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\) and its moment generating function \(L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}\), which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis; by Newman’s theorem \(L_X(s)=e^{bs^2}\prod_k(1+s^2/c_k^2)\) with \(b\ge0\) and \(c_k>0\). Let \(K_\nu(a)=\int_0^\infty e^{-a\cosh u}\cosh(\nu u)\,du\) be the Macdonald function, for \(a>0\) and complex order \(\nu\). Let \(a,\ell>0\), \(\mu\ge0\) and \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N\ge0\), let \(Z\) be standard normal and \(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N\) independent signs \(\pm1\) with probability \(\frac12\) each, independent of \(Z\), let \(Y=\sqrt{2\mu}\,Z+\sum_{k\le N}\lambda_k\varepsilon_k\), so that \(m(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{tY}=e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)\), and let \(q\) be the probability density on \(\mathbb{R}\) proportional to \(m(t)e^{-a\cosh\ell t}\). Then: (i) \(q\) is ferromagnetic, it has Gaussian moments of all orders, and its Gaussian component is zero (\(b=0\)). (ii) \(\int_{\mathbb{R}}m(t)e^{-a\cosh\ell t}\,dt=\frac2\ell\,\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)\) and the moment generating function of \(q\) is \(L_q(s)=\mathbb{E}K_{(s+Y)/\ell}(a)/\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)\) for complex \(s\); for \(\mu=0\) the expectations are averages over the \(2^N\) values of \(Y\). (iii) The clock \(T_q\) of \(q\) is the generalised gamma convolution, with drift \(b=0\) and a unit Thorin atom at the square of each positive zero of the characteristic function of \(q\), whose Laplace transform is \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_q}=1/L_q(\sqrt u)\); here \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uT_q}=\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)/\mathbb{E}K_{(\sqrt u+Y)/\ell}(a)\) for \(u\ge0\). For \(m\equiv1\), \(T_q=\ell^{-2}\sum_je_j/\nu_j(a)^2\) with \(e_j\) independent standard exponential variables and \(0<\nu_1(a)\le\nu_2(a)\le\cdots\) the zeros of \(\nu\mapsto K_{i\nu}(a)\) on \((0,\infty)\) listed with multiplicity.

Proposition 13.5.5, page 552 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(a,\ell>0\), \(\mu\ge0\), \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N\ge0\), \(Z\) standard normal, \(\varepsilon_k\) independent signs, \(Y=\sqrt{2\mu}\,Z+\sum_{k\le N}\lambda_k\varepsilon_k\), \(m(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{tY}\) and \(q\) the probability density proportional to \(m(t)e^{-a\cosh\ell t}\). Let \(K_v(a)=\int_0^\infty e^{-a\cosh u}\cosh(vu)\,du\), and for real \(v\) let \(G_v\) have the generalised inverse Gaussian density \(g^{v-1}e^{-\frac a2(g+1/g)}/(2K_v(a))\) on \((0,\infty)\). Let \(V\) be a random index with \(\mathbb{E}h(V)=\mathbb{E}[h(Y/\ell)K_{Y/\ell}(a)]/\mathbb{E}K_{Y/\ell}(a)\) and, given \(V\), let \(G_V\) have the density of index \(V\). Then \(q\) is the law of \(\ell^{-1}\log G_V\), and also the law of \(\varepsilon\,\ell^{-1}\log G_{|V|}\), with \(\varepsilon\) a sign independent of \(V\) and \(G_{|V|}\). For \(\mu=0\), \(V\) takes the values \(\ell^{-1}\sum_k\eta_k\lambda_k\), \(\eta\in\{\pm1\}^N\), with probabilities proportional to \(K_{\ell^{-1}\sum_k\eta_k\lambda_k}(a)\).

Proposition 13.5.8, page 554 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\) be the Pólya density, where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\), a function with a natural boundary on the lines \(\operatorname{Im}t=\pm\pi/4\). Let \(a_n\to a\) and \(\ell_n\to\ell\) with \(a,\ell>0\), and let \(q_n\) be the probability density proportional to \(m_n(t)e^{-a_n\cosh\ell_nt}\), where \(m_n(t)=\psi_n(it)\) for an even entire function \(\psi_n\) of the Laguerre Pólya class with \(\psi_n(0)>0\), that is \(\psi_n(z)=\psi_n(0)e^{-\alpha_nz^2}\prod_j(1-z^2/z_{n,j}^2)\) with \(\alpha_n\ge0\), \(z_{n,j}>0\) and \(\sum_jz_{n,j}^{-2}<\infty\). Then \(q_n\) does not converge in law to \(p\). The multipliers \(e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)\) with \(\mu,\lambda_k\ge0\) are of this form, and so are \(e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\ge1}\cosh(\lambda_kt)\) with \(\sum_k\lambda_k^2<\infty\). Consequently a sequence of laws of Theorem fm:thm:bessel (multipliers \(e^{\mu t^2}\prod_{k\le N}\cosh(\lambda_kt)\)), which are ferromagnetic, converging in law to \(p\) would prove RH, by the closure of ferromagnetic laws under convergence in law, and its kernel parameters \((a_n,\ell_n)\) would have no limit point in \((0,\infty)^2\); whether such a sequence exists is not known.

Corollary 13.5.9, page 555 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. A symmetric real random variable \(X\) is called ferromagnetic if \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\) and its moment generating function \(L_X(z)=\mathbb{E}e^{zX}\), which is then entire, vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let \(q_1,\dots,q_N\) be probability densities on \(\mathbb{R}\), each proportional to \(m_i(t)e^{-a_i\cosh\ell_it}\) with \(a_i,\ell_i>0\) and \(m_i(t)=e^{\mu_it^2}\prod_{k\le N_i}\cosh(\lambda_{ik}t)\) with \(\mu_i,\lambda_{ik}\ge0\) (the laws of the Bessel kernel theorem, which are ferromagnetic with Gaussian moments of all orders). Let \(J=(J_{ij})\) be a symmetric matrix with \(J_{ij}\ge0\) and \(J_{ii}=0\), and let \((X_1,\dots,X_N)\) have density on \(\mathbb{R}^N\) proportional to \(\exp\big(\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}t_it_j\big)\prod_iq_i(t_i)\). Then \(M=\sum_ic_iX_i\) is ferromagnetic for all \(c_1,\dots,c_N\ge0\), not all \(0\).

Proposition 13.5.10, page 556 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(q_1,q_2\) be laws of the Bessel kernel theorem (densities proportional to \(m_i(t)e^{-a_i\cosh\ell_it}\) with \(a_i,\ell_i>0\) and \(m_i(t)=e^{\mu_it^2}\prod_{k\le N_i}\cosh(\lambda_{ik}t)\), \(\mu_i,\lambda_{ik}\ge0\)), with characteristic functions \(\varphi_1,\varphi_2\). For \(J>0\) let \((X_1,X_2)\) have density proportional to \(e^{Jt_1t_2}q_1(t_1)q_2(t_2)\), so that the characteristic function of \(X_1+X_2\) is proportional to \(Z_J(\theta)=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{(-J)^n}{n!}\varphi_1^{(n)}(\theta)\varphi_2^{(n)}(\theta)\). As \(J\downarrow0\): (i) if \(\alpha\) is a simple zero of \(\varphi_1\) and \(\varphi_2(\alpha)\ne0\), then \(Z_J\) has a zero \(\alpha+J\varphi_2'(\alpha)/\varphi_2(\alpha)+O(J^2)\). (ii) If \(\alpha\) is a simple zero of both \(\varphi_1\) and \(\varphi_2\), then \(Z_J\) has the two real zeros \(\alpha\pm\sqrt J+\frac J4\big(\frac{\varphi_1''}{\varphi_1'}+\frac{\varphi_2''}{\varphi_2'}\big)(\alpha)+O(J^{3/2})\), at distance \(2\sqrt J+O(J^{3/2})\).

Result 13.5.3, page 556 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: computed.
Statement. Let \(q\) be the law with characteristic function \(\varphi_q(\theta)=K_{i\theta/4}(\pi)/K_0(\pi)\) (\(K_\nu\) the modified Bessel function of the second kind), the ferromagnetic law with density proportional to \(e^{-\pi\cosh4t}\) on \(\mathbb{R}\); for the sum of two independent copies the number of zeros of the characteristic function in \((0,\theta]\) has the main terms of the Riemann von Mangoldt formula. Let \(\mathcal D\) be the Mellin transform of the Laplace transform of the clock (the sum of \(e_k/c_k^2\) over the zeros \(\pm c_k\) of the characteristic function, \(e_k\) independent standard exponential variables). The transform of the pair of two copies, and that of a single copy, have no zero in the box \(-0.95<\operatorname{Re}w<-0.05\), \(\frac12<\operatorname{Im}w<11\), in which the transform of the uniform pair \(\pi U+\pi U'\) has the two zeros \(\frac{\rho_1-1}2\) and \(\frac{\rho_2-1}2\), where \(\rho_k=\frac12+i\gamma_k\) are the first two zeros of \(\zeta\) on the critical line (computed: the argument principle on the boundaries of the boxes \(\frac12<\operatorname{Im}w<\frac{17}2\) and \(\frac{17}2<\operatorname{Im}w<11\), sampled, not a ball proof, with the uniform pair computed by the same quadrature as a control, which gives winding \(1\) in each box). The result follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Proposition 13.5.11, page 557 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For \(n\ge1\) let \(r_n(t)=e^{|t|/2}\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2|t|})\), and consider the laws on \(\mathbb{R}\) with densities proportional to \(r_n\) and to \(\sum_{m\ge1}r_m\) (the components of the theta series in Riemann’s formula for the xi function and their mixture). Each of these laws is symmetric, has finite moments of all orders (indeed \(\mathbb{E}e^{b|X|}<\infty\) for every \(b\ge0\), so the characteristic function is entire of order at most one), and has a characteristic function positive on \(\mathbb{R}\), and none of them is ferromagnetic, that is, none has a characteristic function with only real zeros: each characteristic function has infinitely many zeros and none of them is real. For \(n=1\) the characteristic function has \(5\) zeros in the box \(0\le\operatorname{Re}\theta\le40\), \(0\le\operatorname{Im}\theta\le30\), the two of least modulus being \(13.0885+10.8707i\) and \(20.1987+15.0786i\) (computed by the argument principle). The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Theorem 13.5.12, page 558 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(X\) be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\), with characteristic function \(\varphi_X\). Let \(\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots\) be the positive ordinates of the zeros \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_k\) of \(\zeta\) on the critical line, with multiplicity, and put \(s_K=\sum_{k\le K}\gamma_k^{-2}\), \(\beta_K=\frac12\operatorname{Var}X - s_K\) and \(\varphi_K(\theta)=e^{-\beta_K\theta^2}\prod_{k\le K}(1-\theta^2/\gamma_k^2)\). Let \(M_1,M_2,\dots\) be independent symmetric Maxwell variables (density \(x^2e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\), characteristic function \((1-\theta^2)e^{-\theta^2/2}\), variance \(3\)), each ferromagnetic, and let \(Z\) be a standard normal variable independent of them. A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. (i) With no hypothesis, \(\beta_K>0\) for every \(K\). If \(3s_K\le\operatorname{Var}X\), then \(\varphi_K\) is the characteristic function of \(X_K=(\operatorname{Var}X-3s_K)^{1/2}Z+\sum_{k\le K}M_k/\gamma_k\), whose law \(f_K\) is ferromagnetic, with \(\operatorname{Var}X_K=\operatorname{Var}X\) and \(\kappa_4(X_K)=-12\sum_{k\le K}\gamma_k^{-4}\). The condition \(3s_K\le\operatorname{Var}X\) holds for \(K\le16\) and fails for \(K=17\), a certified computation in ball arithmetic (\(3s_{16}=0.0456803\), \(\operatorname{Var}X=0.0462100\), \(3s_{17}=0.0463006\)). (ii) For every \(K\), if the inverse Fourier transform \(f_K\) of \(\varphi_K\) is nonnegative, then \(f_K\) is a ferromagnetic probability density. (iii) The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if \(\varphi_K\to\varphi_X\) pointwise as \(K\to\infty\). Under the Riemann Hypothesis, \(f_K\) converges in law to the Pólya law along every sequence of \(K\) for which \(f_K\ge0\).
Source: ch/fm4.tex, label fm:thm:zc.




Theorem 13.5.14, page 561 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(X\) be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\), and let \(Z\) be a standard normal variable independent of \(X\). Let \(\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots\) be the positive ordinates of the zeros \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_k\) of \(\zeta\) on the critical line, with multiplicity, let \(M_1,M_2,\dots\) be independent symmetric Maxwell variables with density \(x^2e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\), and put \(\mathcal M=\sum_kM_k/\gamma_k\), a series that converges almost surely because its terms are independent and centred with summable variances \(3\gamma_k^{-2}\). Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if \(X+\big(\tfrac12\operatorname{Var}X\big)^{1/2}Z\overset{d}{=}\mathcal M\).
Source: ch/fm4.tex, label fm:thm:maxwell.




Proposition 13.5.15, page 561 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(X\) be the Pólya variable, the symmetric random variable with density \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) and \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\). A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0Y^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let \(\delta\) be the infimum of the total variation distances \(\sup_A|P(X\in A)-P(Y\in A)|\) from \(X\) to ferromagnetic variables \(Y\); when \(Y\) has a density \(f\) the distance is \(\operatorname{TV}(f,p)=\frac12\int|f - p|\). Let \(\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots\) be the positive ordinates of the zeros \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_k\) of \(\zeta\) on the critical line, with multiplicity, put \(s_K=\sum_{k\le K}\gamma_k^{-2}\) and \(\beta_K=\frac12\operatorname{Var}X - s_K\), and let \(f_K\) be the function with Fourier transform \(\varphi_K(\theta)=e^{-\beta_K\theta^2}\prod_{k\le K}(1-\theta^2/\gamma_k^2)\). With no hypothesis on the zeros: \(f_{16}\) is a ferromagnetic probability density, an explicit sum of a normal variable and Maxwell variables, and \(\operatorname{TV}(f_{16},p)<1.266\times10^{-4}\), so that \(\delta<1.266\times10^{-4}\); and \(f_{150}\) is a ferromagnetic probability density by a computer assisted proof in ball arithmetic (the polynomial in the Hermite basis that multiplies the Gaussian is positive on the real line) with \(\operatorname{TV}(f_{150},p)<1.932\times10^{-6}\), so that \(\delta<1.932\times10^{-6}\); and the law \(q\) with density proportional to \(\cosh(\lambda t)\,e^{-a\cosh\ell t}\), \(\lambda=2.146184\), \(a=5.483952\), \(\ell=2.062866\), is ferromagnetic (by Theorem fm:thm:bessel: the law proportional to \(e^{-a\cosh\ell t}\) is ferromagnetic since \(z\mapsto K_{iz}(a)\) has only real zeros (P'olya), and the tilt by \(\cosh(\lambda t)\) keeps it ferromagnetic; \(L_q(s)=\frac{K_{(s+\lambda)/\ell}(a)+K_{(s-\lambda)/\ell}(a)}{2K_{\lambda/\ell}(a)}\)) and \(\operatorname{TV}(q,p)<6.024\times10^{-6}\), so that \(\delta<6.024\times10^{-6}\). The distances are enclosed in ball arithmetic, with explicit bounds for the discretisation and the tails. The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if \(\delta=0\).
Source: ch/fm4.tex, label fm:prop:tvcert.




Theorem 13.5.16, page 562 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})\) and \(p=\Phi/\xi(\frac12)\) the Pólya density, and \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\frac12\Phi(2u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\), the kernel of the de Bruijn Newman flow, with \(H_0(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)\). A law is ferromagnetic if it is symmetric, has \(\mathbb{E}e^{b_0X^2}<\infty\) for some \(b_0>0\), and its moment generating function vanishes only on the imaginary axis. Let \(\mu>0\) and \(H^{(\mu)}(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{-\mu u}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du\). With \(C\) a standard Cauchy variable, \(H^{(\mu)}(z)=\mathbb{E}\,H_0(z+\mu C)\) and \(z^2H^{(\mu)}(z)\to\mu\,\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(0)=0.4467\,\mu\) as \(z\to\infty\) along the reals.
