Proposition 15.5.7, page 626 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\) and \(\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du\), the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann’s xi function, and for real \(\sigma,\theta\) with \(\xi_t(\sigma+i\theta)\ne0\) put \(v_t(\sigma,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\xi_t'(\sigma+i\theta)/\xi_t(\sigma+i\theta)\bigr)\) (when the shifted clock \(\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)\) is a generalized gamma convolution, \(v_t(\alpha,\theta)/\pi\) is its Thorin density in the variable \(\theta=\sqrt z\), away from atoms). Let \(t\ge0\), \(\frac12<\alpha<\sigma_1\) and \(T>0\), and suppose \(v_t(\sigma,\theta)>0\) for every \((\sigma,\theta)\in[\alpha,\sigma_1]\times[0,T]\) at which \(\xi_t(\sigma+i\theta)\ne0\). Then \(\xi_t\) has no zero \(\beta+i\gamma\) with \(\alpha<\beta\le\sigma_1\) and \(0<\gamma<T\).
Source: ch/cp5.tex, label cp:prop:thorincert.




Theorem 15.5.8, page 628 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\) and \(\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du\), the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann’s xi function \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) (so \(\xi_0=\xi\)). Then \(\xi_{0.2}\) has no zero \(s\) with \(0.6\le\operatorname{Re}s\le0.9\) and \(0\le\operatorname{Im}s\le160\). This is certified by a computation in ball arithmetic (Arb, called from Python): \(\xi_{0.2}\) is evaluated by the trapezoid rule for its integral with an enclosure of the error of the rule, and the boundary of the rectangle \([0.6,0.9]\times[0,160]\) is walked counterclockwise, up the right edge, along the top and down the left edge, in \(23{,}219\) steps, with the step condition of the winding number certificate for the point \((0.2,0.6)\) (the step length times an explicit bound for \(|\xi_{0.2}'|\) along the step, plus the radii of the enclosures at its two ends, is below the smallest modulus of the enclosure at its start) verified at every step. The bottom edge is not walked, since \(\xi_{0.2}\) is real and positive on the real axis. The winding number of \(\xi_{0.2}\) around the rectangle is enclosed in \([0\pm3.47\times10^{-7}]\), so it is \(0\).

Proposition 15.6.1, page 631 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\) and, for real \(t\) of either sign, \(\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du\), the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann’s xi function (so \(\xi_0\) is the xi function), and \(H_t(z)=\frac18\xi_t(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)\). A zero \(\frac12+i\gamma\) of \(\xi_t\) on the critical line is the real zero \(z=2\gamma\) of \(H_t\), and while the real zeros are simple they move by \(dz_k/dt=2\sum_{j\ne k}(z_k-z_j)^{-1}\). Let \(\gamma_{71}<\gamma_{72}\) be the ordinates of the 71st and 72nd zeros of \(\xi\) in the upper half plane, the pair near height \(185\). At \(t=-0.287979\) the signs of \(\xi_t(\frac12+i\theta)\) at the \(131\) points \(\theta=184.6+0.01k\), \(k=0,\dots,130\), certified in ball arithmetic (Arb) at \(640\) bits from the trapezoid sum for the integral with an enclosure of its discretisation error, show two sign changes; hence the real function \(\theta\mapsto\xi_t(\frac12+i\theta)\) has at least two zeros in \([184.6,185.9]\), and the pair \((\gamma_{71},\gamma_{72})\) is still real at \(t=-0.287979\). This is the certified upper end of the book’s bracket \([-0.28803,-0.287979]\) for the time at which the pair collides when \(t\) decreases from \(0\); the lower end \(-0.28803\) rests on the asymptotic pair law \(D^2\approx8(t-t_*)\) for the distance \(D\) of the pair in the variable \(z\) near its collision time \(t_*\), and is not certified. Newton’s method on the same trapezoid sum puts the double zero of the pair at \(z_*=370.78087\), \(t_*=-0.287979837009\); a Krawczyk test certifies a real double zero of the trapezoid sum itself (a statement about the sum, not about \(H_t\)) in a box of half width \(2^{-400}\) about this point, and at \(t=t_*+1.2\times10^{-12}\) certified signs \(+,-,+\) of \(H_t\) at \(z_*-4\times10^{-6}\), \(z_*\) and \(z_*+4\times10^{-6}\) show that the pair is still real there, so the collision lies below \(-0.287979837008\). The floating point integration of the motion of the first \(600\) zeros that the book reports with this result (with the monotonicity of two gap functionals at the sampled times) is computed, not certified, and is not claimed here.

Problem 15.2, page 635 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du\) be the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann’s xi function, with \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\). Problem 15.3, page 635 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du\) be the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann’s xi function, with \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\), and let the GGC region \(\mathcal{G}\) be the set of points \((t,\alpha)\), \(t\ge0\), \(\alpha\ge\frac12\), at which \(\xi_t\) has no zero with real part above \(\alpha\), equivalently at which the shifted clock \(\xi_t(\alpha)/\xi_t(\alpha+\sqrt u)\) is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. The symmetrised truncations are \(K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-1/2}F_n(\frac12-w)\) with \(F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]\), where \(e_k,e_k'\) are independent standard exponential variables; Conjecture S says that, for every \(n\), all zeros of \(K_n\) in the strip \(0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14\), and at \(t=0\), \(\alpha=\frac12\) the Hurwitz argument shows that this for infinitely many \(n\) would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. The known part of \(\mathcal{G}\) consists of the points \((0,1)\) (the critical strip), \((0.2,0.6)\) (Polymath15) and a point on the level set \(t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2=0.2\) (Polymath15 with the verification of Platt and Trudgian), conditionally on an announced zero free half plane also \((0,\frac78)\), and every point \((t,\alpha)\) with \(\alpha\ge\frac12\), \(t\ge t_0\) and \((\alpha-\frac12)^2+\frac t2\ge(\alpha_0-\frac12)^2+\frac{t_0}2\) for one of these points \((t_0,\alpha_0)\) (de Bruijn’s strip theorem in Thorin form). Problem: give the symmetrised truncations a coordinate on the phase diagram: for some \((t,\alpha)\) outside the known part, is there a family of explicit truncations of \(\xi_t\), built from finitely many terms of the Pólya integral or of a Dirichlet series and making no use of the zeros, as the \(K_n\) are, that converges to \(\xi_t\) uniformly on compact sets, together with heights \(h_n\to\infty\) such that for infinitely many \(n\) the \(n\)th truncation has no zero with \(\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha\) and \(|\operatorname{Im}s|<h_n\)? Hurwitz’s theorem would then make \((t,\alpha)\) a new point of \(\mathcal{G}\); at \(t=0\) and \(\alpha=\frac12\) the question for the \(K_n\) is Conjecture S, and for the finite stages of the Pólya density as a maximum of exponential variables it is the open problem posed with those stages.

Problem 15.4, page 635 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For \(h\) smooth enough, with \(\hat h(r)=\int h(x)e^{irx}\,dx\), let \(W(h)=\hat h(\frac i2)+\hat h(-\frac i2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\bigl(h(\log n)+h(-\log n)\bigr)+\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\hat h(r)\operatorname{Re}\psi\bigl(\frac14+\frac{ir}2\bigr)\,dr-h(0)\log\pi\), where \(\Lambda\) is von Mangoldt’s function and \(\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma\); by Weil’s explicit formula \(W(h)=\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)\) over the zeros \(\rho=\frac12+i\gamma_\rho\) of Riemann’s xi function. For \(g\) supported in \([-L/2,L/2]\) and \(h=g*\tilde g\) with \(\tilde g(x)=\overline{g(-x)}\), under the Riemann Hypothesis (every \(\gamma_\rho\) real) \(W(h)=\sum_\rho|\hat g(\gamma_\rho)|^2\ge0\) (Weil’s criterion). Take the hat functions \(g_j(x)=\max(0,1-|x-c_j|/w)\) at nodes \(c_j\) spaced \(w\) apart inside \([-L/2,L/2]\), \(N=L/w-1\) functions in all, and the Weil Gram matrix \(G_{jk}=W(g_j*\tilde g_k)\), which is Hermitian. Problem: compute the Cholesky factor of \(G\) for decreasing \(w\) and increasing \(L\), and decide whether its entries converge to an object built from the arithmetic, as the first test of a factorisation \(W(g*\tilde g)=\|Ag\|^2\) with \(A\) built from the arithmetic.

Problem 15.5, page 635 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\) and \(H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du\), the de Bruijn Newman deformation of Riemann’s xi function (so \(H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)\)); while simple, its zeros \(z_k(t)\) move by \(dz_k/dt=2\sum_{j\ne k}(z_k-z_j)^{-1}\), like a log gas. Problem: find a global functional of the zeros of \(H_t\), insensitive to individual close pairs, that is monotone along the flow and whose positivity at \(t=0\) excludes collisions at positive time. Biane’s gap functional, the minimum over one gap of Laguerre’s quantity, is local; the functional asked for should instead be one quantity for all the zeros.

Problem 15.6, page 635 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi_t\) be the heat flow function (\(\xi_t(s)=8\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cosh((2s-1)u)\,du\), \(\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\), \(\xi_0=\xi\)), \(V_{0.2}=(\log\xi_{0.2})''(\frac12)\), \(\theta_1(0.2)\) the least positive ordinate of a zero of \(\xi_{0.2}\), \(v_{0.2}(10,\theta)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi_{0.2}'/\xi_{0.2})(10+i\theta)\), \(\zeta_t=\xi_t/(g\,e^{t\ell^2/4})\) with \(g(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\) and \(\ell=g'/g\), and \(S_t(T)\) the argument term of the zero count of \(\xi_t\) (the change of \(\arg\zeta_t\) along the segments from \(2\) to \(2+iT\) and \(2+iT\) to \(\frac12+iT\), divided by \(\pi\)). Problem (a): prove that \(v_{0.2}(10,\theta)\ge\frac{19}2V_{0.2}\) for every \(\theta\ge\theta_1(0.2)\), which would make the shifted clock of \(\xi_{0.2}\), with the constant part of its Thorin density removed, a GGC transform for every basepoint in \([\frac12,10]\); it suffices to bound \(|\zeta_{0.2}-1|\) on the discs of radius \(5\) about \(10+i\theta\) by a small constant uniform in \(\theta\) (computed: at the four sampled heights the largest of \(256\) sampled values of \(|\zeta_{0.2}-1|\) on each boundary circle is at most \(0.0326\), which is not a bound on the discs). Problem (b): for \(0<t\le0.2\) prove an explicit bound \(|S_t(T)|\le c_1\log T+c_2\) for \(T\ge T_1\), for instance by proving, with an explicit majorant \(M\), the two hypotheses of the Backlund type bound for \(S_t\) (\(\operatorname{Re}\zeta_t(2+iy)>0\) for \(0\le y\le T\), and \(M(\omega)\ge|\zeta_t(2+iT+\frac52e^{\pm i\omega})|\) for \(0\le\omega\le2\pi\)) (computed: the minimum of \(\operatorname{Re}\zeta_{0.2}(2+iy)\) over \(0\le y\le200\) is \(0.69006\), near \(y=14.015\)). At \(t=0\) much sharper explicit bounds are known (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022).

title: Books
text:
Nicholas G. Polson and Vadim Sokolov. 2026. Edition 1.
Computes the Thorin measure whose positivity is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, from Pólya’s integral for Xi in certified ball arithmetic, and proves that finite positivity tests on the heat trace cannot decide it; with hitting times, friable approximants, the reciprocal zeta function and Lee Yang theory.

title: On Langlands Conjectures Probabilistic Methods
text:
Description
This monograph asks what probability can contribute to the Langlands programme, and answers on two sides. The first is a limitation, proved in the opening chapter: no argument that sees only the limiting distribution of Frobenius data can detect automorphy, because equidistribution is a consequence of functoriality, not a route to it. The second is what probability does supply: consequences of the conjectures, calibration against data, and probabilistic reformulations.
The book covers Weyl’s criterion and the Sato Tate law, random matrix models of the zeros of L functions, Hecke operators as random walks on Bruhat Tits trees, hitting times on supersingular isogeny graphs, and Bayesian inference for Sato Tate groups. At its centre is the Thorin framework: for a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the statement that the reciprocal of an even completion of its L function is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. Later chapters turn the same devices on reciprocity, Fermat’s last theorem, random integers and the Poisson Dirichlet law, Hecke characters, Maass forms, Calegari’s theorems on even representations and potential modularity, and the crossing probabilities of critical percolation, whose threshold law is, up to normalisation, the Mellin transform of the completed L function of an elliptic curve. These are reformulations: no new case of reciprocity and no Riemann hypothesis is proved.
Results new to the book include the limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs, the Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis and for the Ramanujan conjecture, an extreme value representation of the L functions of multiplicative eta products, the Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer, and a consistency theorem for the Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups. Open computational problems close every chapter, and the scripts and data behind the numbers are in the repository.

title: On Langlands Conjectures Probabilistic Methods
On Langlands Conjectures Probabilistic Methods
text:
Main results

Equidistribution does not determine automorphy (Proposition 1.5, page 7): Sato Tate equidistribution of a sequence indexed by the primes cannot certify that it comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) with trivial central character, because altering such a sequence on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves the limiting empirical averages of all continuous functions unchanged but, by Ramakrishnan’s refinement of strong multiplicity one, makes it nonautomorphic, and continuum many equidistributed sequences are not automorphic.
Limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs (Theorem 10.6, page 151): As the characteristic grows through primes congruent to 1 modulo 12, with the prime isogeny degree fixed, the mean time for simple random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph to hit a uniformly random curve is asymptotic to the number of vertices times the expected number of visits of simple random walk on the regular tree of the same degree to its starting point, so about twice the number of vertices for 2 isogenies.
Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of automorphic L functions (Theorem 14.8, page 220): The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the L function of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, and the Riemann hypothesis for zeta, are each equivalent to several positivity statements, among them that the reciprocal of the self dual completion, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure sits at the squared ordinates of the zeros, and a Hankel criterion computable from central derivatives; the theorem is an equivalence that extends the first author’s 2018 paper, and it proves no case of either hypothesis.
Thorin criterion for the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at a prime (Corollary 15.4, page 238): For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over the rationals with trivial central character, the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at an unramified prime (outside the degenerate case of trace 2) holds exactly when the reciprocal of the symmetrised Euler factor, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, which is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb (Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin); the corollary is an equivalence and proves no case of the conjecture.
Thorin structure of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree (Theorem 15.15, page 246): The first time that continuous time simple random walk on a regular tree (the Hecke walk, on the Bruhat Tits tree when the degree is a prime plus one) reaches distance n from its start is a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin atoms, given by the zeros of the sphere polynomials of the tree, lie in the Kesten band and follow the arcsine law as n grows, with an exact mean, a variance linear in n and a central limit theorem; Thorin support in the Kesten band is the random walk form of the Ramanujan bound, and this unconditional theorem about the tree proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms.
Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer (Theorem 20.18, page 350): As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, the logarithms of its prime power factors, multiplied by the parameter minus one and labelled by any equidistributed sequence of points such as Frobenius classes or Sato Tate angles, converge in law to the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator carrying independent labels drawn from the equidistribution law, and the labelled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma random measure, so that equidistribution becomes a Gamma process.
Extreme value representation of L functions of eta products (Theorem 29.7, page 541): For every eta product, that is every product of the functions eta(m tau) raised to nonnegative integer powers r_m with the sum of m r_m equal to 24 (the thirty multiplicative eta products among them), the L function is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at an explicit maximum of exponential clocks, so its values at positive real points are probabilities strictly between zero and one that increase strictly to one.
Consistency of Bayes factors under equidistribution (Theorem 31.1, page 571): For any deterministic sequence, such as normalised Frobenius traces, that is equidistributed for a true law with finitely many atoms and finite Kullback Leibler divergence from one candidate law, and with a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor between two candidate laws is asymptotically linear in the number of observations, and as the clipping level grows its slope tends to the difference of the divergences of the true law from the two candidates, with no independence assumed.

All 194 results of the book (140 proved, 6 conditional, 48 open) are on the page Results by chapter, each with its statement, status and number.

Proposition 1.5, page 7 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be the set of primes, \(\pi(x)\) the number of primes \(p\le x\), and \(\mathbb{A}\) the adele ring of \(\mathbb{Q}\). A set \(S\subset\mathcal{P}\) has density zero if \(\#\{p\le x:p\in S\}/\pi(x)\to0\) as \(x\to\infty\). A sequence \((x_p)_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\) of real numbers comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation \(\pi\) of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A})\) with trivial central character if \(x_p=\operatorname{tr}A_p(\pi)\) for all but finitely many primes \(p\), where \(A_p(\pi)\) is the unitarily normalised Satake parameter of \(\pi\) at \(p\), and it is automorphic if it comes from some such \(\pi\); both notions are unchanged when finitely many terms are changed. A sequence \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) is equidistributed with respect to the Sato Tate law \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx\) on \([-2,2]\) if \(\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\phi(x_p)\to\int\phi\,d\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}\) as \(x\to\infty\) for every continuous function \(\phi\) on \([-2,2]\). Let \(\mathcal{E}\) be the set of sequences \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that are equidistributed with respect to \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}\). (1) \(\mathcal{E}\) has the cardinality of the continuum and contains continuum many sequences no two of which agree at all but finitely many primes. The automorphic sequences fall into countably many classes under the relation of agreeing at all but finitely many primes, so all but countably many of those sequences are not automorphic. (2) Let \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) come from \(\pi\), and let \((x'_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) differ from \((x_p)\) exactly on an infinite set \(S\) of density zero. Then \((x'_p)\) is not automorphic, and \((x'_p)\in\mathcal{E}\) if and only if \((x_p)\in\mathcal{E}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch01.tex, label prop:01limits.




Corollary 1.6, page 8 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be the set of primes and \(\pi(x)\) the number of primes \(p\le x\); a set \(S\subset\mathcal{P}\) has density zero if \(\#\{p\le x:p\in S\}/\pi(x)\to0\) as \(x\to\infty\). Call a sequence \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) automorphic if there is a cuspidal automorphic representation \(\pi\) of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A})\), where \(\mathbb{A}\) is the ring of adeles of \(\mathbb{Q}\), with trivial central character such that \(x_p=\operatorname{tr}A_p(\pi)\) for all but finitely many primes \(p\), where \(A_p(\pi)\) is the unitarily normalised Satake parameter of \(\pi\) at \(p\). Let \(\mathcal{E}\) be the set of sequences \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that are equidistributed with respect to the Sato Tate law, that is, with \(\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\phi(x_p)\to\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-2}^{2}\phi(t)\sqrt{4-t^2}\,dt\) as \(x\to\infty\) for every continuous function \(\phi\) on \([-2,2]\). Let \(\Phi\) be any function on \([-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that is unchanged when a sequence is altered on a set of density zero; for instance any function of the set of weak limit points of the empirical measures \(\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\delta_{x_p}\) as \(x\to\infty\), which is unchanged by such alterations. Then for every automorphic \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) there are continuum many sequences in \([-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that are not automorphic and on which \(\Phi\) takes the value it takes on \((x_p)\); if \((x_p)\in\mathcal{E}\), they all lie in \(\mathcal{E}\). In particular \(\Phi\) cannot characterise automorphy.
Source: book/chapters/ch01.tex, label cor:01functional.







Conjecture 5.3, page 68 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(E\) be an elliptic curve over \(\mathbb{Q}\) of conductor \(N\) without complex multiplication. For a prime \(p \nmid N\) put \(a_p = p + 1 - \#E(\mathbb{F}_p)\) and \(x_p = a_p/\sqrt{p} \in [-2,2]\). Let \(p_1 < p_2 < \cdots\) be the primes not dividing \(N\), let \(F_n\) be the empirical distribution function of \(x_{p_1}, \dots, x_{p_n}\), let \(F_{\mathrm{ST}}(t) = \int_{-2}^{t} \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4-u^2}\,du\) be the distribution function of the Sato Tate law on \([-2,2]\), and let \(D_n = \sup_{t \in [-2,2]} |F_n(t) - F_{\mathrm{ST}}(t)|\) be the Kolmogorov discrepancy. For \(x \ge 2\) let \(n = n(x)\) be the number of primes \(p \le x\) with \(p \nmid N\). Conjecture (open): (a) (a conjecture of Akiyama and Tanigawa) \(D_n = O(n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})\) for every \(\varepsilon > 0\); (b) \(\sqrt{n}\,D_n \to 0\) in logarithmic density, that is, for every \(\delta > 0\) the set \(S_\delta\) of real \(x \ge 2\) with \(\sqrt{n}\,D_n > \delta\) has logarithmic density zero, \(\frac{1}{\log X}\int_{S_\delta \cap [2,X]} \frac{dx}{x} \to 0\) as \(X \to \infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05.tex, label conj:05bridge.







Proposition 7.13, page 101 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(p\) be an odd prime, write \(e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}\), and for \(x\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times\) let \(\bar x\) denote its inverse. For \(t\in[0,1]\) let \(I=\{1,\dots,m\}\) with \(m=\lfloor t(p-1)\rfloor\), viewed as a set of residues modulo \(p\), let \(-I=\{p-x:x\in I\}\), and put \(R_I=\sum_{x\in I}e(\bar x/p)\) and \(G_I=\sum_{x\in I}e(x/p)\). Let \(a\) be uniform in \(\mathbb{F}_p^\times\). (1) For \(S_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in I}e\bigl((ax+\bar x)/p\bigr)\), [|S_p|2=,S_p2=.] (2) For \(S'_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in I}e\bigl((x+a\bar x)/p\bigr)\), [|S’_p|2=,S_p’2=.] In both cases the mean is \(\mathbb{E}S_p=-p^{-1/2}(p-1)^{-1}R_I\), respectively \(\mathbb{E}S'_p=-p^{-1/2}(p-1)^{-1}G_I\), which tends to \(0\) as \(p\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch06b.tex, label prop:06bsecond.




Corollary 7.14, page 102 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(p\) be an odd prime, \(e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}\), and \(\bar x\) the inverse of \(x\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times\). For \(t\in[0,1]\) let \(S'_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{1\le x\le\lfloor t(p-1)\rfloor}e\bigl((x+a\bar x)/p\bigr)\) with \(a\) uniform in \(\mathbb{F}_p^\times\), and write \(u_+=\max(u,0)\). As \(p\to\infty\) the variances of the real and imaginary parts of \(S'_p(a,t)\) converge to [,S’=(t+(2t-1)+)-,,S’=(t-(2t-1)+)-.] At \(t=\frac12\) the correction to the real part vanishes, so its limiting variance is \(\frac14\), and the imaginary part loses exactly \(1/\pi^2\): \(\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Im}S'_p(a,\tfrac12)\to\frac14-\frac1{\pi^2}=0.1487\).

Proposition 7.15, page 103 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\mathrm{ST}_h)_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}\) be independent real random variables, each with the Sato Tate law, the semicircle law on \([-2,2]\) with density \(\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\). Put \(c_0(t)=t\) and \(c_h(t)=(e^{2\pi iht}-1)/(2\pi ih)\) for \(h\ne0\), and let \(K(t)=\sum_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}c_h(t)\,\mathrm{ST}_h\) for \(0\le t\le1\), the series being the limit of its symmetric partial sums over \(|h|\le H\) as \(H\to\infty\). Write \(u_+=\max(u,0)\). For \(s,t\in[0,1]\), [,K(s)=(s,t),,K(s)K(t)=(s+t-1)_+.] Consequently \(\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Re}K(t)=\frac12\bigl(t+(2t-1)_+\bigr)\), \(\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Im}K(t)=\frac12\bigl(t-(2t-1)_+\bigr)\), and \(\operatorname{Re}K(t)\), \(\operatorname{Im}K(t)\) are uncorrelated. Moreover, almost surely, [K(1-t)=K(1)-(0t),] so \(\operatorname{Im}K(1-t)=\operatorname{Im}K(t)\), \(K(1)=2\operatorname{Re}K(\tfrac12)=\mathrm{ST}_0\), and \(\operatorname{Im}K(0)=\operatorname{Im}K(1)=0\).

Proposition 7.16, page 105 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\mathrm{ST}_h)_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}\) be independent real random variables, each with the Sato Tate law, the semicircle law on \([-2,2]\) with density \(\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\), and let \(K(t)=t\,\mathrm{ST}_0+\sum_{h\ne0}\frac{e^{2\pi iht}-1}{2\pi ih}\,\mathrm{ST}_h\) for \(0\le t\le1\), the series being the limit of its symmetric partial sums. The random variable \(\operatorname{Im}K(\tfrac12)=\frac1\pi\sum_{h\ \mathrm{odd}}\mathrm{ST}_h/h\) is unbounded above and below, and for every \(M>0\), [(K()>M)e{-2M2},] the Chernoff bound of a centred Gaussian variable with the same variance \(\frac14\). More generally, every real random variable \(X=\sum_h\gamma_h\mathrm{ST}_h\) with \(\sum_h\gamma_h^2<\infty\), in particular every real linear combination of the real and imaginary parts of finitely many values of \(K\), satisfies \(\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda X}\le e^{\lambda^2\mathrm{Var}(X)/2}\) for all real \(\lambda\).

Theorem 9.1, page 135 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(q\ge2\) be an integer, let \(\mathcal{T}_q\) be the \((q+1)\) regular tree with graph distance \(d\) and a fixed vertex \(o\), let \(A\) be its adjacency operator, let \(X=q^{-1/2}A\), a bounded self adjoint operator on \(\ell^2(\mathcal{T}_q)\), and let \(\mu_q\) be the spectral measure of \(X\) at \(\delta_o\), so that \(\langle\delta_o,\phi(X)\delta_o\rangle=\int\phi\,d\mu_q\) for continuous \(\phi\). For \(n\ge0\) let \(A_n\) be the operator \(A_nf(v)=\sum_{d(v,w)=n}f(w)\), with \(A_0=I\), and put \(B_n=q^{-n/2}A_n\). Write \(U_n\) for the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind, \(U_n(\cos\theta)=\sin((n+1)\theta)/\sin\theta\), and \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx/(2\pi)\) for the Sato Tate measure on \([-2,2]\). Then: (1) \(B_1=U_1(X/2)\) and \(B_n=U_n(X/2)-q^{-1}U_{n-2}(X/2)\) for \(n\ge2\). (2) \(c_n=\int U_n(x/2)\,d\mu_q(x)\) equals \(q^{-n/2}\) for \(n\) even and \(0\) for \(n\) odd. (3) \(\mu_q\) is supported on \([-2,2]\) with the Kesten McKay density [_q(dx)=,dx .] (4) If \(S\) is simple random walk on \(\mathcal{T}_q\) started at \(o\), then \(\int x^{2m}\,d\mu_q=(q+1)^{2m}q^{-m}\,\mathbb{P}(S_{2m}=o)\) for \(m\ge0\). (5) The walk returns to \(o\) with probability \(1/q\), and the Green function \(G(1)=\sum_{n\ge0}\mathbb{P}(S_n=o)\), the expected number of visits to \(o\), equals \(q/(q-1)\). (6) \(\mu_q\) converges weakly to \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}\) as \(q\to\infty\).

Proposition 10.3, page 148 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(q\ge1\) be an integer and let \(G\) be a finite connected \((q+1)\) regular graph on \(n\) vertices, possibly with loops and multiple edges, with adjacency matrix \(A\) (a loop contributing \(2\) to the diagonal) and eigenvalues \(q+1=\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n\). Its Ihara zeta function is \(Z_G(u)=\prod_{\mathfrak p}(1-u^{\nu(\mathfrak p)})^{-1}\), the product over the classes \(\mathfrak p\), under cyclic rotation, of primitive closed paths of oriented edges without backtracking and without tail, with \(\nu(\mathfrak p)\) the length; by the Ihara Bass determinant formula it is a rational function of \(u\), and its poles in \(\{\pm1,\pm1/q\}\) are called trivial. \(Z_G\) satisfies the graph Riemann hypothesis if every nontrivial pole lies on the circle \(|u|=q^{-1/2}\), and \(G\) is Ramanujan if every eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(A\) with \(|\lambda|\ne q+1\) satisfies \(|\lambda|\le2\sqrt q\). Let \(P=A/(q+1)\) be the transition matrix of simple random walk on \(G\), let \(\lambda_*=\max\{|\lambda_j|:|\lambda_j|\ne q+1\}\) (with \(\lambda_*=0\) if there is no such eigenvalue), let \(\beta=1\) if \(G\) is bipartite and \(\beta=0\) otherwise, let \(\delta_t=\max_{x}\bigl|P^t(x,x)-(1+\beta(-1)^t)/n\bigr|\), and let \(\rho_q=2\sqrt q/(q+1)\). Then the following are equivalent: (1) \(Z_G\) satisfies the graph Riemann hypothesis; (2) \(G\) is Ramanujan; (3) \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}\delta_t^{1/t}\le\rho_q\). Moreover \(\limsup_t\delta_t^{1/t}=\lambda_*/(q+1)\) exactly, so the return probabilities of a Ramanujan graph approach equilibrium at an exponential rate no slower than the rate \(\rho_q\) at which the return probabilities of simple random walk on the \((q+1)\) regular tree tend to zero.
Source: book/chapters/ch08.tex, label prop:08three.




Theorem 10.6, page 151 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\ell\) be a prime. For a prime \(N\equiv1\pmod{12}\) with \(N\ne\ell\), let \(G_N(\ell)\) be the supersingular \(\ell\) isogeny graph in characteristic \(N\), whose vertices are the \(h=(N-1)/12\) isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over \(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N\), each curve having one edge for each of its \(\ell+1\) subgroups of order \(\ell\), joining it to the quotient curve; dual isogenies pair the edges, so that \(G_N(\ell)\) is an undirected \((\ell+1)\) regular graph, possibly with loops and multiple edges. For simple random walk \((X_t)\) on \(G_N(\ell)\), whose stationary law \(\pi\) is uniform, let \(\tau_y=\min\{t\ge0:X_t=y\}\) and let \(K_N=\sum_y\pi(y)\,\mathbb{E}_x\tau_y\) be the Kemeny constant, which does not depend on the starting vertex \(x\). As \(N\to\infty\) through primes \(N\equiv1\pmod{12}\), with \(\ell\) fixed, [.] Equivalently, the mean hitting time of a uniformly random target, from any fixed start or from a uniformly random one, is asymptotic to \(\ell h/(\ell-1)\); for \(\ell=2\) it is about \(2h\).
Source: book/chapters/ch08.tex, label thm:08kemeny.







Proposition 11.3, page 161 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta\) be the discriminant modular form of weight \(12\) and level \(1\), with Fourier coefficients \(\tau(n)\), and let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-11/2-s}\) be its \(L\) function in the unitary normalisation, with centre \(s=\tfrac12\). For every \(\sigma>1\) we have \(\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|L(\sigma+it,\Delta)|>L(\sigma,\Delta)>0\). In particular \(t\mapsto L(\sigma+it,\Delta)/L(\sigma,\Delta)\) is not a characteristic function.
Source: book/chapters/ch09.tex, label prop:ch09notcf.




Proposition 11.12, page 168 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\theta_p)\), indexed by the primes \(p\), be independent random variables with the Sato Tate law \(\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\) on \([0,\pi]\), and let \(L_{\mathrm{rand}}(s)=\prod_p(1-e^{i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}(1-e^{-i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}\) be the Sato Tate random Euler product. For real \(\sigma>1/2\) and real \(t\) the product \(L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma+it)\), the limit of the partial products over the primes \(p\le P\) as \(P\to\infty\), converges almost surely and in \(L^2\), and [,|L_{}(+it)|^2=(2).]
Source: book/chapters/ch09.tex, label prop:ch09martingale.




Theorem 11.13, page 168 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\theta_p)\), indexed by the primes \(p\), be independent random variables with the Sato Tate law \(\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\) on \([0,\pi]\), and let \(L_{\mathrm{rand}}(s)=\prod_p(1-e^{i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}(1-e^{-i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}\) be the Sato Tate random Euler product; for real \(\sigma>1/2\) every factor is positive and \(\log L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma)=\sum_p\sum_{k\ge1}2\cos(k\theta_p)/(kp^{k\sigma})\) converges almost surely. Let \(V(\sigma)=\sum_pp^{-2\sigma}\), so that \(V(\sigma)=\log\frac{1}{2\sigma-1}+O(1)\) as \(\sigma\to\frac12^+\). Then [N(0,1),^+,] where \(\Longrightarrow\) denotes convergence in law and \(N(0,1)\) is the standard normal law.
Source: book/chapters/ch09.tex, label thm:ch09clt.







Proposition 12.4, page 176 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f\) be a real analytic function on a neighbourhood of a compact interval \([a,b]\), with finitely many zeros \(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_r\) in \((a,b)\), all simple, and no zero at \(a\) or at \(b\). Then, as \(x\to\infty\), the Lebesgue measure of the set \(\{t\in[a,b]:\log|f(t)|<-x\}\) equals \(2e^{-x}\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{1}{|f'(\gamma_j)|}+O(e^{-2x})\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09blefttail.




Conjecture 12.6, page 179 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), be the discriminant cusp form of weight \(12\) for \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\), let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\), whose critical line is \(\operatorname{Re}s=6\), and for each prime \(p\) let \(\theta_p\in[0,\pi]\) be defined by \(\tau(p)=2p^{11/2}\cos\theta_p\). Let \(\gamma_{\mathrm E}\) be Euler’s constant and put \(A_\Delta=\sum_p\bigl(\log(1-\frac1p)+\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{(2\cos m\theta_p)^2}{m^2p^m}\bigr)\) and \(V_\Delta(T)=\frac12\bigl(\log\bigl(2\log\frac{T}{2\pi}\bigr)+\gamma_{\mathrm E}+1+A_\Delta\bigr)\). Conjecture: for \(t\) uniformly distributed on \([T,2T]\), \(\operatorname{Var}\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=V_\Delta(T)+o(1)\) as \(T\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label conj:09bvar.




Proposition 12.7, page 181 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((U_p)\), indexed by the primes, be independent random variables uniformly distributed on the unit circle, and for \(P\ge3\) and real \(h\) put \(X_P(h)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{p\le P}U_pp^{-1/2-ih}\). Then \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_P(h),X_P(h'))=\frac12\sum_{p\le P}\frac{\cos((h - h')\log p)}{p}=\frac12\log\min\bigl(\log P,\frac{1}{|h - h'|}\bigr)+O(1)\), uniformly in \(P\) and in \(0<|h - h'|\le1\). The same holds for the field \(X^\Delta_P(h)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{p\le P}\lambda(p)U_pp^{-1/2-ih}\), where \(\lambda(p)=\tau(p)/p^{11/2}\) and \(\tau(n)\) are the coefficients of the discriminant cusp form \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), with \(\lambda(p)^2/p\) in place of \(1/p\) in the sum, that is, \(\operatorname{Cov}(X^\Delta_P(h),X^\Delta_P(h'))=\frac12\sum_{p\le P}\frac{\lambda(p)^2\cos((h - h')\log p)}{p}=\frac12\log\min\bigl(\log P,\frac{1}{|h - h'|}\bigr)+O(1)\) with the same uniformity.
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bcov.




Proposition 12.8, page 182 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(b\ge2\) be an integer and \(\sigma>0\), and let \(\{B_v(s):0\le s\le n\}\), indexed by the \(b^n\) leaves \(v\) of the \(b\) ary tree of depth \(n\), be Brownian motion indexed by the tree: each edge carries an independent Brownian path of duration one and variance \(\sigma^2\) per unit time, and \(B_v\) is the concatenation of the paths along the edges from the root to \(v\). Put \(c=\sigma\sqrt{2\log b}\), \(\theta=c/\sigma^2=\sqrt{2\log b}/\sigma\) and \(x_n=cn - a\log n\) for a constant \(a>0\). Fix \(y\ge0\). Let \(N_n(y)\) be the number of leaves with \(B_v(n)\ge x_n+y\), and \(Z_n(y)\) the number of leaves with \(B_v(n)\in[x_n+y,x_n+y+1]\) and \(B_v(s)\le\frac snx_n+y+1\) for all \(s\in[0,n]\). As \(n\to\infty\), \(\mathbb{E}N_n(y)\sim\frac{\sigma}{c\sqrt{2\pi}}\,n^{\theta a-\frac12}e^{-\theta y}\) and \(\mathbb{E}Z_n(y)\sim\kappa\,(1+y)\,n^{\theta a-\frac32}e^{-\theta y}\), with \(\kappa=2(\theta-1+e^{-\theta})/(\sigma^3\theta^2\sqrt{2\pi})\). In particular the choice \(a=\frac1{2\theta}\) makes \(\mathbb{E}N_n(y)\) of order one, while \(a=\frac3{2\theta}\) makes \(\mathbb{E}Z_n(y)\to\kappa(1+y)e^{-\theta y}\), and for that choice \(\mathbb{E}N_n(y)\) grows like \(n\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bballot.




Proposition 12.16, page 194 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta), for the Gaussian limit only.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), let \(W\) be a random variable with density \(\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) (the P'olya variable of \(\Delta\)), and let \(\varphi_W(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{itW}\). For real \(t\), \(\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=\log|\varphi_W(t)|-\log|\Gamma(6+it)|+\log(\Gamma(6)L(6,\Delta))\), and, as \(|t|\to\infty\), \(\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=\log|\varphi_W(t)|+\frac\pi2|t|-\frac{11}2\log|t|+C_\Delta+O(1/|t|)\), with \(C_\Delta=\log(120\,L(6,\Delta))-\frac12\log2\pi=3.6355\). Consequently, if all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=6\) (the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,\Delta)\)), then for \(t\) uniformly distributed on \([T,2T]\) the quantity \(\bigl(\log|\varphi_W(t)|+\frac\pi2t-\frac{11}2\log t+C_\Delta\bigr)/\sqrt{\frac12\log\log T}\) converges in law to the standard normal distribution as \(T\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bpolya.




Proposition 12.17, page 195 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta).
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\); let \(W\) have density \(\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) and \(\varphi_W(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{itW}\). Assume the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,\Delta)\), so that the zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) are \(6\pm i\gamma_k\) with \(0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\dots\), listed with multiplicity. Let \(\tau_\Delta=\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\), and let \(Y=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables. For real \(t\ne\pm\gamma_k\), \(\log|\varphi_W(t)|=\sum_k\log\bigl|1-\frac{t^2}{\gamma_k^2}\bigr|=\int_{(0,\infty)}\log\bigl|1-\frac{t^2}{x}\bigr|\,\tau_\Delta(dx)=-\log|\mathcal{L}_Y(t^2)|\), where \(\mathcal{L}_Y(u)=\prod_k(1-u/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}\) is the meromorphic continuation to \(\mathbb{C}\) of the moment generating function \(\mathbb{E}e^{uY}\), \(u<\gamma_1^2\). Moreover, on each interval between consecutive zeros, \(t\mapsto\log|\varphi_W(t)|\) is strictly concave.
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bpotential.




Proposition 12.18, page 195 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E_{j,n}\), \(1\le j\le24\), \(n\ge1\), be independent standard exponential variables and \(M^*=\max_{j,n}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)\), so that the discriminant cusp form \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), satisfies \(\Delta(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}\mathbb{P}(M^*\le y)\) for \(y>0\). Let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), let \(G\) have the gamma law of shape \(6\) and unit rate, independent of \(M^*\), and write \(\mathbb{E}[X;A]=\mathbb{E}[X\,1_A]\) for an event \(A\). For real \(t\), \(\frac{\Gamma(6+it)}{\Gamma(6)}\,L(6+it,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[G^{it};\,G\ge2\pi M^*\bigr]\). The finite measure \(\nu(B)=\mathbb{P}(\log G\in B,\ G\ge2\pi M^*)\) has total mass \(L(6,\Delta)\) and equals \(L(6,\Delta)\) times the law of \(W+\log2\pi\), where \(W\) is the P'olya variable of \(\Delta\), with density \(\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bmstar.







Theorem 13.6, page 204 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), be the discriminant cusp form of weight \(12\) for \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\), let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), and let \(W\) be a random variable with the probability density \(\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\), \(u\in\mathbb{R}\) (the P'olya kernel of \(\Delta\)). Then \(W\) is symmetric, has moments of all orders and an entire moment generating function, and for all \(z\in\mathbb{C}\), \(\mathbb{E}[e^{zW}]=\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\). In particular \(\mathbb{E}[e^{itW}]=\Lambda(6+it,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) is real and even, and the Riemann hypothesis for \(\Delta\) (all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=6\)) is equivalent to the statement that the characteristic function of \(W\) has only real zeros.

Theorem 13.7, page 205 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), and let \(W\) have density \(\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Write each zero of \(z\mapsto\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)\) as \(z=i\gamma\) (no such \(z\) is real, since \(\Lambda(6+x,\Delta)>0\) for real \(x\)), and list one representative of each pair \(\{\gamma,-\gamma\}\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0\) as \(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\dots\), with multiplicity and in order of increasing real part. Unconditionally, \(\sum_k|\gamma_k|^{-2}<\infty\) and for all \(z\in\mathbb{C}\), \(\frac{\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)}{\Lambda(6,\Delta)}=\prod_k\bigl(1+\frac{z^2}{\gamma_k^2}\bigr)\). Consequently \(\mathbb{E}W=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}W=2\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2}\), where the right side is real because nonreal \(\gamma_k\) occur in conjugate pairs.

Theorem 13.8, page 206 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\). A probability law on \([0,\infty)\) is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) if it is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws; equivalently (Thorin) its Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\frac st)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)\), \(s\ge0\), with drift \(a\ge0\) and a positive measure \(\tau\) on \((0,\infty)\), finite on compact sets, the Thorin measure, satisfying \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\). The following are equivalent: (i) all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=6\); (ii) the function \(s\mapsto\Lambda(6,\Delta)/\Lambda(6+\sqrt s,\Delta)\), \(s>0\), is the Laplace transform of a GGC. When they hold, writing the zeros as \(6\pm i\gamma_k\) with \(\gamma_k>0\), listed with multiplicity, the GGC has drift \(0\) and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\), it is the law of \(X=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables, and its L'evy measure has density \(k(x)/x\), where \(k(x)=\sum_ke^{-\gamma_k^2x}\), \(x>0\), is completely monotone.

Theorem 13.10, page 208 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a self dual cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge2\), with completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, conductor included, so that \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) is entire of order one, real on the real axis, and satisfies \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon\Lambda(1-s,\pi)\) with \(\varepsilon=\pm1\). A probability law on \([0,\infty)\) is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) if it is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws; equivalently its Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\frac st)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)\), \(s\ge0\), with \(a\ge0\) and a positive measure \(\tau\) on \((0,\infty)\), finite on compact sets, the Thorin measure, satisfying \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\). Suppose \(\Lambda(\frac12,\pi)\ne0\). Then the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(\pi\) (all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\)) holds if and only if \(s\mapsto\Lambda(\frac12,\pi)/\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt s,\pi)\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC, and then its Thorin measure is \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\) over the ordinates \(\gamma_k>0\) of the zeros \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_k\).

Lemma 14.6, page 216 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist \(|\cdot|^{iy}\) of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), and let \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\gamma(s,\pi)L(s,\pi)\) be its completed \(L\) function in the unitary normalisation, in which the Dirichlet series \(L(s,\pi)=\sum_ma_\pi(m)m^{-s}\) converges absolutely for \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\) and \(\gamma(s,\pi)=N_\pi^{s/2}\prod_{j=1}^n\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\mu_j)\), with \(N_\pi\) the conductor, \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\) and archimedean parameters \(\mu_j\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\mu_j>-\frac12\); \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) is entire of order one and satisfies \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon(\pi)\Lambda(1-s,\tilde\pi)\) with \(|\varepsilon(\pi)|=1\), \(\tilde\pi\) the contragredient. Let \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\), \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\) and \(F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)/\Xi_\pi(0)\), and when \(\pi\cong\tilde\pi\) let \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r\). Then (i) \(\Xi_\pi\) is entire, even, and \(\Xi_\pi(\bar z)=\overline{\Xi_\pi(z)}\), so it is real on \(\mathbb{R}\); (ii) for real \(x\ne0\), \(\Xi_\pi(x)=|\Lambda(\frac12+x,\pi)|^2/x^{2r}\ge0\), \(\Xi_\pi(0)>0\), and \(\Xi_\pi(x)>0\) for \(|x|\ge\frac12\); (iii) \(\Xi_\pi\) has order at most one, and every zero \(z\) of \(\Xi_\pi\) satisfies \(|\operatorname{Re}z|<\frac12\); (iv) \(F_\pi\) is entire of order at most \(\frac12\) with \(F_\pi(0)=1\), and if the zeros of \(\Xi_\pi\) are listed in pairs \(\pm z_k\) with multiplicity and \(s_k=z_k^2\), then \(F_\pi(s)=\prod_k(1-s/s_k)\) with \(\sum_k|s_k|^{-1}<\infty\); (v) if \(\pi\cong\tilde\pi\) then \(\varepsilon(\pi)=(-1)^r\), and \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi\) is entire, even and real on \(\mathbb{R}\) with \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(0)\ne0\). The same statements hold for \(\Xi_\zeta(z)=\xi(\frac12+z)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)\), which is moreover strictly positive on \(\mathbb{R}\).

Theorem 14.7, page 217 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E\) be an entire function with \(E(-z)=E(z)\), \(E(\bar z)=\overline{E(z)}\) and \(E(0)=1\), of order less than two, whose zeros lie in a strip \(|\operatorname{Re}z|\le\sigma_0\). List its zeros as pairs \(\pm z_k\) with multiplicity, put \(t_k=-z_k^2\) and \(F(s)=E(\sqrt s)=\prod_k(1+s/t_k)\). A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(\exp(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,\tau(dt))\), \(s\ge0\), with drift \(a\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(\tau\), a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\); a Stieltjes function is a function on \((0,\infty)\) of the form \(a/s+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\sigma(dt)/(s+t)\) with \(a,b\ge0\) and \(\sigma\) a positive measure with \(\int\sigma(dt)/(1+t)<\infty\). Then \(k(x)=\sum_ke^{-t_kx}\) converges absolutely and locally uniformly on \((0,\infty)\), the sums \(S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}\), \(n\ge1\), converge absolutely and are real, and the following are equivalent. (a) Every zero of \(E\) lies on \(i\mathbb{R}\); equivalently \(t_k\in(0,\infty)\) for all \(k\). (b) \(1/F\) restricted to \((0,\infty)\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (c) \(1/F(s)=\mathbb{E}e^{-sX}\) for \(s\ge0\), where \(X=\sum_kE_k/t_k\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables; that is, \(1/F\) is a GGC transform with drift \(0\) and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{t_k}\). (d) \(k\) is completely monotone on \((0,\infty)\). (e) \(F\) has no zero in \((0,\infty)\) and \(F'/F\) is a Stieltjes function on \((0,\infty)\). (e’) \(E\) has no real zero, and \(\operatorname{Im}(F'/F)(s)\le0\) at every \(s\) with \(\operatorname{Im}s>0\) and \(F(s)\ne0\). (f) There is a positive measure \(\nu\) on \([0,\infty)\) with \(S_{j+1}=\int u^j\nu(du)\) for all \(j\ge0\); equivalently, the Hankel matrices \((S_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^N\) and \((S_{i+j+2})_{i,j=0}^N\) are positive semidefinite for every \(N\). When these hold, \(\nu=\sum_kt_k^{-1}\delta_{1/t_k}\), the Stieltjes function in (e) is \(\sum_k(s+t_k)^{-1}\), and the Bernstein measure of \(k\) (the positive measure \(\mu\) with \(k(x)=\int e^{-tx}\mu(dt)\)) is \(\sum_k\delta_{t_k}\).

Theorem 14.8, page 220 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist \(|\cdot|^{iy}\) of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with contragredient \(\tilde\pi\) and completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\gamma(s,\pi)L(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation: the Dirichlet series \(L(s,\pi)=\sum_ma_\pi(m)m^{-s}\) converges absolutely for \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\), \(\gamma(s,\pi)=N_\pi^{s/2}\prod_{j=1}^n\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\mu_j)\) with \(N_\pi\) the conductor, \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\) and archimedean parameters \(\mu_j\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\mu_j>-\frac12\), and \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) is entire of order one with \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon(\pi)\Lambda(1-s,\tilde\pi)\), \(|\varepsilon(\pi)|=1\), so that the critical line is \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\). Let \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\), \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\) and \(F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)/\Xi_\pi(0)\). List the zeros of \(\Xi_\pi\) as pairs \(\pm z_k\) with multiplicity, write \(z_k=i\gamma_k\), call \(t_k=-z_k^2=\gamma_k^2\) the Thorin atoms of \(\pi\), and put \(k_\pi(x)=\sum_ke^{-t_kx}\) and \(S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}\) for \(n\ge1\). A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(\exp(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,\tau(dt))\), \(s\ge0\), with drift \(a\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(\tau\), a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\); a Stieltjes function is a function on \((0,\infty)\) of the form \(a/s+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\sigma(dt)/(s+t)\) with \(a,b\ge0\) and \(\sigma\) a positive measure with \(\int\sigma(dt)/(1+t)<\infty\). The following are equivalent. (a) The generalized Riemann hypothesis holds for \(\pi\), that is, all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) lie on \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\) (equivalently, it holds for \(\tilde\pi\)). (b) \(s\mapsto1/F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(0)/\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (c) \(1/F_\pi\) is the Laplace transform of \(\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\), with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables: a GGC with drift zero and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\). (d) The L'evy function \(k_\pi(x)=\sum_ke^{xz_k^2}\), which converges for every \(x>0\), is completely monotone on \((0,\infty)\). (e) \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) has no real zero other than \(\frac12\), and \(F_\pi'/F_\pi\) is a Stieltjes function; equivalently (Herglotz criterion) \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) has no real zero other than \(\frac12\) and \(\operatorname{Im}(F_\pi'/F_\pi)(s)\le0\) whenever \(\operatorname{Im}s>0\) and \(F_\pi(s)\ne0\). (f) \((S_{j+1})_{j\ge0}\) is a Stieltjes moment sequence; equivalently (Thorin Hankel criterion) all Hankel matrices \((S_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^N\) and \((S_{i+j+2})_{i,j=0}^N\) are positive semidefinite. The same holds for the Riemann zeta function with \(\Xi_\zeta(z)=\xi(\frac12+z)\), \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)\), and, when \(\pi\cong\tilde\pi\), with \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r\) in place of \(\Xi_\pi\), in which case every Thorin atom has half the multiplicity.

Lemma 14.12, page 222 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, contragredient \(\tilde\pi\), \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\) and self dual completion \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\). There is a real, even, continuous function \(\Phi_\pi\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) with \(\int\Phi_\pi=1\) and constants \(c,C>0\) such that \(|\Phi_\pi(u)|\le C\exp(-ce^{c|u|})\) and \(\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0)=\int_{-\infty}^\infty\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}\,du\) for all \(z\in\mathbb{C}\).

Proposition 14.13, page 223 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, contragredient \(\tilde\pi\), \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\) and self dual completion \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\). List the zeros of \(\Xi_\pi\) as pairs \(\pm i\gamma_k\) with multiplicity, let \(t_k=\gamma_k^2\) and \(S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}\), and let \(\Phi_\pi\) be the P'olya kernel of \(\pi\), the real even continuous function with \(\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0)=\int\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}du\) for all complex \(z\). Suppose \(\Phi_\pi\ge0\) and let \(W_\pi\) be a random variable with density \(\Phi_\pi\) (the P'olya variable of \(\pi\)). Then the odd cumulants of \(W_\pi\) vanish and the even ones are \(\kappa_{2n}(W_\pi)/(2n)!=(-1)^{n+1}S_n/n\), \(n\ge1\). Consequently the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(\pi\) holds if and only if the sequence \(m_j=(-1)^j(j+1)\kappa_{2j+2}(W_\pi)/(2j+2)!\), \(j\ge0\), is a Stieltjes moment sequence (the sequence of moments \(\int u^j\nu(du)\) of a positive measure \(\nu\) on \([0,\infty)\)). In particular the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(\pi\) implies \((-1)^{n+1}\kappa_{2n}(W_\pi)>0\) for all \(n\).

Proposition 14.14, page 223 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the generalized Riemann hypothesis for L(s, pi), for the Laplace transform representation only (the slope limit is unconditional).
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\) with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with \(\pi\cong\tilde\pi\) (\(\tilde\pi\) the contragredient), completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\ge1\) and \(H(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r\). Unconditionally, \(\lim_{s\to0^+}d\log|\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt s,\pi)|/d\log s=r/2\). Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(\pi\), for \(s>0\), \(H(0)/\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt s,\pi)=s^{-r/2}\,\mathbb{E}e^{-sX}=\int_0^\infty e^{-sx}(m_r*\mu_X)(dx)\), where \(m_r(dx)=x^{r/2-1}dx/\Gamma(r/2)\) on \((0,\infty)\), \(X=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\) is the generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\) built from the zeros \(\pm i\gamma_k\) of \(H\) listed with multiplicity (\(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables), and \(\mu_X\) is the law of \(X\). The infinite measure \(m_r\) is the increasing limit as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) of \(\epsilon^{-r/2}\) times the gamma law of shape \(r/2\) and rate \(\epsilon\), whose Thorin measure is \(\frac r2\delta_\epsilon\): a Thorin atom of mass \(r/2\) escaping to the origin.

Theorem 14.17, page 226 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, self dual completion \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\) (\(\tilde\pi\) the contragredient, \(r\) the order of \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) at \(s=\frac12\)) and P'olya kernel \(\Phi_\pi\), the real even continuous function with \(|\Phi_\pi(u)|\le C\exp(-ce^{c|u|})\) for some \(c,C>0\) and \(\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0)=\int\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}du\) for all complex \(z\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\) let \(H_{\pi,\lambda}(t)=\int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{\lambda u^2}\Phi_\pi(u)e^{itu}\,du\). For \(\sigma\ge0\), condition \(\Theta_\sigma\) says that every zero \(z\) of \(\Xi_\pi\) satisfies \(|\operatorname{Re}z|\le\sigma\), equivalently that every zero of \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) lies in \(|\operatorname{Re}s-\frac12|\le\sigma\); let \(P_\sigma=\{x+iy:x\le\sigma^2-y^2/(4\sigma^2)\}\) for \(\sigma>0\) and \(P_0=(-\infty,0]\). Suppose \(\Theta_\sigma\) holds for \(\pi\) and let \(\lambda\ge0\). (i) (de Bruijn) The zeros of \(H_{\pi,\lambda}\) lie in \(|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\sigma_\lambda\), where \(\sigma_\lambda=(\max(\sigma^2-2\lambda,0))^{1/2}\); Gaussian tilting moves the Thorin atoms (the squares of the zeros of \(H_{\pi,\lambda}\)) from \(-P_\sigma\) into \(-P_{\sigma_\lambda}\), and for \(\lambda\ge\sigma^2/2\) all zeros of \(H_{\pi,\lambda}\) are real. (ii) If \(\Phi_\pi\ge0\), let \(W_{\pi,\lambda}\) have density proportional to \(e^{\lambda u^2}\Phi_\pi(u)\). For every \(\lambda\ge\sigma^2/2\) the function \(s\mapsto H_{\pi,\lambda}(0)/H_{\pi,\lambda}(i\sqrt s)=1/\mathbb{E}e^{\sqrt sW_{\pi,\lambda}}\) is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{x_k(\lambda)^2}\), where \(\pm x_k(\lambda)\) are the real zeros of \(H_{\pi,\lambda}\). Unconditionally (\(\sigma=\frac12\)), \(H_{\pi,\lambda}\) has only real zeros for every \(\lambda\ge\frac18\), and (ii) holds for these \(\lambda\).

Proposition 14.20, page 230 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E\) be an entire function, even, real on \(\mathbb{R}\), with \(E(0)=1\), of order at most two, whose zeros \(\pm z_k\) (listed with multiplicity) satisfy \(\sum_k|z_k|^{-4}<\infty\); let \(t_k=-z_k^2\) and \(F(s)=E(\sqrt s)\). Then \(F(s)=e^{bs}\prod_k(1+s/t_k)e^{-s/t_k}\) for some real \(b\), and the following are equivalent: (a) all \(t_k>0\); (b) for independent standard exponential variables \(E_k\) the series \(Y=b+\sum_k(E_k-1)/t_k\), which converges in \(L^2\), is real valued and satisfies \(1/F(s)=\mathbb{E}e^{-sY}\) for \(s\ge0\); (c) \(1/F\) agrees on \((0,\infty)\) with a function holomorphic and zero free on \(\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]\). The law of \(Y\) in (b) is infinitely divisible with L'evy measure \(x^{-1}\sum_ke^{-t_kx}dx\) on \((0,\infty)\); when \(\sum_kt_k^{-1}=\infty\) its first moment \(\int_0^1\sum_ke^{-t_kx}dx\) near the origin is infinite, which is why the centring is needed.

Theorem 15.3, page 237 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(L>0\) and \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), and put \(f_x(s)=(2-x)/(2\cosh(L\sqrt s)-x)\) for \(s>0\). Then \(f_x\) is the Laplace transform of a probability law on \([0,\infty)\) if and only if \(-2\le x<2\). In that case, writing \(x=2\cos\theta\) with \(0<\theta\le\pi\), the law is a generalized gamma convolution with drift \(0\) and Thorin measure \(\tau_{\theta,L}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{t_k}\), \(t_k=((\theta+2\pi k)/L)^2\), namely the law of \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}E_k/t_k\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables, with mean \(L^2/(2-x)\).
