Theorem 22.13, page 413 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Assume the following theorems, which are used and not reproved: the modularity of semistable elliptic curves over \(\mathbb{Q}\) (Wiles; Taylor and Wiles), Ribet’s level lowering theorem for weight two newforms with trivial character (Ribet), and Mazur’s torsion theorem (Mazur), which through an argument of Serre gives the positivity in (i) below. Let \(p\ge5\) be prime, suppose \(a^p+b^p=c^p\) with \(abc\ne0\), normalised so that \(\gcd(a,b,c)=1\), \(a\equiv -1\bmod 4\) and \(b\) is even, and let \(E\) be its Frey curve \(y^2=x(x - a^p)(x+b^p)\). Say that two systems of mod \(p\) Frobenius traces have zero discrepancy Thorin mass when the set of primes at which they differ has Dirichlet density zero, equivalently when the functional \((\sigma - 1)\sum_\ell e_\ell\log\ell\,\mathsf{1}\{\ell\text{ in that set}\}\) of a zeta distributed random integer, with \(e_\ell\) the exponent of \(\ell\), converges to \(0\) as \(\sigma\downarrow1\). Then the mod \(p\) representation \(\bar\rho_{E,p}\) would have zero discrepancy Thorin mass against some weight two Hecke eigensystem of level \(2\). But (i) against the Eisenstein system \(a_\ell=\ell+1\) the discrepancy is the Gamma law of shape \(c(E,p)>0\), where \(c(E,p)\) is the Haar measure of the set of elements without eigenvalue \(1\) in the image of \(\bar\rho_{E,p}\) in \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)\); and (ii) there is no cuspidal system, because the Hecke Thorin measure of level \(2\), the Thorin measure \(\sum_f\delta_{\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)}\) over the normalised eigenforms \(f\) of \(S_2(\Gamma_0(2))\), is empty. Hence there is no such solution.
Source: book/chapters/ch_flt.tex, label thm:flttwo.




Open Problem 22.1, page 416 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Give a probabilistic proof of the bound \(|a_\ell(f)|\le2\sqrt\ell\) of Eichler and Shimura with Weil for the Hecke eigenvalues \(a_\ell(f)\), \(\ell\ne N\) prime, of the weight two newforms \(f\) of prime level \(N\), for instance through hitting times or a heat kernel on the supersingular \(\ell\) isogeny graph in characteristic \(N\). The positivity of the Thorin atoms \(\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)\) of the Hecke generalized gamma convolution \(H_N(\ell)\), whose Thorin measure is \(\sum_f\delta_{\ell+1 - a_\ell(f)}\), needs only \(a_\ell(f)<\ell+1\), which the Perron Frobenius theorem gives; the bound itself gives the Hasse Weil bounds on the Kemeny constants and spanning tree counts of the isogeny graphs. Compare the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture for Maass forms, where no geometric proof is available.
Source: book/chapters/ch_flt.tex, label op:flthasse.




Open Problem 22.2, page 416 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. The Taylor Wiles method chooses, for each \(n\), finite sets of auxiliary primes \(q\equiv 1\bmod p^n\) at which \(\bar\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_q)\) has distinct eigenvalues, where \(\bar\rho\) is the residual mod \(p\) Galois representation; by Chebotarev’s theorem and the hitting rate theorem for the largest prime factors of a zeta distributed random integer \(N_\sigma\), \(\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)\), such primes occur among the large prime factors of \(N_\sigma\) at a positive rate. Is there a formulation of the patching argument in which the auxiliary sets are the atoms of the Gamma process (the Poisson limit, as \(\sigma\downarrow1\), of the rescaled sizes \((\sigma - 1)\log q\) of the prime factors \(q\) of \(N_\sigma\) together with their Frobenius labels) in a fixed Chebotarev class, and the patched objects are limits in law as \(\sigma\downarrow1\)?
Source: book/chapters/ch_flt.tex, label op:fltpatch.




Open Problem 22.3, page 416 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For an elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb{Q}\) and a prime \(p\) let the Eisenstein Thorin shape \(c(E,p)\) be the Haar measure of the set of elements without eigenvalue \(1\) in the image of the mod \(p\) Galois representation of \(E\) in \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)\), equivalently the density of the primes \(\ell\) with \(p\nmid|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|\). Serre’s argument from Mazur’s torsion theorem gives \(c(E,p)>0\) for \(p\ge5\) and every curve with \(E[2]\subset E(\mathbb{Q})\). One rational point of order \(2\) is not enough: the semistable curve \(y^2+xy=x^3 - 45x+81\) of conductor \(66\) has torsion \(\mathbb{Z}/10\), so \(c(E,5)=0\). Is there a proof of this positivity through the Gamma law of the Eisenstein discrepancy, the limit law with shape \(c(E,p)\) of the functional \((\sigma - 1)\sum_\ell e_\ell\log\ell\,\mathsf{1}\{p\nmid|E(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|\}\) of a zeta distributed random integer with exponents \(e_\ell\), and the supersingular isogeny walks? Such a proof must use an input special to \(\mathbb{Q}\): over some quadratic fields there are curves with torsion \(\mathbb{Z}/2\times\mathbb{Z}/10\), whose analogue of the Eisenstein shape at \(5\), over the primes of the field, vanishes.
Source: book/chapters/ch_flt.tex, label op:fltmazur.







Theorem 23.5, page 424 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\nu=\sum_jc_j\delta_{x_j}\) be a discrete signed measure with distinct atoms \(x_j>0\) and \(\sum_j|c_j|<\infty\), and let \(g(r)=\int(1-\cos rx)\,\nu(dx)\). For \(R>0\) and a function \(h\) on \([0,\infty)\) write \(\mathcal{G}_R[h]=\int_0^\infty h(r)e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\big/\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\). Then for every \(k\) [ _R=_jc_j, ] so that, with \(\delta_k=\min\bigl(x_k,\inf_{j\ne k}|x_j-x_k|\bigr)\) assumed positive, [ |c_k+2_R|(_j|c_j|)e^{-_k2R2/2}. ] In particular \(c_k=-2\lim_{R\to\infty}\mathcal{G}_R[g(r)\cos(rx_k)]\), the same limit holds for the plain Bohr mean, that is \(c_k=-2\lim_{R\to\infty}\frac1R\int_0^Rg(r)\cos(rx_k)\,dr\), and the map \(\nu\mapsto g\) is injective.
Source: book/chapters/ch_laplace.tex, label thm:lapbohr.




Corollary 23.6, page 425 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(L(s)=\sum_na_nn^{-s}\) have an Euler product with \(-L'/L(s)=\sum_n\Lambda_L(n)n^{-s}\) absolutely convergent for \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\), as for Artin L functions and, by the Rankin Selberg method of Jacquet and Shalika and the Cauchy Schwarz inequality, for cuspidal automorphic ones. For \(\alpha>1\) let [ g_(r)=_{n}(1-(rn)) ] be the transported density, which equals \(\operatorname{Re}\frac{L'}{L}(\alpha+ir)-\frac{L'}{L}(\alpha)\) when the \(\Lambda_L(n)\) are real, and for \(R>0\) let \(\mathcal{G}_R[h]=\int_0^\infty h(r)e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\big/\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\). Then for \(n\ge2\) [ L(n)=-2n^{R}_R, ] and the error at a finite \(R\) is at most [ 2n^(_m|_L(m)|m{-})e{-_n2R2/2},_n=(1+1/n). ] If \(L=L(s,\rho)\) for an Artin representation \(\rho\) unramified at \(p\), then \(\Lambda_L=\Lambda_\rho\) and \(\operatorname{tr}\rho(\operatorname{Frob}_p^m)=\Lambda_\rho(p^m)/\log p\), so, since two such Euler products whose transported densities agree on an interval of \(r\) have the same coefficients, the transported density on any interval of \(r\) determines every Frobenius trace.
Source: book/chapters/ch_laplace.tex, label cor:lapfrob.




Theorem 23.9, page 429 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. First stated in Polson (2017, version 26 of 2026), On Hilbert’s 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be self dual, and let \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(w)\) be the completed L function \(\Lambda(\tfrac12+w,\pi)\) divided by the power of \(w\) that removes any zero at \(w=0\); for the Riemann zeta function use \(\Xi_\zeta(w)=\xi(\tfrac12+w)\) in its place. This function is even and entire of order at most one; its zeros \(z=\beta+i\gamma\), counted with multiplicity, form a multiset \(\mathcal{Z}\) closed under \(z\mapsto-z\) and \(z\mapsto\bar z\), and \(|\beta|<\tfrac12\). Let \(C\) be a standard Cauchy variable, with density \(1/(\pi(1+x^2))\). Let \(a>|\beta|\) for every \(z=\beta+i\gamma\) in \(\mathcal{Z}\); this holds unconditionally for \(a\ge\tfrac12\). Let \(H_a\) be the generalized gamma convolution with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-sH_a}=\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(a)/\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(a+\sqrt s)\) and \(V_a\) its Thorin density. In the variable \(r>0\), the square root of the Thorin variable, the Thorin measure of \(H_a\) is [ V_a(r^2),2r,dr=_{z}(|+(a-)C|)(dr),r>0. ] Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis this is \(\sum_{\gamma>0}\mathrm{Law}(|\gamma+aC|)\) for every \(a>0\), a superposition of folded Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates with common scale \(a\). For \(b>0\), \(V_{a+b}\) is obtained from \(V_a\) by adding independent Cauchy noise of scale \(b\) before folding, and, for \(a>\tfrac12\), this is multiplication by \(e^{-bx}\) of the whole Lévy measure of \(\log\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi\) at basepoint \(a\), archimedean and polynomial factors included.
Source: book/chapters/ch_laplace.tex, label thm:lapcauchy.




Theorem 23.12, page 436 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(G\) be a compact connected simply connected Lie group, such as \(\mathrm{SU}(2)\) or \(\mathrm{USp}(2n)\), with alcove \(\mathcal{A}\), positive roots \(\alpha\) and half sum of the positive roots \(\rho_G\), the Lie algebra of a maximal torus carrying the invariant inner product in which, for \(\mathrm{SU}(2)\) and \(\mathrm{USp}(2n)\), the eigenvalue angles are orthonormal coordinates. Let \(f_G=c|\Delta_G|^2\) on \(\mathcal{A}\), with \(\Delta_G=\prod_{\alpha>0}(e^{i\alpha/2}-e^{-i\alpha/2})\) and \(c\) a normalising constant, be the Sato Tate law, the image of Haar measure on conjugacy classes. Among densities \(f\) on \(\mathcal{A}\) such that \(\sqrt f\) vanishes on the boundary \(\partial\mathcal{A}\) and \(\int_{\mathcal{A}}|\nabla\sqrt f|^2<\infty\), the Good and Gaskins roughness \(\int_{\mathcal{A}}|\nabla\sqrt f|^2\), one quarter of the trace of the Fisher information for location, is at least \(|\rho_G|^2\), with equality exactly for the Sato Tate law \(f_G\). For \(G=\mathrm{SU}(2)\), with \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\) and \(\sqrt f=\sqrt{2/\pi}\sum_jb_j\sin j\theta\), \(\sum_jb_j^2=1\), [ _0((f)’)2d=_jj2b_j2,=^{j-1}
\[\begin{pmatrix}e^{i\theta}&0\\0&e^{-i\theta}\end{pmatrix}\]
, ] so the roughness is the Laplace eigenvalue energy \(\sum_\lambda|\lambda+\rho_G|^2b_\lambda^2\), which is \(|\rho_G|^2\) plus the Casimir energy, in the basis of symmetric power characters, and the Sato Tate law is \(b=e_1\). Given angles \(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n\), put \(\hat m_j=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Sym}^{j-1}(\theta_i)\), the trace being that of the matrix above at \(\theta=\theta_i\). Near the Sato Tate law, the maximiser of \(\frac1n\sum_i\log f(\theta_i)-\omega\int_0^\pi\bigl((\sqrt f)'\bigr)^2d\theta\) over \(\sqrt f=\sqrt{2/\pi}\sum_{j\le J}b_j\sin j\theta\) satisfies [ b_j=+O(_{2l2J-1}m_l^2),jJ. ]
Source: book/chapters/ch_laplace.tex, label thm:lapgg.




Open Problem 23.1, page 438 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(L\) have an Euler product with \(-L'/L(s)=\sum_n\Lambda_L(n)n^{-s}\) absolutely convergent for \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\), and for \(\alpha>1\) let \(g_\alpha(r)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_L(n)n^{-\alpha}\bigl(1-\cos(r\log n)\bigr)\) be its transported density. The restriction of \(g_\alpha\) to any interval \([0,r_0)\) determines every \(\Lambda_L(n)\), but only through analytic continuation, which is unstable. Suppose \(g_\alpha\) is known on \([0,r_1]\) to within \(\eta\). The Gaussian means \(-2n^\alpha\mathcal{G}_R[g_\alpha(r)\cos(r\log n)]\), with \(\mathcal{G}_R[h]=\int_0^\infty h(r)e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\big/\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/(2R^2)}\,dr\) truncated at \(r_1\), recover \(\Lambda_L(n)\) to within \(\varepsilon\) once \(\eta\) is of order \(\varepsilon n^{-\alpha}\) and \(r_1\) of order \(n\log(n^\alpha/\varepsilon)\). Is an interval of length of order \(n\), the reciprocal of the gap \(\log(1+1/n)\) between the frequencies \(\log n\) and \(\log(n+1)\), necessary for every stable method, as Ingham’s inequality for nonharmonic Fourier series suggests? A positive answer would be an uncertainty principle for the Galois face, comparable with the bounds in effective Chebotarev theorems.
Source: book/chapters/ch_laplace.tex, label op:lapwindow.




Open Problem 23.2, page 438 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. The inversions of the transported density and of the Thorin law of an L function are exact but need exact input. Treat the ordinates \(0<\gamma_1\le\dots\le\gamma_K\) of its zeros as a sample from the normalised counting measure of the zeros, or the transported density \(g_\alpha(r)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_L(n)n^{-\alpha}\bigl(1-\cos(r\log n)\bigr)\), \(\alpha>1\), on a grid as noisy data; define the penalised likelihood of Good and Gaskins for the square root of the Thorin density \(U_\alpha(z)=g_\alpha(\sqrt z)/(2\pi\sqrt z)\), or for the density of the Thorin variable \(H\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-sH}=e^{b\sqrt s}L(\alpha)/L(\alpha+\sqrt s)\), \(b=\frac{L'}{L}(\alpha)\); identify its maximiser, as de Montricher, Tapia and Thompson did for the classical penalised likelihood; and compare its error with that of the Gaussian mean inversion of the transported density on the same input.
Source: book/chapters/ch_laplace.tex, label op:lapgg.







Theorem 24.3, page 448 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(Y\) be a compact metric space, \(\mu\) a probability measure on \(Y\), and \((\theta_p)\) labels in \(Y\) attached to the primes and equidistributed with respect to \(\mu\) outside a finite set \(S\) of primes (for Frobenius classes in a finite Galois group, \(\mu\) is the image of Haar measure on the set of conjugacy classes and Chebotarev’s theorem supplies the hypothesis). For \(\sigma>1\) let \(N_\sigma\) be the zeta random integer, \(\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)\), with prime exponents \(e_p\), let \(\Xi_\sigma=\sum_{p\notin S}(\sigma-1)e_p\log p\,\delta_{\theta_p}\) be its labelled factorisation, and let \(A_\sigma\) be the event that \(N_\sigma\) has no prime factor outside \(S\). The Dirichlet process with base measure \(\mu\) is the random probability measure \(\Gamma_\mu/\Gamma_\mu(Y)\), with \(\Gamma_\mu\) the Gamma random measure with shape measure \(\mu\). As \(\sigma\downarrow1\): (i) the normalised labelled factorisation \(\mathcal{P}_\sigma=\Xi_\sigma/\Xi_\sigma(Y)\), set equal to \(\mu\) on \(A_\sigma\), converges in law, as a random probability measure on \(Y\) with the weak topology, to the Dirichlet process \(P\) with base measure \(\mu\), and jointly with it the total mass \(\Xi_\sigma(Y)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{p\notin S}e_p\log p\) converges to a standard exponential variable \(E\) independent of \(P\); (ii) for every continuous \(Q\ge0\) on \(Y\) the Frobenius functional \(\Xi_\sigma(Q)\) converges in law to \(E\int_YQ\,dP\), a standard exponential variable times a Dirichlet mean, and for \(\lambda\ge0\) [ (-,E_YQ,dP)=(1+_YQ,dP)^{-1}=(-_Y(1+Q),d); ] (iii) for a partition of \(Y\) into \(\mu\) continuity sets \(B_1,\dots,B_k\) with \(\mu(B_i)>0\), the shares \(\mathcal{P}_\sigma(B_i)\) converge jointly in law to the Dirichlet law with parameters \(\mu(B_1),\dots,\mu(B_k)\), so that each share \(\mathcal{P}_\sigma(B)\) converges to a Beta variable with parameters \((\mu(B),1-\mu(B))\), of mean \(\mu(B)\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label thm:pddirichlet.




Theorem 24.4, page 451 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Fix \(\vartheta>0\), let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on a compact metric space \(Y\) and \((\theta_p)\) labels in \(Y\) equidistributed with respect to \(\mu\) outside a finite set \(S\) of primes, and let \(d_\vartheta(n)\) be the Dirichlet coefficients of \(\zeta(s)^\vartheta\), multiplicative with \(d_\vartheta(p^k)=\binom{\vartheta+k-1}{k}\). For \(\sigma>1\) let the random integer \(N_\sigma^{(\vartheta)}\) have the law \(d_\vartheta(n)n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)^\vartheta\), with prime exponents \(e_p\), and let \(\Xi^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma=\sum_{p\notin S}(\sigma-1)e_p\log p\,\delta_{\theta_p}\) be its labelled factorisation. Then the prime exponents are independent negative binomial variables, \(\mathbb{P}(e_p=k)=\binom{\vartheta+k-1}{k}(1-p^{-\sigma})^\vartheta p^{-k\sigma}\), and as \(\sigma\downarrow1\): (i) the marked process \(\sum_{p\notin S,\,e_p\ge1}\delta_{((\sigma-1)e_p\log p,\,\theta_p)}\) converges in law, vaguely on \((0,\infty)\times Y\), to the Poisson process with intensity \(\vartheta x^{-1}e^{-x}dx\otimes\mu\); (ii) the labelled factorisation \(\Xi^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma\) converges in law to the Gamma random measure \(\Gamma_{\vartheta\mu}\) with shape measure \(\vartheta\mu\), its total mass, which is \((\sigma-1)\log N^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma\) up to the primes in \(S\), to a Gamma variable with shape \(\vartheta\), and the normalised factorisation to the Dirichlet process \(\Gamma_{\vartheta\mu}/\Gamma_{\vartheta\mu}(Y)\) with base measure \(\vartheta\mu\); (iii) the ranked normalised sizes of the prime factors converge to the Poisson Dirichlet law \(\mathrm{PD}(\vartheta)\), and for every continuous \(Q\ge0\) on \(Y\) the functional \(\Xi^{(\vartheta)}_\sigma(Q)\) converges to a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin measure \(\vartheta\) times the image of \(\mu\) restricted to \(\{Q>0\}\) under \(1/Q\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label thm:pdtheta.




Theorem 24.5, page 452 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(K/\mathbb{Q}\) be a finite Galois extension with group \(G\), let \(C\subset G\) be a conjugacy class with \(\delta(C)=|C|/|G|\), write \(p\in C\) when the Frobenius class of the unramified prime \(p\) is \(C\), and leave the ramified primes out of every class. Let \(n\) be uniform on \(\{2,\dots,x\}\) with prime factorisation \(n=\prod_pp^{e_p}\), and call a prime factor \(p\) of \(n\) chosen with probability \(e_p\log p/\log n\) a size biased prime factor. By the prime number theorem for \(K\) in the form \(\pi_C(t)=\delta(C)\operatorname{li}(t)+O\bigl(t\exp(-a_K\sqrt{\log t})\bigr)\) of Lagarias and Odlyzko, with \(\pi_C(t)\) the number of primes \(p\le t\) in \(C\) and \(a_K>0\) a constant depending on \(K\), the limit \(c_C=\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p\in C}\frac{\log p}{p}-\delta(C)\log t\bigr)\) exists. Let \(\kappa_C=-c_C-\sum_{p\in C}\frac{\log p}{p(p-1)}\), which by the Abelian theorem is the Euler Kronecker drift of the class \(C\) for the set of ramified primes, so that \(\sum_C\bigl(\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\delta(C)-\kappa_C\bigr)=-\sum_{p\text{ ramified}}\frac{\log p}{p-1}\), with \(\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\) Euler’s constant. Then, as \(x\to\infty\), the size biased prime factor lies in \(C\) with probability [ (C)++O((x)^{-2}). ]
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label thm:pdmertens.




Theorem 24.6, page 455 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(K/\mathbb{Q}\) be a finite Galois extension with group \(G\), and for a conjugacy class \(C\) of \(G\) let \(\delta(C)=|C|/|G|\). Let \(n\) be uniform on \(\{2,\dots,x\}\) with prime factorisation \(n=\prod_pp^{e_p}\), let \(p^*\) be a size biased prime factor of \(n\), chosen with probability \(e_p\log p/\log n\), and let \(F^*=e_{p^*}\log p^*/\log n\) be its share. As \(x\to\infty\), \(p^*\) is unramified with probability tending to \(1\), and the pair \((F^*,\text{Frobenius class of }p^*)\) converges in law to the product of the uniform law on \((0,1)\) and the law \(C\mapsto\delta(C)\) on the conjugacy classes. The same holds for the zeta random integer \(N_\sigma\), \(\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)\), as \(\sigma\downarrow1\), for a finite set \(S\) of primes containing the ramified ones: off the event \(A_\sigma\) that \(N_\sigma\) has no prime factor outside \(S\), pick \(p^*\) among the prime factors of \(N_\sigma\) outside \(S\), with probability proportional to \(e_p\log p\), \(e_p\) now the exponent of \(p\) in \(N_\sigma\), and take its share relative to their part \(\sum_{p\notin S}e_p\log p\) of \(\log N_\sigma\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label thm:pdsizebiased.




Theorem 24.8, page 458 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(K/\mathbb{Q}\) be a finite Galois extension with nontrivial group \(G\), \(S\) the set of ramified primes, \(C\) a conjugacy class with \(\delta(C)=|C|/|G|\), and \(\delta_{\min}=\min_C\delta(C)\). For \(\sigma>1\) let \(N_\sigma\) be the zeta random integer, \(\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)\), with prime exponents \(e_p\); let \(L_C(\sigma)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{p\notin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}e_p\log p\) be the mass of the class \(C\); let \(A_\sigma\) be the event that \(N_\sigma\) has no prime factor outside \(S\); and let \(\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)\) be the share of \(C\), equal to \(L_C(\sigma)/\sum_{C'}L_{C'}(\sigma)\) off \(A_\sigma\) and to \(\delta(C)\) on \(A_\sigma\). Let \(P_C(s)=\sum_{p\notin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}\sum_{m\ge1}p^{-ms}/m\); the function \(h_C(s)=P_C(s)-\delta(C)\log\frac1{s-1}\) is real analytic near \(s=1\), and \(h_C(1)=b_C-\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\delta(C)+\sum_{p\notin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}\sum_{m\ge2}\frac{p^{-m}}{m}\), where \(b_C=\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p\notin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}\frac1p-\delta(C)\log\log t\bigr)\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{E}}\) is Euler’s constant. (i) \(\mathbb{P}(L_C(\sigma)=0)=e^{-P_C(\sigma)}=e^{-h_C(1)}(\sigma-1)^{\delta(C)}\bigl(1+O(\sigma-1)\bigr)\). (ii) The Kolmogorov distance between the law of \(\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)\) and its limit \(\mathrm{Beta}(\delta(C),1-\delta(C))\) is at least [ (L_C()=0)-(A_)=e{-h_C(1)}(){(C)}(1+o(1)), ] hence at least of order \((\sigma-1)^{\delta_{\min}}\) for the smallest class.
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label thm:pdrate.




Theorem 24.9, page 460 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(D(s)=\sum_na(n)n^{-s}=\exp\bigl(\sum_p\sum_{m\ge1}w_m(p)p^{-ms}/m\bigr)\) be an Euler product with \(w_m(p)\ge0\) bounded, and suppose the labels \((\theta_p)\) are equidistributed with respect to a probability measure \(\mu\) on a compact metric space \(Y\) and \(w_1(p)=w(\theta_p)\) outside a finite set \(S\) of primes, for a continuous \(w\ge0\) on \(Y\) with \(\int w\,d\mu>0\). For \(\sigma>1\) let \(N^D_\sigma\) have the law \(a(n)n^{-\sigma}/D(\sigma)\), with prime exponents \(e_p\). Then the prime exponents of \(N^D_\sigma\) are independent, \(e_p=\sum_mmM(p^m)\) with independent Poisson variables \(M(p^m)\) of means \(w_m(p)p^{-m\sigma}/m\), and as \(\sigma\downarrow1\) the labelled factorisation \(\sum_{p\notin S}(\sigma-1)e_p\log p\,\delta_{\theta_p}\) converges in law to the Gamma random measure with shape measure \(w\mu\), the normalised factorisation to the Dirichlet process with base measure \(w\mu\), and the ranked normalised sizes of the prime factors to the Poisson Dirichlet law \(\mathrm{PD}(\vartheta)\) with [ =Yw,d={s}, ] the order of the pole of \(D\) at \(s=1\) when \(D\) continues meromorphically. In particular, for \(D=L(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho)\) with \(\rho\) an Artin representation, \(w=|\chi_\rho|^2\) and \(\vartheta=\langle\rho,\rho\rangle\), the shape of the Gamma limit of the Rankin Selberg random integer; and for \(D=\zeta_K\) with \(K/\mathbb{Q}\) of degree \(n\) and Galois closure of group \(G\) acting on the \(n\) embeddings, \(w(g)\) is the number of fixed points of \(g\) and \(\vartheta=1\) by Burnside’s lemma.
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label thm:pdewens.




Open Problem 24.1, page 463 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(K/\mathbb{Q}\) be a finite Galois extension with nontrivial group \(G\) and set of ramified primes \(S\), let \(C\) run over the conjugacy classes, with \(\delta(C)=|C|/|G|\) and \(\delta_{\min}=\min_C\delta(C)\), and for the zeta random integer \(N_\sigma\), \(\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)\), with prime exponents \(e_p\), let \(\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)\) be the share of the class \(C\), the proportion of \(\sum_{p\notin S}e_p\log p\) carried by the primes with Frobenius in \(C\) (set to \(\delta(C)\) when \(N_\sigma\) has no prime factor outside \(S\)). As \(\sigma\downarrow1\) the vector of shares converges to the Dirichlet law with parameters \(\delta(C)\), and in the Kolmogorov distance of the shares the limit is approached no faster than \((\sigma-1)^{\delta_{\min}}\). Prove the matching upper bound: that the Kolmogorov distance between the law of \(\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C)\) and \(\mathrm{Beta}(\delta(C),1-\delta(C))\) is \(O\bigl((\sigma-1)^{\delta(C)}\bigr)\), and that, for the Euclidean distance between share vectors, the Wasserstein distance between the laws of \((\mathcal{P}_\sigma(C))_C\) and of its Dirichlet limit is \(O\bigl((\sigma-1)\log\frac1{\sigma-1}\bigr)\), the order at which the means converge.
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label op:pdrate.




Open Problem 24.2, page 463 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For a finite Galois extension \(K/\mathbb{Q}\) with group \(G\) and set of ramified primes \(S\), the Mertens constants per class \(b_C=\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p\notin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}\frac1p-\delta(C)\log\log t\bigr)\) and \(c_C=\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{p\le t,\,p\notin S,\,\mathrm{Frob}_p\in C}\frac{\log p}{p}-\delta(C)\log t\bigr)\), with \(\delta(C)=|C|/|G|\), are expressed through the values \(L(1,\chi)\) and \(\frac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)\) of the Artin L functions of the irreducible characters \(\chi\) of \(G\). For the splitting field of a polynomial of degree \(n\) with group \(S_n\), the deficit of the identity class, which governs the share of that class among the distinct unramified prime factors of a uniform random integer, is \(b_{\{1\}}-\delta(\{1\})B'=\lim_{t\to\infty}\sum_{p\le t,\,p\notin S}\bigl(\mathsf{1}_{\{1\}}(\mathrm{Frob}_p)-\delta(\{1\})\bigr)/p\), where \(B'=B-\sum_{p\in S}1/p\) and \(B\) is the Mertens constant; it is negative for \(x^3-x-1\), whose smallest completely split prime is \(59\). A prime \(p<n\) splits completely only if it divides the index of \(\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]\), with \(\alpha\) a root of the polynomial, and this happens: in Dedekind’s field of \(x^3-x^2-2x-8\) the prime \(2\) splits completely and adds \(\frac5{12}\) to the sum. Read from the primes below \(10^7\), the deficit is positive for Dedekind’s field and for \(x^3-x+15\), in which \(3\) and \(5\) split completely, so both signs occur already with group \(S_3\). Determine the distribution of the sign of the deficit over the fields with group \(S_n\) ordered by discriminant, and its sign along a family such as \(x^n-x-1\). This is the analogue, for the weights \(1/p\), of the problem of the signs of the Euler Kronecker drifts.
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label op:pdmertens.




Open Problem 24.3, page 463 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For a finite Galois extension with labels \(\theta_p\) the Frobenius classes, equidistributed with respect to the image \(\mu\) of Haar measure, and the zeta random integer \(N_\sigma\), \(\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma=n)=n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)\), with prime exponents \(e_p\), the Frobenius functional of a function \(Q\ge0\) on the classes is \(\Xi_\sigma(Q)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{p}e_p\log p\,Q(\theta_p)\), the sum over the unramified primes; as \(\sigma\downarrow1\) it converges to a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin measure the image of \(\mu\) restricted to \(\{Q>0\}\) under \(1/Q\). By Bondesson the product of two independent generalized gamma convolution variables is a generalized gamma convolution, so the product of independent copies of the limits of \(\Xi_\sigma(Q_1)\) and \(\Xi_\sigma(Q_2)\) is one, with a Thorin measure \(\tau_{Q_1,Q_2}\). Multiplying Dirichlet series realises the additive closure, the Frobenius functional of the product of two independent random integers being the sum of two independent ones, and tensor products, as in Rankin Selberg convolution, give the functional of \(Q_1Q_2\). Find the arithmetic operation, if any, that realises the multiplicative closure, a representation or an L function whose Frobenius functional has Thorin measure \(\tau_{Q_1,Q_2}\); and compute \(\tau_{Q_1,Q_2}\) for \(Q_1=Q_2=\operatorname{tr}^2\), the squared trace of the two dimensional irreducible representation of \(S_3\). For a finite group the Thorin measure of a limiting Frobenius functional is finitely supported and that of such a product is not, so the operation, if any, leads to an infinite label space, such as a Sato Tate group.
Source: book/chapters/ch_pd.tex, label op:pdproduct.







Theorem 25.7, page 476 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E/\mathbb{Q}\) be an elliptic curve of conductor \(N_E\), \(\rho\) its normalised \(\ell\) adic representation, \(K\) an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant \(d_K\) and \(\chi_K\) its quadratic character. For \(\sigma > 1\) let \(X_\sigma\) be the Rankin Selberg subordinator of \(\rho\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\), the nonnegative random variable with Laplace transform \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda X_\sigma} = D^S(\sigma+\lambda)/D^S(\sigma)\), \(\lambda \ge 0\), where \(D^S(s) = L^S(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho)\) is the Rankin Selberg L function with the Euler factors at the primes dividing \(N_E d_K\) removed, and let \(X^K_\sigma\) be the same subordinator built over \(K\), with Laplace transform \(D^S_K(\sigma+\lambda)/D^S_K(\sigma)\), where \(D^S_K(s) = L^S_K(s,\rho|_K\otimes\check\rho|_K)\) is the Euler product over the primes of \(K\) not dividing \(N_E d_K\) attached to the restriction of \(\rho\) to \(\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/K)\). (i) \(D^S_K(s) = D^S(s)\,L^S(s,\rho\otimes\check\rho\otimes\chi_K)\), the partial products being over the primes not dividing \(N_E d_K\). (ii) If \(E\) has complex multiplication by \(K\) then \(D^S_K(s) = D^S(s)^2\) exactly, so that \(X^K_\sigma\) has the law of the sum of two independent copies of \(X_\sigma\) for every \(\sigma > 1\), and \((\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma\) converges in law as \(\sigma \downarrow 1\) to the Gamma law of shape \(2\) and scale \(1\). (iii) If \(E\) has no complex multiplication by \(K\) then \((\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma\) converges in law as \(\sigma \downarrow 1\) to the standard exponential law, the Gamma shape being \(1\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_gl1.tex, label thm:gl1cmshape.




Theorem 25.8, page 478 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\chi\) be a primitive real Dirichlet character modulo \(q \ge 3\) and \(\kappa \in \{0,1\}\) its parity, so that \(\Lambda(s,\chi) = (q/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+\kappa}{2})L(s,\chi)\) satisfies \(\Lambda(s,\chi) = \Lambda(1-s,\chi)\). Put \(\Xi_\chi(w) = \Lambda(\frac12+w,\chi)\), an even entire function of order one, and write its zeros, with multiplicity, as the pairs \(\pm i\gamma_k\), one \(\gamma_k\) taken from each pair (only \(\gamma_k^2\) enters below). Suppose \(L(\frac12,\chi) \ne 0\). Then \(\Xi_\chi(\sqrt\lambda)/\Xi_\chi(0) = \prod_k(1+\lambda/\gamma_k^2)\) for \(\lambda \ge 0\), the product converging absolutely, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,\chi)\) holds if and only if \(\lambda \mapsto \Xi_\chi(0)/\Xi_\chi(\sqrt\lambda)\) is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, in which case the Thorin measure is \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\) and the generalized gamma convolution is \(\sum_k E_k/\gamma_k^2\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential random variables. Moreover, without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis, for every \(a \ge \frac12\) (basepoint \(\frac12+a \ge 1\)) the function \(V_a(z) = \operatorname{Re}(\Xi_\chi'/\Xi_\chi)(a+i\sqrt z)/(2\pi\sqrt z)\), \(z > 0\), is nonnegative and \(\Xi_\chi(a)/\Xi_\chi(a+\sqrt\lambda) = \mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda H_a}\) for \(\lambda > 0\), where \(H_a\) is a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin density \(V_a\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_gl1.tex, label thm:gl1thorin.




Open Problem 25.1, page 481 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For a prime \(p \equiv 1 \pmod 4\) write \(p = \pi\bar\pi\) with \(\pi\) a primary Gaussian prime (\(\pi \equiv 1\) modulo \(2+2i\)) and let \(\theta_p = |\arg\pi| \in [0,\pi]\); by Hecke’s theorem the angles \(4\theta_p\) are equidistributed modulo \(2\pi\). Let \(\pi_1(x)\) be the number of primes \(p \le x\) with \(p \equiv 1 \pmod 4\) and \(D(x)\) the discrepancy of the angles \(4\theta_p\), \(p \le x\), from the uniform law. Determine whether \(\sqrt{\pi_1(x)}\,D(x)\) has a limit law as \(x \to \infty\) (the Kolmogorov law would be the Brownian bridge prediction, as for the discrepancy of Sato Tate angles), or whether the arithmetic of the Hecke L functions \(L(s,\lambda_k)\), \(\lambda_k((\alpha)) = (\alpha/|\alpha|)^{4k}\), forces a different law; and the same question for the imaginary quadratic fields of class number one.
Source: book/chapters/ch_gl1.tex, label op:gl1disc.




Open Problem 25.2, page 481 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(N_\sigma\) be the zeta distributed random integer, \(\mathbb{P}(N_\sigma = n) = n^{-\sigma}/\zeta(\sigma)\), and colour each prime factor \(p \equiv 1 \pmod 4\) by its Hecke angle \(4\theta_p\) on the circle, where \(\theta_p = |\arg\pi|\) for a primary Gaussian prime \(\pi\) dividing \(p\); as \(\sigma \downarrow 1\) the labelled factorisation converges to a Dirichlet process whose base measure is \(\frac12\) times the uniform probability on the circle. The rate of convergence of this Dirichlet process is governed, for the means, by the constants \((L'/L)(1,\lambda_k)\) of the Hecke L functions of the characters \(\lambda_k((\alpha)) = (\alpha/|\alpha|)^{4k}\) of \(\mathbb{Q}(i)\), in the same way that the drift of the Frobenius Gamma process of a finite Galois extension is governed by Euler Kronecker constants. Compute these constants for \(\mathbb{Q}(i)\) and \(k \le 20\), determine the sign pattern of the deficits of the arcs (the differences between the mean shares of the arcs and their limiting values), and find the analogue for the circle, where no arc is a finite union of classes, of the theorem giving the atoms at zero and a lower bound for the rate of convergence of the shares of the classes.
Source: book/chapters/ch_gl1.tex, label op:gl1rate.




Open Problem 25.3, page 481 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(E/\mathbb{Q}\) be an elliptic curve of conductor \(N_E\) with normalised \(\ell\) adic representation \(\rho\), \(K\) an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant \(d_K\) with quadratic character \(\chi_K\), and \(X^K_\sigma\) the Rankin Selberg subordinator of \(\rho\) over \(K\), the nonnegative random variable with Laplace transform \(D^S_K(\sigma+\lambda)/D^S_K(\sigma)\), where \(D^S_K(s) = L^S_K(s,\rho|_K\otimes\check\rho|_K)\) is the Rankin Selberg Euler product over the primes of \(K\) not dividing \(N_E d_K\) attached to the restriction \(\rho|_K\) of \(\rho\) to \(\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/K)\), so that as \(\sigma \downarrow 1\) the law of \((\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma\) tends to the Gamma law of shape \(2\) if \(E\) has complex multiplication by \(K\) and of shape \(1\) otherwise. By Faltings’ theorem finitely many \(a_p\) determine \(\rho\) up to isomorphism, so finitely many primes decide whether \(\rho\otimes\chi_K \cong \rho\). Find an explicit bound, in terms of \(N_E\) and \(d_K\), on the primes needed so that the empirical Laplace transform of \((\sigma-1)X^K_\sigma\) at a suitable \(\sigma\) separates shape \(1\) from shape \(2\) with a proof, and compare with the bound from the effective Chebotarev theorem.
Source: book/chapters/ch_gl1.tex, label op:gl1cm.







Corollary 26.1, page 486 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(u\) be a Hecke Maass eigenform with Hecke eigenvalue \(\lambda(p)\) at the prime \(p\), and \(L_p(s,u) = (1-\lambda(p)p^{-s}+p^{-2s})^{-1}\) its Euler factor at \(p\). The function \(s \mapsto \frac{2-\lambda(p)}{p^{\sqrt s}+p^{-\sqrt s}-\lambda(p)} = (2-\lambda(p))\,p^{-\sqrt s}L_p(\sqrt s,u)\), \(s > 0\), is the Laplace transform of a probability law on \([0,\infty)\) if and only if \(-2 \le \lambda(p) < 2\), in which case, writing \(\lambda(p) = 2\cos\theta_p\) with \(0 < \theta_p \le \pi\), the law is the generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure (Thorin comb) \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{t_k}\), \(t_k = ((\theta_p+2\pi k)/\log p)^2\). In particular the Ramanujan conjecture \(|\lambda(p)| \le 2\) at \(p\) (with \(\lambda(p) \ne 2\)) holds if and only if the local factor of \(u\) at \(p\) is a generalized gamma convolution transform in the variable \(\sqrt s\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label cor:msramanujan.




Theorem 26.4, page 489 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Gamma\) be a congruence subgroup of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\), let \(\lambda_j = \frac14+r_j^2\), \(j \ge 1\), be the Laplace eigenvalues of the Maass cusp forms on \(\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}\), and let \(\Theta_\Gamma(t) = \sum_{j\ge1}e^{-t\lambda_j}\) be their heat trace. (i) \(e^{t/4}\Theta_\Gamma(t) = \sum_j e^{-tr_j^2}\) is completely monotone on \((0,\infty)\) if and only if \(\lambda_j \ge \frac14\) for every \(j\), that is if and only if Selberg’s eigenvalue conjecture holds for \(\Gamma\); in that case its Bernstein measure is \(\sum_j\delta_{r_j^2}\). (ii) Unconditionally, \(e^{t(\frac14-(7/64)^2)}\Theta_\Gamma(t)\) is completely monotone on \((0,\infty)\). (iii) For \(\Gamma = \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\) the equivalent conditions of (i) hold, and \(\sum_j e^{-tr_j^2} \sim \frac{1}{12t}\) as \(t \to 0\). (iv) The measure \(\sum_j\delta_{r_j^2}\) is not a Thorin measure, since \(\sum_j r_j^{-2} = \infty\). Part (i) is an equivalence and does not prove Selberg’s eigenvalue conjecture, which is open in general; part (ii) rests on the bound \(\lambda_j \ge \frac14-(\frac{7}{64})^2\) of Kim and Sarnak, valid for every congruence subgroup, and part (iii) on the fact that every cuspidal eigenvalue of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\) exceeds \(\frac14\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label thm:mscm.




Theorem 26.5, page 492 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}\) be a compact hyperbolic surface, with primitive closed geodesics \(P\) of length \(\ell(P)\) and norm \(N(P) = e^{\ell(P)}\), Selberg zeta function \(Z(s) = \prod_P\prod_{k\ge0}(1-N(P)^{-(s+k)})\), and \(R(s) = Z(s+1)/Z(s) = \prod_P(1-N(P)^{-s})^{-1}\) for \(\operatorname{Re}s > 1\). Let \(\alpha > 1\). Then for \(\lambda > 0\), \(R(\alpha)/R(\alpha+\sqrt\lambda) = e^{-b\sqrt\lambda}\,\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda H}\) with \(b = (R'/R)(\alpha) = -\sum_P\sum_{k\ge1}\ell(P)N(P)^{-k\alpha}\), where \(H\) is a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin density \(U(z) = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt z}\sum_P\sum_{k\ge1}\ell(P)N(P)^{-k\alpha}\,2\sin^2\bigl(\frac{k\ell(P)\sqrt z}{2}\bigr) \ge 0\), equal to \((\operatorname{Re}(R'/R)(\alpha+i\sqrt z)-b)/(2\pi\sqrt z)\). The same holds for the modular surface \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}\), and for the Dedekind zeta function of any number field and the Rankin Selberg L function \(L(s,\pi\times\tilde\pi)\) of an automorphic representation \(\pi\) and its contragredient \(\tilde\pi\), whose logarithmic coefficients are nonnegative, with the primes of the field or the Rankin Selberg coefficients in place of the geodesics.
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label thm:msthorin.




Theorem 26.6, page 494 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let the geodesic integers \(\mathfrak n\) be the elements of the free abelian monoid generated by the primitive closed geodesics \(P\) of a compact hyperbolic surface or of the modular surface, with the multiplicative norm \(N(\mathfrak n)\) extending \(N(P) = e^{\ell(P)}\), \(\ell(P)\) the length, and let \(R(\sigma) = \sum_{\mathfrak n}N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma} = Z(\sigma+1)/Z(\sigma)\) for \(\sigma > 1\), \(Z\) the Selberg zeta function. Let \(\mathfrak n_\sigma\) be the random geodesic integer with \(\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak n_\sigma = \mathfrak n) = N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma}/R(\sigma)\). Its exponents \(e_P\) are independent geometric variables with \(\mathbb{P}(e_P \ge k) = N(P)^{-k\sigma}\), and as \(\sigma \downarrow 1\) the point process of the rescaled sizes \((\sigma-1)e_P\ell(P)\) converges to the Poisson process with intensity \(x^{-1}e^{-x}\,dx\), the Gamma process; the ranked normalised sizes \(e_P\ell(P)/\log N(\mathfrak n_\sigma)\) converge in law to the Poisson Dirichlet law \(\mathrm{PD}(1)\); the normalised size of the largest primitive geodesic factor has Dickman’s law in the limit; and the number of distinct primitive factors is asymptotically normal with mean and variance \(\log\frac{1}{\sigma-1}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label thm:mspd.




Open Problem 26.1, page 499 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(R(s) = Z(s+1)/Z(s)\) for a compact hyperbolic surface with Selberg zeta function \(Z\), and \(R^*(s) = (s-1)R(s)\). Determine for which \(a \in (0,\frac12)\) the function \(\lambda \mapsto R^*(\frac12+a)/R^*(\frac12+a+\sqrt\lambda)\) is, after removal of a drift factor \(e^{|b|\sqrt\lambda}\) for a suitable real constant \(b\), the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution, and compute its Thorin density numerically for the Bolza surface or for a Hurwitz surface of small genus, where the spectrum and the geodesics are both available. The question is whether the logarithmic divergences coming from the Laplace spectrum, whose spectral parameters \(r_j\) (eigenvalues \(\frac14+r_j^2\)) satisfy \(\sum_j r_j^{-2} = \infty\), cancel into a positive density.
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label op:mscentre.




Open Problem 26.2, page 499 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Order the primitive closed geodesics \(P\) of the modular surface \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}\) by norm \(N(P) = e^{\ell(P)}\), \(\ell(P)\) the length (they correspond to the narrow classes of primitive binary quadratic forms of positive nonsquare discriminant \(d\)), and colour each by the residue of its discriminant \(d\) modulo \(q\), or by whether \(d\) is fundamental. Determine the densities of the colours, prove the Dirichlet process limit as \(\sigma \downarrow 1\), with that base measure, of the labelled factorisation of the random geodesic integer \(\mathfrak n_\sigma\), where the geodesic integers \(\mathfrak n\) are the finite products of primitive geodesics with the multiplicative norm \(N(\mathfrak n)\), \(R(\sigma) = \sum_{\mathfrak n}N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma}\) for \(\sigma > 1\), and \(\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak n_\sigma = \mathfrak n) = N(\mathfrak n)^{-\sigma}/R(\sigma)\), and identify the analogue of the values \(L(1,\chi)\) in the Mertens constants.
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label op:mschebotarev.




Open Problem 26.3, page 499 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\rho\) be an even icosahedral two dimensional Artin representation of conductor \(N\) (even meaning \(\det\rho(c) = 1\) for complex conjugation \(c\)) with \(\rho(c) = I\) and trivial determinant, so that \(\rho\) is self dual, the case in which its heat trace is computed with the gamma factor of a Maass form. Compute from its Frobenius traces the Galois heat trace \(\mathcal{W}^+_\rho(x)\), \(x > 0\), the explicit formula expression built from \(N\), the gamma factor \(\Gamma_\mathbb{R}(s)^2\) of a Maass form of eigenvalue \(\frac14\) (\(\Gamma_\mathbb{R}(s) = \pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\)) and the traces \(\operatorname{tr}\rho(\mathrm{Frob}_p)\), which equals half the sum of \(e^{-x\gamma^2}\) over the zeros \(\frac12+i\gamma\) of the completed L function \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) when \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) is entire, and which is completely monotone if and only if \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) is entire and all its zeros lie on \(\operatorname{Re}s = \frac12\); test its complete monotonicity numerically; and search by Hejhal’s algorithm for a Maass form of eigenvalue \(\frac14\) on \(\Gamma_0(N)\) whose Hecke eigenvalues are \(\operatorname{tr}\rho(\mathrm{Frob}_p)\). A single such form would be the first even icosahedral instance of reciprocity; the computation is within reach for the smallest conductors.
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label op:mseven.




Open Problem 26.4, page 499 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(X(N) = \Gamma(N)\backslash\mathbb{H}\) be the principal congruence cover of level \(N\) of the modular surface, whose area grows like \(N^3\) while its first nonzero Laplace eigenvalue \(\lambda_1\) stays bounded below by \(\frac{975}{4096} = \frac14-(\frac{7}{64})^2\), the bound of Kim and Sarnak. Determine whether Brownian motion on \(X(N)\) started at a fixed point exhibits cutoff in total variation at a time of order \(\log N\), as random walks on expander graphs do, and how the cusps, whose number grows with \(N\), affect the profile.
Source: book/chapters/ch_maass.tex, label op:mscutoff.







Theorem 27.5, page 507 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E\) be the elliptic curve \(y^2 = x^3+1\), of conductor \(N = 36\), with \(L(E,s) = \sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}\) (continued analytically to all \(s\in\mathbb{C}\)), where \(\eta(6\tau)^4 = \sum_{n\ge1}a_ne^{2\pi in\tau}\) is the newform of weight \(2\) and level \(36\) attached to \(E\) and \(\eta(\tau) = e^{\pi i\tau/12}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{2\pi in\tau})\) is the Dedekind eta function, and with completed function \(\Lambda(E,s) = (\sqrt N/(2\pi))^s\,\Gamma(s)\,L(E,s) = (3/\pi)^s\,\Gamma(s)\,L(E,s)\). For a rectangle of aspect ratio \(r\) (width over height) let \(\pi_h(r) = \frac{\Gamma(2/3)}{\Gamma(1/3)^2}\int_0^{\lambda(ir)}t^{-2/3}(1-t)^{-2/3}\,dt\) be Cardy’s formula for the probability of an open left to right crossing in critical percolation in the scaling limit (a theorem of Smirnov for site percolation on the triangular lattice, and a universality hypothesis for other models), where \(\lambda(\tau) = \theta_2(q)^4/\theta_3(q)^4\) with \(q = e^{i\pi\tau}\), \(\theta_2(q) = \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}q^{(n+1/2)^2}\) and \(\theta_3(q) = \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}q^{n^2}\). Let \(T = \sup\{r > 0 : [0,r]\times[0,1]\text{ has a horizontal open crossing}\}\) be the crossing threshold, the random variable with \(\mathbb{P}(T > r) = \pi_h(r)\), which by Kleban and Zagier’s formula \(d\pi_h/dr = -\kappa\,\eta(ir)^4\) has density \(f_T(t) = \kappa\,\eta(it)^4\) on \((0,\infty)\), with \(\kappa = 2^{4/3}\pi\,\Gamma(\tfrac23)/\Gamma(\tfrac13)^2 \approx 1.4936684\). Then: (1) \(\mathbb{E}[T^{s-1}] = \kappa\,\Lambda(E,s)\) for all \(s\in\mathbb{C}\), the integral converging absolutely; (2) \(\kappa = 1/\Lambda(E,1)\), equivalently \(L(E,1) = \frac{\Gamma(1/3)^2}{3\cdot2^{4/3}\,\Gamma(2/3)} \approx 0.7010911\); (3) \(T \overset{d}{=} 1/T\), and this is equivalent to the functional equation \(\Lambda(E,s) = \Lambda(E,2-s)\) with root number \(+1\); (4) the characteristic function of \(\log T\) is \(\Xi_E(t) = \Lambda(E,1+it)/\Lambda(E,1)\), so the Riemann hypothesis for \(E\) is the statement that the characteristic function of the log crossing threshold has only real zeros.
Source: book/chapters/ch_percolation.tex, label perc:thm:main.




Corollary 27.6, page 508 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(E, s), where E is the elliptic curve y^2 = x^3 + 1.
Statement. Let \(E\) be the elliptic curve \(y^2 = x^3+1\) of conductor \(36\), with completed L function \(\Lambda(E,s) = (3/\pi)^s\,\Gamma(s)\,L(E,s)\), where \(L(E,s)\) is the Hasse Weil L function of \(E\), and let \(T\) be the crossing threshold of critical percolation in the scaling limit (the aspect ratio at which the rectangle \([0,r]\times[0,1]\) stops having an open left to right crossing as \(r\) grows, so that \(\mathbb{P}(T > r)\) is Cardy’s crossing probability, a theorem of Smirnov for site percolation on the triangular lattice and a universality hypothesis for other models), the random variable on \((0,\infty)\) with density \(\kappa\,\eta(it)^4\), where \(\eta(\tau) = e^{\pi i\tau/12}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{2\pi in\tau})\) is the Dedekind eta function and \(\kappa = 2^{4/3}\pi\,\Gamma(\tfrac23)/\Gamma(\tfrac13)^2\), so that \(\mathbb{E}[T^{s-1}] = \Lambda(E,s)/\Lambda(E,1)\) for all complex \(s\). Let \(\Xi_E(t) = \Lambda(E,1+it)/\Lambda(E,1)\), an even entire function of order one with \(\Xi_E(0) = 1\) and Hadamard product \(\Xi_E(t) = \prod_k(1-t^2/\rho_k^2)\) over its zeros \(\rho_k\) with positive real part, listed with multiplicity. Assume the Riemann hypothesis for \(E\), so that \(\rho_k = \gamma_k > 0\). Theorem 27.8, page 510 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.

Proposition 27.11, page 512 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(T\) be the crossing threshold of critical percolation in the scaling limit (the aspect ratio at which the rectangle \([0,r]\times[0,1]\) stops having an open left to right crossing as \(r\) grows, so that \(\mathbb{P}(T > r)\) is Cardy’s crossing probability, a theorem of Smirnov for site percolation on the triangular lattice and a universality hypothesis for other models), the random variable on \((0,\infty)\) with density \(\kappa\,\eta(it)^4\), where \(\eta(\tau) = e^{\pi i\tau/12}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{2\pi in\tau})\) is the Dedekind eta function and \(\kappa = 2^{4/3}\pi\,\Gamma(\tfrac23)/\Gamma(\tfrac13)^2\). Its Laplace transform \(\varphi(s) = \mathbb{E}\,e^{-sT}\) extends to a meromorphic function on \(\mathbb{C}\) with simple poles at \(s = -\pi n/3\) for each \(n\) with \(a_n\ne0\), where \(\eta(6\tau)^4 = \sum_{n\ge1}a_ne^{2\pi in\tau}\) is the newform of the elliptic curve \(y^2 = x^3+1\). Define \(m\) by \(-\varphi'(s)/\varphi(s) = \int_0^\infty e^{-sx}m(x)\,dx\), formally \(m(x) = \sum_{a_n\ne0}e^{-\pi nx/3}-\sum_{\varphi(z)=0}e^{zx}\); \(T\) is infinitely divisible exactly when \(m\ge0\), its Lévy measure then being \(m(x)\,dx/x\), and self decomposable exactly when \(m\) is in addition nonincreasing. Numerically (Laplace inversion by de Hoog’s method at 40 digits), on a grid of 39 points in \([0.02,5.9]\), \(m(x)\) is positive (minimum \(0.0021\)) and strictly decreasing, and \(m(x)e^{\pi x/3}\to1\) (to \(10^{-8}\) by \(x = 3\)), reflecting the leading pole at \(n = 1\). To working precision, therefore, \(T\) is infinitely divisible and self decomposable. It is not a generalized gamma convolution because \(m\) is not completely monotone: the zeros of \(\varphi\) enter with negative weight. The positivity and monotonicity of \(m\) are numerical observations on a finite grid, not a proof; the chapter poses a proof as an open computational problem.

Proposition 27.12, page 513 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E\) be the elliptic curve \(y^2 = x^3+1\) of conductor \(36\), with completed L function \(\Lambda(E,s) = (3/\pi)^s\,\Gamma(s)\,L(E,s)\), where \(L(E,s)\) is the Hasse Weil L function of \(E\), and let \(T\) be the crossing threshold of critical percolation in the scaling limit (the aspect ratio at which the rectangle \([0,r]\times[0,1]\) stops having an open left to right crossing as \(r\) grows, so that \(\mathbb{P}(T > r)\) is Cardy’s crossing probability, a theorem of Smirnov for site percolation on the triangular lattice and a universality hypothesis for other models), the random variable on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\mathbb{E}[T^{s-1}] = \Lambda(E,s)/\Lambda(E,1)\) for all complex \(s\) (its density is proportional to \(\eta(it)^4\), \(\eta\) the Dedekind eta function). Let \(X = \log T\), with cumulant generating function \(K_X(y) = \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{yX} = \log\bigl(\Lambda(E,1+y)/\Lambda(E,1)\bigr)\) and characteristic function \(\Xi_E(t) = \Lambda(E,1+it)/\Lambda(E,1) = \prod_\rho(1-t^2/\rho^2)\), the product over the zeros \(\rho\) of \(\Xi_E\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho > 0\), listed with multiplicity. Let \(Z_m = \sum_\rho\rho^{-2m}\), the sum over the zeros of \(\Xi_E\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho > 0\); there are none on the imaginary axis, since \(\Xi_E(iy) = \mathbb{E}\,e^{-yX} > 0\). Then, unconditionally, the odd cumulants of \(X\) vanish and [_{2m}(X) = (-1)^{m+1},,Z_m,m,] where \(\kappa_j\) denotes the cumulant of order \(j\). The candidate reciprocal law \(W\), with characteristic function \(\varphi_W(y) = e^{-K_X(y)} = 1/\mathbb{E}[T^y]\) (a probability law under the Riemann hypothesis for \(E\)), has cumulants (defined by \(\log\varphi_W(y) = \sum_j\kappa_j(W)(iy)^j/j!\), which makes sense whether or not \(W\) exists) \(\kappa_{2m}(W) = (-1)^{m+1}\kappa_{2m}(X)\); in particular \(\mathrm{Var}(W) = \mathrm{Var}(\log T) = 2Z_1\). Under the Riemann hypothesis for \(E\), when the zeros are \(\rho = \gamma_k > 0\) with \(\gamma_1\) the smallest, \(Z_m = \sum_k\gamma_k^{-2m} > 0\) for every \(m\) and \(Z_m^{-1/(2m)}\) increases to \(\gamma_1\).

Theorem 27.13, page 516 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E\) be the elliptic curve \(y^2 = x^3+1\) of conductor \(36\), with completed L function \(\Lambda(E,s) = (3/\pi)^s\,\Gamma(s)\,L(E,s)\), where \(L(E,s)\) is the Hasse Weil L function of \(E\), and let \(T\) be the crossing threshold of critical percolation in the scaling limit (the aspect ratio at which the rectangle \([0,r]\times[0,1]\) stops having an open left to right crossing as \(r\) grows, so that \(\mathbb{P}(T > r)\) is Cardy’s crossing probability, a theorem of Smirnov for site percolation on the triangular lattice and a universality hypothesis for other models), the random variable on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\mathbb{E}[T^{s-1}] = \Lambda(E,s)/\Lambda(E,1)\) for all complex \(s\) (its density is proportional to \(\eta(it)^4\), \(\eta\) the Dedekind eta function). Let \(X = \log T\) and \(K_X(y) = \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{yX} = \log\bigl(\Lambda(E,1+y)/\Lambda(E,1)\bigr)\); let \(\rho\) run over the zeros, listed with multiplicity, of \(\Xi_E(t) = \Lambda(E,1+it)/\Lambda(E,1)\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho > 0\), so that \(K_X(y) = \sum_\rho\log(1+y^2/\rho^2)\); let \(Z_m = \sum_\rho\rho^{-2m} = (-1)^{m+1}\frac{m\,\kappa_{2m}(\log T)}{(2m)!}\), where \(\kappa_{2m}\) denotes the cumulant of order \(2m\); and let [G(u) = =  = {m}(-u)^{m-1}Z_m.] The \(2\sin^2\) lemma (for a symmetric law \(W\) with Lévy density \(k(|x|)/|x|\), where \(k(x) = \int_0^\infty e^{-xt}\,U(dt)\), one has \(-\log\mathbb{E}\,e^{iyW} = \int_{\mathbb{R}}2\sin^2(\frac{xy}{2})\frac{k(|x|)}{|x|}\,dx = \int_0^\infty\log(1+\frac{y^2}{t^2})\,U(dt)\)), applied to \(K_X\), identifies the candidate Thorin measure as \(\sum_\rho\delta_\rho\). The following are equivalent. (1) The Riemann hypothesis holds for \(L(E,s)\). (2) \(y\mapsto1/\mathbb{E}[T^y]\) is the characteristic function of a symmetric extended generalized gamma convolution; that is, the Thorin measure produced by the \(2\sin^2\) lemma is positive. (3) \(G\) is a Stieltjes function (a function \(a+\int_{[0,\infty)}\frac{\mu(dt)}{u+t}\) with \(a\ge0\) and \(\mu\) a positive measure). (4) For every \(n\) the Hankel matrix \(H_n = [Z_{i+j+1}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\), built from the even cumulants of \(\log T\), is positive semidefinite.

Theorem 28.4, page 523 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\rho\) be a self dual Galois representation with completed L function \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) satisfying \(\Lambda(s,\rho)=\Lambda(1-s,\rho)\), and let \(\Lambda_\rho(n)\) be the coefficients of \(-L'/L(s,\rho)\). For a gamma factor \(\gamma(s)\) and the conductor \(N_\rho\) of \(\rho\), the Galois heat trace is, for \(x>0\), [(x)={}e{-xt2}(N+2(+it))dt-{n},e{-(n)2/(4x)}.] For \(w\ge0\) let \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho\) and \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) be the heat traces computed with the gamma factors \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s+\frac w2)=\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2)\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2+1)\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2)^2\) respectively (where \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)\)), with the same conductor and the same Frobenius data. (a) Unconditionally, [^{}(x)-^{}_(x)=_w(x):=,e{-xC_w2}=_0,e{-u^2/(4x)},du,] where \(C_w=C+\frac w2\,T\), \(C\) has the hyperbolic secant distribution with density \(\operatorname{sech}(\pi t)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), and \(T\) is an independent standard Cauchy variable. So \(\Delta_w\) is completely monotone, and \(\Delta_w(x)\sim\frac14 f_w(0)\sqrt{\pi/x}\) as \(x\to\infty\), where \(f_w(0)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\operatorname{sech}(\pi s)\,\frac{w/(2\pi)}{(w/2)^2+s^2}\,ds\) is the density of \(C_w\) at \(0\) (for \(w=0\) read as \(f_0(0)=1\); the values for \(w=0,1,3,11\) are \(1\), \(0.4413\), \(0.1953\), \(0.0574\)). Theorem 28.5, page 526 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(F\) be a CM field, let \(E/F\) be an elliptic curve without complex multiplication, and for each prime \(\mathfrak{p}\) of good reduction write \(a_{\mathfrak p}=2\sqrt{N\mathfrak p}\cos\theta_{\mathfrak p}\) with \(\theta_{\mathfrak p}\in[0,\pi]\) (so that the Sato Tate law is \(\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\)). Let \(\mathfrak{n}_\sigma\), for real \(\sigma>1\), be the random integral ideal of \(F\) with \(\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak{n}_\sigma=\mathfrak n)=N\mathfrak n^{-\sigma}/\zeta_F(\sigma)\), with its prime factors labelled by \(\theta_{\mathfrak p}\), and let \(e_{\mathfrak p}\) be the exponent of \(\mathfrak p\) in \(\mathfrak n_\sigma\). As \(\sigma\downarrow1\): (i) the labelled factorisation converges in law to the Gamma process with label law the Sato Tate law, and the normalised factorisation converges to the Dirichlet process with base measure \(\frac2\pi\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\); (ii) for continuous \(Q\ge0\) on \([0,\pi]\) the Frobenius functional \(\Xi_\sigma(Q)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{\mathfrak p}e_{\mathfrak p}\log N\mathfrak p\,Q(\theta_{\mathfrak p})\) converges in law to the generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is the image of the Sato Tate law under \(\theta\mapsto1/Q(\theta)\), and for \(Q=\cos^2\) the Thorin density is \(\frac{2}{\pi t^2}\sqrt{t-1}\) on \((1,\infty)\); (iii) the same holds with the labels \((\theta_{\mathfrak p},\operatorname{Frob}_{\mathfrak p})\in[0,\pi]\times G\) for any finite Galois extension \(L/F\) with group \(G\), with base measure the product of the Sato Tate law and Haar measure on \(G\), the joint equidistribution following from the Weyl criterion with the L functions \(L(s,\operatorname{Sym}^m E\otimes\chi)\), \(\chi\) an irreducible character of \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)\), whose nonvanishing on \(\operatorname{Re}s=1\) follows from the potential automorphy of all symmetric powers (Allen, Calegari, Caraiani, Gee, Helm, Le Hung, Newton, Scholze, Taylor and Thorne) by Brauer induction and the theorem of Jacquet and Shalika.

Corollary 28.6, page 528 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(F\) be a CM field, let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_F)\) of weight zero (cohomological for the trivial coefficient system), and let \(\mathfrak p\) be a prime of \(F\) at which \(\pi\) is unramified with trivial central character, with Hecke eigenvalue \(\lambda(\mathfrak p)=\alpha_{\mathfrak p}+\alpha_{\mathfrak p}^{-1}=2\cos\theta_{\mathfrak p}\), \(\theta_{\mathfrak p}\in(0,\pi]\), in the unitary normalisation, so that the local L factor is \(L_{\mathfrak p}(s,\pi)=(1-\alpha_{\mathfrak p}N\mathfrak p^{-s})^{-1}(1-\alpha_{\mathfrak p}^{-1}N\mathfrak p^{-s})^{-1}\), and assume \(\lambda(\mathfrak p)\ne2\). Then, unconditionally (the Ramanujan bound \(|\lambda(\mathfrak p)|\le2\) being a theorem over CM fields), the function of \(u>0\) given by \((2-\lambda(\mathfrak p))\,N\mathfrak p^{-\sqrt u}\,L_{\mathfrak p}(\sqrt u,\pi)=(2-\lambda(\mathfrak p))/(2\cosh(\sqrt u\log N\mathfrak p)-\lambda(\mathfrak p))\) is the Laplace transform, in \(u\), of a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure the comb \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{((\theta_{\mathfrak p}+2\pi k)/\log N\mathfrak p)^2}\).

Theorem 28.7, page 528 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(A/\mathbb{Q}\) be an abelian surface with \(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(A)=\mathbb{Z}\) (endomorphisms over \(\mathbb{C}\)), let \(N_A\) be its conductor, let \(L(s,A)\) be its Hasse Weil L function, and let \(\Lambda(s,A)=N_A^{s/2}\,\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^2\,L(s,A)\), with \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)\). Suppose \(\Lambda(s,A)\) is entire (as it is for the modular surfaces, and is expected for all) and \(\Lambda(1,A)\ne0\). Put \(\Xi_A(w)=\Lambda(1+w,A)\), an even function of \(w\) with zeros \(\pm i\gamma_k\) (one \(\gamma_k\) for each pair, with multiplicity), that is zeros \(1\pm i\gamma_k\) in \(s\). Then the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,A)\) holds if and only if \(\Xi_A(0)/\Xi_A(\sqrt\lambda)\) is the Laplace transform, in \(\lambda\), of a generalized gamma convolution; in that case the Thorin measure is \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\) and the generalized gamma convolution is \(\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables. Moreover, with no assumption on the location of the zeros (but still assuming \(\Lambda(s,A)\) entire and \(\Lambda(1,A)\ne0\)), for every \(a\ge\frac12\) the function \(\Xi_A(a)/\Xi_A(a+\sqrt\lambda)\) is the Laplace transform, in \(\lambda\), of a generalized gamma convolution of drift zero and Thorin density \(V_a(z)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\Xi_A'/\Xi_A\bigr)(a+i\sqrt z)/(2\pi\sqrt z)\), \(z>0\) (the shifted Thorin representation at the basepoint \(1+a\)).

Open Problem 28.1, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\rho\) be a self dual Galois representation with distinct Hodge Tate weights \((0,w)\), \(w>0\), and let \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho\) and \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) be its Galois heat traces computed with the gamma factors \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s+\frac w2)\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2)^2\) respectively, so that \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho-\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho=\Delta_w\) is completely monotone. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis (with \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) entire and root number \(+1\)), \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) fails to be completely monotone for odd \(\rho\). Find an unconditional proof that at most one of \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho\) and \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) is completely monotone; the question is whether a completely monotone function can differ from another by \(\Delta_w\) when both are heat traces of the same Frobenius data.

Open Problem 28.2, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(F\) be a CM field and \(E/F\) an elliptic curve without complex multiplication, with Galois representation \(\rho\). The Rankin Selberg subordinator over \(F\) (the Frobenius labelled subordinator attached to the Rankin Selberg L function of \(\rho|_F\) with its contragredient, as in the book’s chapter on reciprocity through the swap) has Gamma shape \(1\), since \(L(s,\rho|_F\otimes\check\rho|_F)=\zeta_F(s)L(s,\operatorname{ad}^0\rho|_F)\) and the second factor is holomorphic and nonzero at \(s=1\) (by the potential automorphy theorem of Allen, Calegari, Caraiani, Gee, Helm, Le Hung, Newton, Scholze, Taylor and Thorne, Brauer induction and the theorem of Jacquet and Shalika). Determine the Euler Kronecker drift (the coefficient \(\kappa_C\) of \(\lambda(\sigma-1)\) in the expansion of the logarithm of the Laplace transform, at \(\lambda\), of the Frobenius labelled functional as \(\sigma\downarrow1\), as in the book’s Euler Kronecker drift theorem over the rationals) over \(F\) in terms of the Euler Kronecker constant of \(F\) and \(L'/L(1,\operatorname{Sym}^2E/F)\), and its dependence on the degree of \(F\); and decide whether the deficits of the Sato Tate classes can change sign with the field.

Open Problem 28.3, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. State the Sato Tate conjecture for a generic abelian surface over \(\mathbb{Q}\) (with geometric endomorphism ring \(\mathbb{Z}\)) in the form of the theorem on the Dirichlet process over a CM field, with base measure the law of the trace of a Haar distributed element of \(\mathrm{USp}(4)\), and determine which Frobenius functionals have Gamma limits that are provable from the potential modularity of abelian surfaces over totally real fields (Boxer, Calegari, Gee and Pilloni) alone, that is from the Rankin Selberg L function and the standard L function of \(\mathrm{GSp}_4\) without symmetric powers.

Open Problem 28.4, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. The Bergeron and Venkatesh conjecture is that \(\log|H_1(\Gamma_N,\mathbb{Z})_{\mathrm{tors}}|/\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma_N\backslash\mathbb{H}^3)\to\frac{1}{6\pi}\) for \(\Gamma_N\) running through principal congruence subgroups of an arithmetic lattice in \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})\), and the entropy theorem for Jacobians of modular curves in the book (after Tsfasman and Vldu) says that for a fixed prime \(\ell\) and \(N\to\infty\) through primes, \(\frac1g\log|J_0(N)(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|\to\log\frac{\ell^\ell}{(\ell^2-1)^{(\ell-1)/2}}\), the spanning tree entropy of the \((\ell+1)\) regular tree, with \(g\) the genus of \(X_0(N)\). Identify the constant \(\frac{1}{6\pi}\) as an entropy of a random walk or Brownian motion on hyperbolic three space in the sense in which \(\log\frac{\ell^\ell}{(\ell^2-1)^{(\ell-1)/2}}\) is the spanning tree entropy of the \((\ell+1)\) regular tree, and find the common statement of which the two are the \(p\) adic and the archimedean cases: a Jacquet Langlands invariant growth rate of torsion, computed from return probabilities on the universal cover.

Proposition 29.1, page 535 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E_1,E_2,\ldots\) be independent standard exponential variables, let \(M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)\), and let \(P(y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})\) for \(y>0\), so that the Dedekind eta function \(\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), satisfies \(\eta(iy)=e^{-\pi y/12}P(y)\). The variable \(M\) is almost surely finite and positive, and \(\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=P(y)\) for \(y>0\). The function \(P\) is continuous and strictly increasing, and \(1-P(y)\sim e^{-2\pi y}\) as \(y\to\infty\), while \(P(y)\sim y^{-1/2}e^{-\pi/(12y)}\) as \(y\to0\). The density of \(M\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{24}\bigl(1-E_2(iy)\bigr)P(y)\), where \(E_2(\tau)=1-24\sum_{N\ge1}\sigma(N)q^N\), with \(\sigma(N)\) the sum of the divisors of \(N\), is the quasimodular Eisenstein series of weight two.
