title: 21 October: from the odds to a bet
text:
Wednesday 21 October, 7:20 to 10:00. The night is one path. Hong Kong win odds become a probability, a model corrects that probability, a cutoff turns it into a bet, and the Kelly fraction sizes the stake. The book is Chapter 13, Horse Race Betting, and Chapter 4 for the Kelly fraction.
Two labs, then a notebook.
The lab’s \(\alpha\) is the weight on the public log-odds. The cutoff in this note is \(t\). The book uses \(\alpha\) for that cutoff. They are different objects.

title: 21 October: from the odds to a bet
text:
The odds are a forecast
A quoted win dividend \(O\) is the amount a $1 winning ticket returns, stake included. Two conversions:
\[
\frac{1}{O+1} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \frac{1}{O}.
\]
The lab normalizes either one inside the race so the field sums to 1. The take on the panel is \(1 - 1/\sum(1/O)\). Hong Kong keeps about 17.5% of the pool. Read the panel and see which conversion that sentence belongs to.
Favorites win about 4 to 5 percentage points more often than the public odds imply, at both Happy Valley and Sha Tin. A point on the 45° line would mean the crowd is calibrated.
In the lab, section 1. Before touching the control, write the implied probability of a horse quoted at 3.5 under both formulas. Then switch the conversion, and compare the favorite’s bias, the fitted \(\alpha\), and the overround.

title: 21 October: from the odds to a bet
text:
One number corrects the crowd
The public-only model rescales the log-odds inside the race and renormalizes:
\[
c_i = \frac{\exp(\alpha \,\mathrm{logit}\, p_i)}{\sum_{k \in \mathrm{race}} \exp(\alpha \,\mathrm{logit}\, p_k)}.
\]
\(\alpha>1\) stretches the gaps and moves probability from longshots toward favorites. The value of \(\alpha\) is the one that minimizes the negative log-likelihood of the horses that won. The case study reports \(\alpha=1.06\). Read the maximum likelihood estimate off the panel, and the gain in log-likelihood per race. The horizontal line at 1.92 is the edge of a 95% likelihood interval. Compare it with \(\hat\alpha \pm 1.96\,\mathrm{SE}\).

title: 21 October: from the odds to a bet
text:
The field is one softmax
A race with \(K\) horses is one winner, not \(K\) separate yes-or-no questions. The full model adds four factors to the public log-odds. Each is known before the race: the jockey’s past win rate, the trainer’s past win rate, the starting gate relative to the field, and the horse’s rating relative to the field, per 10 points.
\[
\eta_i = \alpha\,\mathrm{logit}(p_i) + \beta_J \,\mathrm{jockey}_i + \beta_T \,\mathrm{trainer}_i + \beta_D \,\mathrm{draw}_i + \beta_R \,\mathrm{rating}_i/10,
\]
\[
c_i = \frac{e^{\eta_i}}{\sum_{k \in \mathrm{race}} e^{\eta_k}}.
\]
The loss is \(-\log c\) for the horse that won. Two horses, and no extra factors, bring this back to the sigmoid. In the notebook, pass one field of four through this formula before you look at the lab’s example race.
In section 3 of the lab, which coefficients have \(|z|>2\)? Say, in one sentence, what a negative jockey coefficient means once the public log-odds are already in the model. Switch the evaluation to later races and see whether the full model still beats the public-only model.

title: 21 October: from the odds to a bet
section: The cutoff comes from the two costs
text:
The cutoff comes from the two costs
Bet $1 on the favorite when the model’s probability clears a cutoff \(t\). At decimal odds 2.5 the book pays \(+1.5\) if the horse wins and \(-1\) if it loses. Not betting pays 0 either way.
A false positive costs the stake, \(c_{FP}=1\). A false negative is the profit you do not take, \(c_{FN}=1.5\). Betting has positive expected payoff when
\[
t = \frac{c_{FP}}{c_{FP}+c_{FN}} = \frac{1}{2.5}.
\]
Equal costs put the cutoff at \(1/2\). A missed event that costs five times a false alarm, the week-7 case, puts it at \(1/6\). The model supplies \(p\). The costs supply \(t\).
In the notebook, compute the expected payoff of a $1 bet at \(p=0.30\), \(0.40\), and \(0.50\), then replace \(1.5\) with \(5\) and recompute \(t\).

title: 21 October: from the odds to a bet
section: The ROC curve is every cutoff
text:
The ROC curve is every cutoff
One cutoff is one point. Sensitivity is the share of winners you bet. Specificity is the share of losers you refuse, so the horizontal coordinate is the share of losers you bet. Lowering \(t\) moves up and to the right: more winners kept, more losing bets taken. The diagonal is a score with nothing in it. The costs choose the point. The curve says whether any point is worth having.
Chapter 13 writes the expected profit per race of the rule “bet $1 on the favorite when \(p>t\)” as
\[
\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{profit}\mid t) = P(\mathrm{win})\cdot \mathrm{sensitivity}(t)\cdot 1.5 - P(\mathrm{lose})\cdot \bigl(1-\mathrm{specificity}(t)\bigr)\cdot 1.
\]
Open the logistic regression lab. At a cutoff of \(0.5\) the NBA model predicts that every favorite wins, so specificity is \(0\%\). Write down why, from \(p=\sigma(0.156\times \mathrm{spread})\), before you move the slider. Then set the cutoff to \(0.75\) and read the new sensitivity and specificity off the matrix and off the curve.
Section 5 of the notebook draws the same curve for the Hong Kong favorites, the Horse Race Betting example in Chapter 13. The model is win on public_prob. The marked cutoffs are \(t=0.3\) and \(t=0.5\).
Section 6 is the 2013 majors. The file is loaded and the one match with no break-point count is dropped. The fit, the confusion matrix, the decision boundary, and the upset rates are yours.
Section 7 is the kernel trick from the same chapter. A circle is drawn, mapped by \(\phi(x_1,x_2)=(x_1^2,\sqrt{2}x_1 x_2,x_2^2)\), and fit twice: once as a line in \(x\), once as a plane in \(\phi(x)\). The inner product \(\phi(a)^\top\phi(b)\) equals \((a^\top b)^2\), which is the kernel.

title: 21 October: from the odds to a bet
text:
The stake, then the take
An edge is model probability times the dividend, minus one. For a bet that pays \(b\) to \(1\) and wins with probability \(p\), the Kelly fraction of the bankroll is
\[
f^\star = \frac{bp - (1-p)}{b}.
\]
The growth per bet is \(g(f)= p\log(1+bf) + (1-p)\log(1-f)\). Past \(f^\star\), growth falls.
In section 4, load the two case-study bets, \(4/1\) at \(p=1/4\) and \(12/1\) at \(p=1/10\). Compute both edges and both fractions in the notebook before you read them off the panel. Then set the stake to \(2f^\star\) and predict the median growth before you run the paths.
In section 6 the model is refit on the early races and bet on the later ones. Start from the actual odds and lower the take until flat staking breaks even. Compare that take with the \(17.5\%\) the track deducts. The closing sentence is what else would have to go right for a real bettor: the edge has to beat the take, survive the price impact of your own money, and still be there in the races the model did not fit.

title: Results by chapter On Langlands Conjectures
text:
Theorem 28.4, page 523 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\rho\) be a self dual Galois representation with completed L function \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) satisfying \(\Lambda(s,\rho)=\Lambda(1-s,\rho)\), and let \(\Lambda_\rho(n)\) be the coefficients of \(-L'/L(s,\rho)\). For a gamma factor \(\gamma(s)\) and the conductor \(N_\rho\) of \(\rho\), the Galois heat trace is, for \(x>0\), [(x)={}e{-xt2}(N+2(+it))dt-{n},e{-(n)2/(4x)}.] For \(w\ge0\) let \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho\) and \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) be the heat traces computed with the gamma factors \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s+\frac w2)=\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2)\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2+1)\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2)^2\) respectively (where \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)\)), with the same conductor and the same Frobenius data. (a) Unconditionally, [^{}(x)-^{}_(x)=_w(x):=,e{-xC_w2}=_0,e{-u^2/(4x)},du,] where \(C_w=C+\frac w2\,T\), \(C\) has the hyperbolic secant distribution with density \(\operatorname{sech}(\pi t)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), and \(T\) is an independent standard Cauchy variable. So \(\Delta_w\) is completely monotone, and \(\Delta_w(x)\sim\frac14 f_w(0)\sqrt{\pi/x}\) as \(x\to\infty\), where \(f_w(0)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\operatorname{sech}(\pi s)\,\frac{w/(2\pi)}{(w/2)^2+s^2}\,ds\) is the density of \(C_w\) at \(0\) (for \(w=0\) read as \(f_0(0)=1\); the values for \(w=0,1,3,11\) are \(1\), \(0.4413\), \(0.1953\), \(0.0574\)). (b) Suppose \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) is entire with root number \(+1\) and satisfies the generalized Riemann hypothesis, and that \(\rho\) is odd with Hodge Tate weights \((0,w)\), so that its gamma factor is \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s+\frac w2)\). Then \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho(x)=\frac12\sum e^{-x\gamma^2}\), the sum over all zeros \(\frac12+i\gamma\) of \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) with multiplicity (so \(\gamma\) and \(-\gamma\) both occur), is completely monotone, and \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) is not: \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho(x)-\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho(\infty)\sim-\frac14 f_w(0)\sqrt{\pi/x}\) as \(x\to\infty\), which is negative and increasing.
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label thm:calparity.




Theorem 28.5, page 526 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(F\) be a CM field, let \(E/F\) be an elliptic curve without complex multiplication, and for each prime \(\mathfrak{p}\) of good reduction write \(a_{\mathfrak p}=2\sqrt{N\mathfrak p}\cos\theta_{\mathfrak p}\) with \(\theta_{\mathfrak p}\in[0,\pi]\) (so that the Sato Tate law is \(\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\)). Let \(\mathfrak{n}_\sigma\), for real \(\sigma>1\), be the random integral ideal of \(F\) with \(\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak{n}_\sigma=\mathfrak n)=N\mathfrak n^{-\sigma}/\zeta_F(\sigma)\), with its prime factors labelled by \(\theta_{\mathfrak p}\), and let \(e_{\mathfrak p}\) be the exponent of \(\mathfrak p\) in \(\mathfrak n_\sigma\). As \(\sigma\downarrow1\): (i) the labelled factorisation converges in law to the Gamma process with label law the Sato Tate law, and the normalised factorisation converges to the Dirichlet process with base measure \(\frac2\pi\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\); (ii) for continuous \(Q\ge0\) on \([0,\pi]\) the Frobenius functional \(\Xi_\sigma(Q)=(\sigma-1)\sum_{\mathfrak p}e_{\mathfrak p}\log N\mathfrak p\,Q(\theta_{\mathfrak p})\) converges in law to the generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is the image of the Sato Tate law under \(\theta\mapsto1/Q(\theta)\), and for \(Q=\cos^2\) the Thorin density is \(\frac{2}{\pi t^2}\sqrt{t-1}\) on \((1,\infty)\); (iii) the same holds with the labels \((\theta_{\mathfrak p},\operatorname{Frob}_{\mathfrak p})\in[0,\pi]\times G\) for any finite Galois extension \(L/F\) with group \(G\), with base measure the product of the Sato Tate law and Haar measure on \(G\), the joint equidistribution following from the Weyl criterion with the L functions \(L(s,\operatorname{Sym}^m E\otimes\chi)\), \(\chi\) an irreducible character of \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)\), whose nonvanishing on \(\operatorname{Re}s=1\) follows from the potential automorphy of all symmetric powers (Allen, Calegari, Caraiani, Gee, Helm, Le Hung, Newton, Scholze, Taylor and Thorne) by Brauer induction and the theorem of Jacquet and Shalika.
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label thm:calcm.




Corollary 28.6, page 528 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(F\) be a CM field, let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_F)\) of weight zero (cohomological for the trivial coefficient system), and let \(\mathfrak p\) be a prime of \(F\) at which \(\pi\) is unramified with trivial central character, with Hecke eigenvalue \(\lambda(\mathfrak p)=\alpha_{\mathfrak p}+\alpha_{\mathfrak p}^{-1}=2\cos\theta_{\mathfrak p}\), \(\theta_{\mathfrak p}\in(0,\pi]\), in the unitary normalisation, so that the local L factor is \(L_{\mathfrak p}(s,\pi)=(1-\alpha_{\mathfrak p}N\mathfrak p^{-s})^{-1}(1-\alpha_{\mathfrak p}^{-1}N\mathfrak p^{-s})^{-1}\), and assume \(\lambda(\mathfrak p)\ne2\). Then, unconditionally (the Ramanujan bound \(|\lambda(\mathfrak p)|\le2\) being a theorem over CM fields), the function of \(u>0\) given by \((2-\lambda(\mathfrak p))\,N\mathfrak p^{-\sqrt u}\,L_{\mathfrak p}(\sqrt u,\pi)=(2-\lambda(\mathfrak p))/(2\cosh(\sqrt u\log N\mathfrak p)-\lambda(\mathfrak p))\) is the Laplace transform, in \(u\), of a generalized gamma convolution with drift zero and Thorin measure the comb \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\delta_{((\theta_{\mathfrak p}+2\pi k)/\log N\mathfrak p)^2}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label cor:calbianchi.




Theorem 28.7, page 528 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(A/\mathbb{Q}\) be an abelian surface with \(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(A)=\mathbb{Z}\) (endomorphisms over \(\mathbb{C}\)), let \(N_A\) be its conductor, let \(L(s,A)\) be its Hasse Weil L function, and let \(\Lambda(s,A)=N_A^{s/2}\,\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^2\,L(s,A)\), with \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)\). Suppose \(\Lambda(s,A)\) is entire (as it is for the modular surfaces, and is expected for all) and \(\Lambda(1,A)\ne0\). Put \(\Xi_A(w)=\Lambda(1+w,A)\), an even function of \(w\) with zeros \(\pm i\gamma_k\) (one \(\gamma_k\) for each pair, with multiplicity), that is zeros \(1\pm i\gamma_k\) in \(s\). Then the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,A)\) holds if and only if \(\Xi_A(0)/\Xi_A(\sqrt\lambda)\) is the Laplace transform, in \(\lambda\), of a generalized gamma convolution; in that case the Thorin measure is \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\) and the generalized gamma convolution is \(\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables. Moreover, with no assumption on the location of the zeros (but still assuming \(\Lambda(s,A)\) entire and \(\Lambda(1,A)\ne0\)), for every \(a\ge\frac12\) the function \(\Xi_A(a)/\Xi_A(a+\sqrt\lambda)\) is the Laplace transform, in \(\lambda\), of a generalized gamma convolution of drift zero and Thorin density \(V_a(z)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\Xi_A'/\Xi_A\bigr)(a+i\sqrt z)/(2\pi\sqrt z)\), \(z>0\) (the shifted Thorin representation at the basepoint \(1+a\)).
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label thm:calg2.




Open Problem 28.1, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\rho\) be a self dual Galois representation with distinct Hodge Tate weights \((0,w)\), \(w>0\), and let \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho\) and \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) be its Galois heat traces computed with the gamma factors \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s+\frac w2)\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\frac w2)^2\) respectively, so that \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho-\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho=\Delta_w\) is completely monotone. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis (with \(\Lambda(s,\rho)\) entire and root number \(+1\)), \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) fails to be completely monotone for odd \(\rho\). Find an unconditional proof that at most one of \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{hol}}_\rho\) and \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{ev}}_\rho\) is completely monotone; the question is whether a completely monotone function can differ from another by \(\Delta_w\) when both are heat traces of the same Frobenius data.
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label op:calparity.




Open Problem 28.2, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(F\) be a CM field and \(E/F\) an elliptic curve without complex multiplication, with Galois representation \(\rho\). The Rankin Selberg subordinator over \(F\) (the Frobenius labelled subordinator attached to the Rankin Selberg L function of \(\rho|_F\) with its contragredient, as in the book’s chapter on reciprocity through the swap) has Gamma shape \(1\), since \(L(s,\rho|_F\otimes\check\rho|_F)=\zeta_F(s)L(s,\operatorname{ad}^0\rho|_F)\) and the second factor is holomorphic and nonzero at \(s=1\) (by the potential automorphy theorem of Allen, Calegari, Caraiani, Gee, Helm, Le Hung, Newton, Scholze, Taylor and Thorne, Brauer induction and the theorem of Jacquet and Shalika). Determine the Euler Kronecker drift (the coefficient \(\kappa_C\) of \(\lambda(\sigma-1)\) in the expansion of the logarithm of the Laplace transform, at \(\lambda\), of the Frobenius labelled functional as \(\sigma\downarrow1\), as in the book’s Euler Kronecker drift theorem over the rationals) over \(F\) in terms of the Euler Kronecker constant of \(F\) and \(L'/L(1,\operatorname{Sym}^2E/F)\), and its dependence on the degree of \(F\); and decide whether the deficits of the Sato Tate classes can change sign with the field.
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label op:calshape.




Open Problem 28.3, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. State the Sato Tate conjecture for a generic abelian surface over \(\mathbb{Q}\) (with geometric endomorphism ring \(\mathbb{Z}\)) in the form of the theorem on the Dirichlet process over a CM field, with base measure the law of the trace of a Haar distributed element of \(\mathrm{USp}(4)\), and determine which Frobenius functionals have Gamma limits that are provable from the potential modularity of abelian surfaces over totally real fields (Boxer, Calegari, Gee and Pilloni) alone, that is from the Rankin Selberg L function and the standard L function of \(\mathrm{GSp}_4\) without symmetric powers.
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label op:calg2.




Open Problem 28.4, page 533 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. The Bergeron and Venkatesh conjecture is that \(\log|H_1(\Gamma_N,\mathbb{Z})_{\mathrm{tors}}|/\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma_N\backslash\mathbb{H}^3)\to\frac{1}{6\pi}\) for \(\Gamma_N\) running through principal congruence subgroups of an arithmetic lattice in \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})\), and the entropy theorem for Jacobians of modular curves in the book (after Tsfasman and Vldu) says that for a fixed prime \(\ell\) and \(N\to\infty\) through primes, \(\frac1g\log|J_0(N)(\mathbb{F}_\ell)|\to\log\frac{\ell^\ell}{(\ell^2-1)^{(\ell-1)/2}}\), the spanning tree entropy of the \((\ell+1)\) regular tree, with \(g\) the genus of \(X_0(N)\). Identify the constant \(\frac{1}{6\pi}\) as an entropy of a random walk or Brownian motion on hyperbolic three space in the sense in which \(\log\frac{\ell^\ell}{(\ell^2-1)^{(\ell-1)/2}}\) is the spanning tree entropy of the \((\ell+1)\) regular tree, and find the common statement of which the two are the \(p\) adic and the archimedean cases: a Jacquet Langlands invariant growth rate of torsion, computed from return probabilities on the universal cover.
Source: book/chapters/ch_cal.tex, label op:caltorsion.

title: Results by chapter On Langlands Conjectures
text:
Proposition 29.1, page 535 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E_1,E_2,\ldots\) be independent standard exponential variables, let \(M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)\), and let \(P(y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})\) for \(y>0\), so that the Dedekind eta function \(\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), satisfies \(\eta(iy)=e^{-\pi y/12}P(y)\). The variable \(M\) is almost surely finite and positive, and \(\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=P(y)\) for \(y>0\). The function \(P\) is continuous and strictly increasing, and \(1-P(y)\sim e^{-2\pi y}\) as \(y\to\infty\), while \(P(y)\sim y^{-1/2}e^{-\pi/(12y)}\) as \(y\to0\). The density of \(M\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{24}\bigl(1-E_2(iy)\bigr)P(y)\), where \(E_2(\tau)=1-24\sum_{N\ge1}\sigma(N)q^N\), with \(\sigma(N)\) the sum of the divisors of \(N\), is the quasimodular Eisenstein series of weight two.
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label prop:ch11M.




Theorem 29.2, page 537 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E_{j,n}\) (\(1\le j\le24\), \(n\ge1\)) be independent standard exponential variables and \(M^*=\max_{j\le24,\,n\ge1}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)\), so that \(\mathbb{P}(M^*\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})^{24}\) for \(y>0\). For complex \(s\) and \(c>0\) let \(Q(s,c)=\Gamma(s,c)/\Gamma(s)=\Gamma(s)^{-1}\int_c^\infty t^{s-1}e^{-t}\,dt\) be the regularised upper incomplete gamma function, which is entire in \(s\) and vanishes at \(s=0,-1,-2,\ldots\). Let \(\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), be Ramanujan’s cusp form of weight \(12\), and \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) its \(L\) function, continued to an entire function. For every complex \(s\), \(L(s,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[Q(s,2\pi M^*)\bigr]\). For real \(s>0\), equivalently, \(L(s,\Delta)=\mathbb{P}(G_s\ge2\pi M^*)\), where \(G_s\) has the gamma law of shape \(s\) and unit rate and is independent of \(M^*\).
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label thm:ch11main.




Corollary 29.3, page 538 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), be Ramanujan’s cusp form of weight \(12\), and \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) its \(L\) function, continued to an entire function. For real \(s>0\), \(0<L(s,\Delta)<1\).
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label cor:ch11bounds.




Corollary 29.4, page 538 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), be Ramanujan’s cusp form of weight \(12\), and \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) its \(L\) function, continued to an entire function. On \(s>0\), \(L(s,\Delta)\) is strictly increasing, and \(L(s,\Delta)\uparrow1\) as \(s\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label cor:ch11monotone.




Proposition 29.5, page 539 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E_{j,n}\) (\(1\le j\le24\), \(n\ge1\)) be independent standard exponential variables, \(M^*=\max_{j\le24,\,n\ge1}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)\), and \(F(y)=\mathbb{P}(M^*\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})^{24}\) for \(y>0\), so that Ramanujan’s cusp form \(\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), satisfies \(\Delta(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}F(y)\). For all \(y>0\), \(F(y)=y^{-12}e^{2\pi(y-1/y)}F(1/y)\). Consequently \(F(y)\sim y^{-12}e^{-2\pi/y}\) as \(y\to0\), and \(1-F(y)\sim24e^{-2\pi y}\) as \(y\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label prop:ch11selfsim.




Proposition 29.6, page 540 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E_{j,n}\) (\(1\le j\le24\), \(n\ge1\)) be independent standard exponential variables and \(M^*=\max_{j\le24,\,n\ge1}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)\), let \(G_6\) have the gamma law of shape \(6\) and unit rate, independent of \(M^*\), and let \(W=\log(G_6/2\pi)\). Let \(\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), be Ramanujan’s cusp form of weight \(12\), let \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)=\int_0^\infty\Delta(iy)y^{s-1}\,dy\) be its completed \(L\) function, and let \(\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\), \(u\in\mathbb{R}\), be its P'olya kernel. Conditionally on \(\{G_6\ge2\pi M^*\}\), \(W\) has density \(\Phi_\Delta\), and for every complex \(z\), \(\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{zW}\bigm|G_6\ge2\pi M^*\bigr]\).
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label prop:ch11posterior.




Theorem 29.7, page 541 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)\), \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), be the Dedekind eta function, and let \(f(\tau)=\prod_m\eta(m\tau)^{r_m}=q\prod_m\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^{mn})^{r_m}=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nq^n\), where the product runs over positive integers \(m\), the \(r_m\ge0\) are integers and \(\sum_mm\,r_m=24\); let \(L(s,f)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}\), which converges absolutely in a right half plane. Let \(E_{m,j,n}\) (\(m\) with \(r_m>0\), \(1\le j\le r_m\), \(n\ge1\)) be independent standard exponential variables and \(M_f=\max_m\max_{j\le r_m}\max_{n\ge1}E_{m,j,n}/(2\pi mn)\), whose distribution function is \(F_f(y)=\mathbb{P}(M_f\le y)=\prod_mP(my)^{r_m}\) with \(P(y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})\), and for \(c>0\) let \(Q(s,c)=\Gamma(s)^{-1}\int_c^\infty t^{s-1}e^{-t}\,dt\) be the regularised upper incomplete gamma function, entire in \(s\) and zero at \(s=0,-1,-2,\ldots\). Then \(f(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}F_f(y)\) for \(y>0\), \(L(s,f)\) continues to an entire function, and for every complex \(s\), \(L(s,f)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[Q(s,2\pi M_f)\bigr]\). For real \(s>0\), \(L(s,f)=\mathbb{P}(G_s\ge2\pi M_f)\), where \(G_s\) has the gamma law of shape \(s\) and unit rate and is independent of \(M_f\); in particular \(0<L(s,f)<1\), and \(L(s,f)\) increases strictly to \(1\) as \(s\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label thm:ch11general.




Proposition 29.9, page 545 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(K=\sup_{t\le1}|b_t|\) for a standard Brownian bridge \(b\), so that \(\mathbb{P}(K\le x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}(-1)^ne^{-2n^2x^2}\) (Kolmogorov’s law). Then \(K^2\) has the law of the maximum of independent exponential variables, one of rate \(2j\) for each even \(j\ge2\) and two of rate \(2j\) for each odd \(j\ge1\). Moreover, let \(M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)\) with \(E_1,E_2,\ldots\) independent standard exponential variables, so that \(\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})\), and let \(M_1,M_2,M_3\) be independent copies of \(M\), with \(K\) independent of \(M_3\). Then \(\max(M_1,M_2)\overset{d}{=}\max\bigl(K^2/\pi,\,M_3/2\bigr)\).
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label prop:ch11kolmogorov.




Open Problem 29.1, page 545 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)\) with \(E_1,E_2,\ldots\) independent standard exponential variables, so that \(\mathbb{P}(M\le y)=\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})\) for \(y>0\), and let \(M^*\) be the maximum of \(24\) independent copies of \(M\). Find a natural Brownian or Bessel functional with the law of \(M\), or of \(M^*\), or show that none exists among first passage and last exit times of one dimensional diffusions.
Source: book/chapters/ch11.tex, label prob:ch11brownian.

title: Results by chapter On Langlands Conjectures
text:
Proposition 30.16, page 564 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(K\) be a compact, connected and simple Lie group with Haar probability measure \(dh\), let \(T\) be a maximal torus with Haar probability measure \(dt\), \(W\) the Weyl group and \(T^+\) a Weyl chamber, and let \(\varphi\ge0\) be a smooth class function on \(K\) with \(\int\varphi\,dh=1\). Observe \(Y_1,\dots,Y_n\) independent with density \(p(y\mid M)=\varphi(M^{-1}y)\) with respect to \(dh\), that is \(Y=M\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\) of density \(\varphi\), where \(M=\eta t\eta^{-1}\) with class parameter \(t\in T^+\) and nuisance parameter \(u=\eta T\in K/T\). Suppose the Fisher information of this model at \(M=e\) is finite and nonsingular. Then: (i) the Fisher metric is \(c\,n\) times a fixed bi invariant Riemannian metric on \(K\), for a constant \(c=c(\varphi)>0\); Jeffreys’ prior for \(M\) is Haar measure, and its image on conjugacy classes has the Weyl density \(|W|^{-1}\prod_{\alpha}|e^{i\alpha(t)}-1|\) (product over all roots \(\alpha\)) with respect to \(dt\), that is, it is the Sato Tate measure of \(K\); (ii) the reference prior of the two group algorithm of Berger and Bernardo, ordered as (class, conjugator), namely \(\pi(u\mid t)\propto|I_{22}(t,u)|^{1/2}\) and \(\pi(t)\propto\exp\bigl\{\int\pi(u\mid t)\log|I_{11\cdot2}(t,u)|^{1/2}\,du\bigr\}\), where \(I=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}I_{11}&I_{12}\\I_{21}&I_{22}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\) is the Fisher information matrix in the coordinates \((t,u)\) and \(I_{11\cdot2}=I_{11}-I_{12}I_{22}^{-1}I_{21}\), is the product of the \(K\) invariant probability measure on \(K/T\) and the uniform (Haar) measure \(dt\) on the Weyl chamber, and its image on classes is the image of Haar measure on \(T\). For \(K=\mathrm{SU}(2)\) the reference prior for the angle \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\) is \(d\theta/\pi\), so \(x=2\cos\theta\) has the arcsine law, against the Sato Tate prior \(\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\); for \(K=\mathrm{USp}(4)\) it is uniform on \(0\le\theta_2\le\theta_1\le\pi\), against the density proportional to \((\cos\theta_1-\cos\theta_2)^2\sin^2\theta_1\sin^2\theta_2\) given by the Weyl integration formula.
Source: book/chapters/ch11b.tex, label thm:11brefprior.

title: Results by chapter On Langlands Conjectures
text:
Theorem 31.1, page 571 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Fix a compact set \(K\subset\mathbb{R}\), a finite set \(D\subset K\), and let \(\nu\) be Lebesgue measure on \(K\) plus counting measure on \(D\). Let the candidate laws \(P_0,P_1\) and the true law \(\mu_0\) be probability measures on \(K\) with \(\nu\) densities \(f_0,f_1,m\), so that their atoms lie in \(D\). Write \(h=\log(f_1/f_0)\), with values in \([-\infty,\infty]\); for a clipping level \(M>0\) write \(h_M=\max(-M,\min(M,h))\); and for a deterministic sequence \((x_k)\) in \(K\) define the clipped log Bayes factor \(\log B_n^M=\sum_{k\le n}h_M(x_k)\). Call \((x_k)\) equidistributed for \(\mu_0\) relative to \(D\) if \(n^{-1}\#\{k\le n:x_k=a\}\to\mu_0(\{a\})\) for each \(a\in D\) and \(n^{-1}\sum_{k\le n,\,x_k\notin D}\delta_{x_k}\) converges weakly to the restriction of \(\mu_0\) to \(K\setminus D\). Suppose that \((x_k)\) is equidistributed for \(\mu_0\) relative to \(D\), that \(h\) is finite on \(D\), that on \(K\setminus D\) the function \(h\) agrees almost everywhere with a continuous map \(\tilde h:K\to[-\infty,\infty]\), through which \(h\) is evaluated off \(D\), and that \(\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)<\infty\), where \(\mathrm{KL}\) denotes the Kullback Leibler divergence. Then for every \(M>0\), \(\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log B_n^M=\int h_M\,d\mu_0\), and as \(M\to\infty\) the right side tends to \(\int h\,d\mu_0=\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)-\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_1)\in[-\infty,\infty)\). In particular, if \(\mu_0=P_0\) the double limit is \(-\mathrm{KL}(P_0\|P_1)\).
Source: book/chapters/ch12.tex, label thm:12consist.




Corollary 31.3, page 573 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E/\mathbb{Q}\) be an elliptic curve and \(0<\varepsilon<\frac12\), and let \(x_p=a_p/\sqrt p\in[-2,2]\) be its normalised Frobenius traces at the primes \(p\) of good reduction, \(p_1<p_2<\cdots\). Compare the models \(M_{\mathrm{ST}}\), under which \(x_p\sim(1-\varepsilon)\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}+\varepsilon\delta_0\), and \(M_{\mathrm{CM}}\), under which \(x_p\sim\frac12\delta_0+\frac12\,\mathrm{arcsine}\), where the Sato Tate law \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}\) has density \((2\pi)^{-1}\sqrt{4-x^2}\) and the arcsine law has density \((\pi\sqrt{4-x^2})^{-1}\) on \([-2,2]\). With densities taken with respect to Lebesgue measure on \([-2,2]\) plus counting measure at \(0\), the log likelihood ratio of \(M_{\mathrm{CM}}\) to \(M_{\mathrm{ST}}\) is \(h(x)=-\log(1-\varepsilon)-\log(4-x^2)\) for \(x\neq0\) and \(h(0)=\log\frac1{2\varepsilon}\); for \(M>0\) let \(h_M=\max(-M,\min(M,h))\) and \(\log B_n^M=\sum_{k\le n}h_M(x_{p_k})\). If \(E\) has no complex multiplication, \(\lim_{M\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log B_n^M=-1-\log(1-\varepsilon)\). If \(E\) has complex multiplication, the limit is \(\frac12\log\frac1{2\varepsilon}-\frac12\log(1-\varepsilon)>0\).
Source: book/chapters/ch12.tex, label thm:12elliptic.

title: Results by chapter On Langlands Conjectures
text:
Open Problem 32.3, page 584 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. (Part (b) of the problem; part (a), the bound \(D_n=O(n^{-1/2+\delta})\) for every \(\delta>0\) for a single curve, is the conjecture of Akiyama and Tanigawa.) For an elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb{Q}\) without complex multiplication let \(p_1<p_2<\cdots\) be its primes of good reduction, \(x_p=a_p(E)/\sqrt p\in[-2,2]\) with \(a_p(E)=p+1-\#E(\mathbb{F}_p)\), \(F_n\) the empirical distribution function of \(x_{p_1},\dots,x_{p_n}\), \(F_{\mathrm{ST}}\) the distribution function of the Sato Tate law \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=(2\pi)^{-1}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx\) on \([-2,2]\), and \(D_n=\sup_x|F_n(x)-F_{\mathrm{ST}}(x)|\). Question: let \(E\) be chosen uniformly among the curves without complex multiplication of conductor at most \(X\), and let \(n=\lfloor X^c\rfloor\) with \(c>0\) fixed. For which \(c\) does \(\sqrt n\,(F_n-F_{\mathrm{ST}})\circ F_{\mathrm{ST}}^{-1}\) converge in law to a Brownian bridge as \(X\to\infty\), and \(\sqrt n\,D_n\) to the Kolmogorov law?
Source: book/chapters/ch13.tex, label op:disc.




Open Problem 32.4, page 585 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Question: is there a criterion, stated through quantitative properties of the twisted sums \(\sum_{p\le x}x_p\chi(p)\log p\) at the square root scale (rates in the law of large numbers, mean squares on the logarithmic scale, large deviation rates), uniform over Dirichlet characters \(\chi\) of growing conductor, that decides whether a sequence \((x_p)\) in \([-2,2]\) indexed by the primes is close to the normalised Hecke eigenvalues \(x_p(f)=a_p(f)/p^{(k-1)/2}\) of a holomorphic newform \(f\) of weight \(k\) with trivial nebentypus, in the sense that \(\sum_{p\le x}(x_p-x_p(f))\chi(p)\log p=o(\sqrt x)\) for every \(\chi\)?
Source: book/chapters/ch13.tex, label op:inverse.




Open Problem 32.8, page 589 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), be Ramanujan’s cusp form of weight \(12\) for \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\), with \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\), and let \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\). Write the zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) as \(6\pm i\gamma_k\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\gamma_k>0\), and let \(k_\Delta(x)=\sum_k e^{-\gamma_k^2x}\) for \(x>0\). Prove by a probabilistic argument that \(k_\Delta\) is completely monotone on \((0,\infty)\).
Source: book/chapters/ch13.tex, label op:thorin.




Open Problem 32.9, page 590 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), be Ramanujan’s cusp form of weight \(12\) for \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\), with \(L\) function \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\). Let \(M^*\) be the maximum of \(24\) independent copies of \(M=\max_{n\ge1}E_n/(2\pi n)\), with \(E_n\) independent standard exponential variables, so that \(L(s,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\,Q(s,2\pi M^*)\) for every complex \(s\), where \(Q(s,c)=\Gamma(s,c)/\Gamma(s)\) is the regularised upper incomplete gamma function. (a) Question: can properties of the law of \(M^*\), such as the self similarity \(F(y)=y^{-12}e^{2\pi(y-1/y)}F(1/y)\) of its distribution function \(F\) given by modularity, be used to locate or count the zeros of \(L(s,\Delta)\)? (b) Question: for which newforms \(f\) is there a random variable \(M_f\), the maximum of countably many independent variables with distribution functions of the form \((1-e^{-cy})^{\kappa}\) with \(c,\kappa>0\), such that \(f(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}\,\mathbb{P}(M_f\le y)\) for all \(y>0\)?
Source: book/chapters/ch13.tex, label op:ev.




Open Problem 32.10, page 591 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For primes \(N\equiv1\bmod12\) let \(K_N\) be the Kemeny constant of simple random walk on the supersingular \(2\) isogeny graph in characteristic \(N\), which is \(3\) regular on \(h=(N-1)/12\) vertices; thus \(K_N=\sum_{j=2}^{h}(1-\lambda_j/3)^{-1}\), where \(\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_h\) are the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix other than the eigenvalue \(3\), and \(K_N/h\to2\) as \(N\to\infty\) through these primes. Question: does the empirical distribution of \(K_N-2h\) over the primes \(N\le Y\) with \(N\equiv1\bmod12\) converge as \(Y\to\infty\), and is \(K_N-2h\) bounded?
Source: book/chapters/ch13.tex, label op:kemeny.




Open Problem 32.11, page 592 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. The book’s consistency theorem for Bayesian identification states the following. Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}\) be compact, \(D\subset K\) finite, and \(\nu\) Lebesgue measure on \(K\) plus counting measure on \(D\); let candidate laws \(P_0\), \(P_1\) and a true law \(\mu_0\) have \(\nu\) densities \(f_0\), \(f_1\), \(m\), let \(h=\log(f_1/f_0)\), with values in \([-\infty,\infty]\), and for a clipping level \(M>0\) let \(h_M=\max(-M,\min(M,h))\) and \(\log B_n^M=\sum_{k\le n}h_M(x_k)\) for a sequence \((x_k)\) in \(K\). Suppose that \((x_k)\) is equidistributed for \(\mu_0\) relative to \(D\), meaning that \(n^{-1}\#\{k\le n:x_k=a\}\to\mu_0(\{a\})\) for each \(a\in D\) and that \(n^{-1}\sum_{k\le n,\,x_k\notin D}\delta_{x_k}\) converges weakly to the restriction of \(\mu_0\) to \(K\setminus D\); that \(h\) is finite on \(D\); that on \(K\setminus D\) it agrees almost everywhere with a continuous map \(K\to[-\infty,\infty]\) through which it is evaluated there; and that the Kullback Leibler divergence \(\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)\) is finite. Then for every \(M\), \(\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log B_n^M=\int h_M\,d\mu_0\), and as \(M\to\infty\) this tends to \(\int h\,d\mu_0=\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_0)-\mathrm{KL}(\mu_0\|P_1)\in[-\infty,\infty)\). Problem: (a) extend this theorem to the \(52\) Sato Tate groups of abelian surfaces, whose laws of the normalised coefficients \((a_1,a_2)\) of the characteristic polynomials of Frobenius can have atoms and components on lower dimensional sets, and to motives of higher rank; (b) make it effective, by bounding the number of primes after which the log Bayes factor favours the true group against every other candidate, polynomially in the logarithm of the conductor and without assuming the Riemann hypothesis.
Source: book/chapters/ch13.tex, label op:bayes.




Open Problem 32.12, page 592 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(E/\mathbb{Q}\) have conductor \(N_E\) and analytic rank \(r_E\), let \(a_p=p+1-\#E(\mathbb{F}_p)\) and \(S_E(x)=\sum_{p\le x,\,p\nmid N_E}a_p\log p/p\), and assume the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,E)\). Then \(S_E(x)-(\tfrac12-r_E)\log x\), with \(\log x\) uniform on \([0,Y]\) and \(Y\to\infty\), converges in law to a distribution \(\mu_E\) with mean \(C_E\); let \(Z_E\) have the law \(\mu_E\) shifted to mean zero. Question: as \(E\) runs through the curves of conductor at most \(X\) and analytic rank \(r\in\{0,1\}\), does the law of \(Z_E/\log N_E\) converge as \(X\to\infty\), and is the limit the one predicted by the low lying zeros of the corresponding orthogonal family?
Source: book/chapters/ch13.tex, label op:rankbias.

title: On Statistical Methods for Genetics Fisher, Ewens and the Bayesian Programme
text:
Description
This book treats the mathematical theory of population genetics as a problem in statistical inference, from Fisher’s Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection to learned inference for the coalescent.
It shows that Fisher’s decomposition of the rate of change of mean fitness holds for arbitrary genotype frequencies, with an exact remainder computed for one and two loci. It shows that the usual plug in estimate of the additive genetic variance is inflated by a term that grows with the number of loci, and that shrinkage under a horseshoe prior gives a conservative correction. It derives the Ewens sampling formula from de Finetti’s theorem, proves that among sampling weights only power weights preserve the residual allocation structure of Poisson Dirichlet subdivisions, and leaves the case of general weights as a stated conjecture. It develops rational conjugacy for Pochhammer priors on concentration parameters, with exact residue formulas for normalizing constants and Zipf tails for the counts they generate. For inference without a likelihood it proves that a learned quantile map that attains the Bayes risk is sufficient, that the number of segregating sites is not sufficient for the mutation rate, and that DeepSets encoders see only the site frequency spectrum.
The book is written for statisticians and mathematical biologists with graduate level probability. Numerical results are labelled as computations where they rest on simulation.

title: On Statistical Methods for Genetics Fisher, Ewens and the Bayesian Programme
On Statistical Methods for Genetics Fisher, Ewens and the Bayesian Programme
text:
Main results

Whole genome Fundamental Theorem decomposition (Theorem 3.5, page 66): For arbitrary genotype frequency paths, the rate of change of mean Malthusian fitness splits exactly into an additive part and a remainder; the remainder vanishes whenever the log frequencies move inside the span of the gene contents, and it vanishes for every assignment of fitnesses only then.
Exact remainder for one locus with k alleles (Theorem 3.16, page 76): In the one locus random mating model with constant fitnesses, the change in mean fitness is the additive term divided by mean fitness plus an explicit quadratic remainder in the dominance deviations.
Oracle shrinkage understates the additive variance (Proposition 4.10, page 140): Shrinkage tuned to estimate each average effect as well as possible necessarily understates the additive variance, by an explicit amount.
Shrinkage weights are stick breaking weights (Theorem 5.15, page 180): The Beta law of the horseshoe type shrinkage weight is exactly the law of the first stick breaking weight of the two parameter GEM family, which links shrinkage priors to Ewens Pitman partitions.
Rigidity of the residual allocation structure (Theorem 7.11, page 271): Among sampling densities that charge every interval, only power weights keep the induced subdivision of the size biased layout a residual allocation model, so for a discount strictly between zero and one no such density other than the uniform one carries a two parameter Poisson Dirichlet law to the stick breaking sequence of another member of the family.
A bottleneck that attains the Bayes risk is sufficient (Theorem 10.12, page 399): If a learned map that factors through a summary of the data attains the minimal check loss, the summary is sufficient, so sufficiency can be tested by comparing risks.
The number of segregating sites is not sufficient for theta, likelihood argument (Proposition 11.12, page 443): The conditional law of the infinite sites data given the site count depends on theta through the latent tree, shown explicitly for three and four sequences.
DeepSets encoders factor through the site frequency spectrum (Theorem 11.16, page 445): Any encoder built from per site permutation invariant features depends on the data only through the site frequency spectrum, which caps what such an encoder can learn.

All 58 results of the book (57 proved, 1 open) are on the page Results by chapter, each with its statement, status and number.
